#### `Pass 145.0` (`0c48bbf`) — THE WHOLE-OPERATOR PIN, AND THE INVARIANT ANSWER

**New:** `FormatRequest::whole_operator(page_index, span)` and a
`FormatRequest::pinned(span)` builder. `whole_operator(page, span)` is
**equivalent to `FormatRequest::new(page, "").pinned(span)`** — both spellings
work and **produce identical bytes, pinned by a test** rather than asserted.
`EditRequest` gets the same affordance (empty `find` + `pinned_span`), because
**the two verbs share one locator** and giving the affordance to only one of
them would have been a new asymmetry.

Implemented as **`effective_find` in `text_edit::edit`, resolved ONCE right
after the anchor is located**, so the code-range match, the font-coverage
gate, the synthesis gate and every disclosure count **read one string**. That
is the structural choice: four consumers of the resolved text, one
resolution.

**AN EMPTY `find` WITH NO PIN IS STILL REFUSED, by the same name it always
was** (acceptance criterion 1, met as written) — a caller that forgot to pin
gets a refusal, not silent whole-operator behaviour. **Both CLI verbs refuse
it with a message naming the FLAG that would fix it**, which core cannot know
about; that split is the reason the refusal exists in two places rather than
one.

**★★ THE SUBTLE HALF, and it is the defect a shallower fix would have
shipped.** `plan_font` used to check encoding coverage against **`req.find`**.
On a whole-operator request that is `""` — and **every face covers the empty
string** — so a family change to a face that **cannot show the run** would have
been **ACCEPTED**. `plan_font` now takes the **resolved** text. Pinned by a
named test. Note the shape: the new affordance did not break coverage
checking, it **hollowed it out silently**, and the only symptom would have
been a run changed to a face that renders nothing.

##### ★★★ THE INVARIANT ANSWER — OWED EITHER WAY, AND NOW MEASURED

`crates/pdfce-core/tests/operator_span_invariant.rs` walks `fixtures/`:

| quantity | value | per-item form (hard rule 10a) |
|---|---:|---|
| files walked | **4,289** | — |
| files with text | **1,623** | 37.8 % of 4,289 |
| runs | **18,559** | 11.4 runs per text-bearing file |
| glyphs | **669,436** | 36.1 glyphs per run |
| `operator_span` groups | **29,246** | **1.58 groups per run**; 22.9 glyphs per group |
| **non-contiguous groups** | **0** | 0 of 29,246 |
| **groups not indexing text cleanly** | **0** | 0 of 29,246 |

⇒ **THE INVARIANT HOLDS.** `pdfceGUI`'s shipped workaround — *"the glyphs
sharing one `operator_span` always slice a contiguous, matchable range out of
the run's text"* — **is sound**, and it is now **a documented guarantee plus a
test that re-runs on every `cargo test`** rather than an undocumented
behaviour they were relying on. **Sabotage-checked**: excluding one glyph per
group from the coverage computation turns the probe **red**, so the zeroes are
zeroes rather than a probe that measures nothing.

**This is the branch the 296th filing said was NOT symmetric**, and the
asymmetry resolved the good way: had it failed, a build their operator is
using would have been resting on luck and they would have needed telling
urgently. It held, so what is owed instead is a **guarantee**, which is
`decision 094` below and the channel reply.

##### ★★ THE MULTI-OPERATOR CLAIM — FILED AS THE REPORTER'S ACCOUNT, EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED — IS CONFIRMED

**2,420 of 18,559 runs (13.0 %) carry glyphs from more than one show
operator.** **Common, not exotic.** Their third table row was right.

Two consequences, and the second is the rule-4 one:

- **It is what makes the whole-operator affordance load-bearing rather than a
  convenience.** On 13 % of runs, a `find` string rebuilt from `TextRun::text`
  names a range across several operators, which `match_run` cannot express —
  the reporter's third failed attempt, now explained rather than relayed.
- **The report carries a `whole operator:` disclosure naming the case**
  (`CLAUDE.md` rule 4). **The EXTENT was pdfce's choice, not the operator's** —
  the caller said *"this pin"*, pdfce decided how far that reaches — so the
  choice is disclosed off-canvas, and printed by the CLI. Acceptance criterion
  2 met.

**One probe, two answers**, exactly as the 296th filing's method note asked.
Built once.

##### THE DOCS HALF

`docs/core-api/01-reading-and-model.md` gains a new **§8.4.0** stating the two
facts a caller building a locator needs, plus the guarantee:

- **`text.chars().count()` is NOT `glyphs.len()`** — `/ToUnicode` maps a code
  to a **STRING** (ISO 32000-1 §9.10.3), so one glyph can carry several
  characters. **Measured 1 of 191 synthetic runs** — **and THAT RATIO IS THE
  TRAP**: near-zero on synthetic text, **routine on real typeset copy**. A
  `find`-based locator therefore looks correct in every synthetic fixture a
  shell writes for itself. *(The 296th filing recorded the same single
  offender against a different denominator — 1 across 256 fixture PDFs. Same
  fact, two denominators; both are stated here because a bare "1" is not a
  measurement.)*
- **A `TextRun` is not a show operator** — the 13 % table above.
- **The invariant, as a guarantee**, with the 29,246 / 0 numbers beside it, so
  the guarantee carries its own evidence rather than pointing at a filing.

`docs/core-api/02-editing-and-saving.md` gains the `FormatRequest` half.
Acceptance criterion 4 (both doc gaps closed in the same change) met.

##### CLI (rule 11), AND IT CLOSES A LOOP THAT COULD NOT PREVIOUSLY BE CLOSED

- **`extract-text --json --spans`** emits **`op_start` / `op_len` / `stream`**
  per glyph. **Without the flag those fields are ABSENT, not zero** —
  provenance capture is off by default and *"not captured"* must not read as
  *"offset 0"*. `stream` is `"page"` or `"form:N"` and **is not optional to
  read**. This is the field whose absence made the 296th filing unable to
  settle the multi-operator claim from outside; it can now be settled from
  outside by anyone.
- **`format-text --pin-span START:LEN`** and **`edit-text --pin-span
  START:LEN`**. **`START:LEN`, not `START:END`**, because that is the shape the
  value has everywhere else it exists — `ByteSpan` carries start+len, and the
  JSON emits `op_start`/`op_len`. Two spellings of one value is how a caller
  gets it wrong once and never notices.

##### ★★ TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY RUNNING THE BINARY, NOT BY THE TESTS — BOTH IN THIS PASS'S OWN NEW CODE

1. **`cmd_edit_text` PARSED `--pin-span` and never attached it.** The refusal
   read *"empty find text"* — **exactly what the feature was supposed to
   remove** — and **every unit test passed**, because they exercise the core
   API directly. A CLI flag that is parsed and dropped is invisible to any
   test that does not go through `main`.
2. **A shipped `pdfce-cli` refusal carried FOURTEEN baked-in spaces**, and
   **`check-string-gaps.sh` reported PASS on it.**

**The generalisable half:** the suite is 4,463 tests and neither defect was in
its reach, because both live in the **shell layer between the flags and the
core API** — the one layer a core-API test cannot exercise by construction.
Driving the release binary is not belt-and-braces here; it is the only
instrument that covers that layer.

##### ★★★ THE GATE THAT UNDER-REPORTED, FIXED AS A CLASS

**This is the THIRD time `check-string-gaps.sh` has missed by admitting only
the spelling somebody had already seen.** Its own header says the previous
repair *"widens both ends of the class rather than only the end that
failed"* — and it widened both ends to `{`/`}` **and stopped**.

**The next miss was `"…with an empty              --find to mean…"` — TWO
holes at once:**

- the literal **was not recognised as prose** (an `eprintln!`, not an
  `#[error(...)]`), so the prose rules never ran on it;
- and **even in prose mode the trailing class did not admit a HYPHEN** — and
  **the next word after a gap in a CLI diagnostic is, more often than
  anything else, a `--flag`.**

**Fixed by the same structural argument that scoped the `{}` widening:** a
literal opening with **the binary's own diagnostic prefix** (`"pdfce-cli: "` /
`"pdfce-gui: "`) is **a sentence an operator reads**, never an aligned report
column. That is a property of the string's *role*, not of the characters that
have failed so far.

**MEASURED BEFORE WIDENING**, which is what makes the scoping a decision
rather than a guess:

| widening | findings | legitimate (aligned columns, DXF byte streams) | true defects |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| blanket trailing-class widening | **24** | ~18 | 1 |
| **scoped to prose** (diagnostic-prefix rule) | **1** | 0 | **1** |

⇒ **The scoped rule found exactly the defect and nothing else.** A gate that
reports 24 findings of which ~18 are legitimate is a gate that will be
switched off (`D:/dev/rag/rust/ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`).
**A self-test fixture for the shape was added**, so the third miss cannot
become a fourth silently.

**★ THE TRANSFERABLE STATEMENT, NOW THREE FOR THREE:** *in prose mode the
trailing class should be read as **"anything that starts a word"**, not as a
list of the characters that have failed so far.* Three repairs, each one
admitting only the spelling that had just been seen, is the same shape as
`R220`'s three-deep escalation — **a repair that generalises to the instance
rather than to the class is a repair that schedules its own successor.**

#### What was wrong

`crates/pdfce-render/src/image.rs`'s `decode_sampled` converts every texel
through `crate::color`, which counts its own shortfalls — a missing or
malformed `/tintTransform`, a `/Separation /All` approximation, an ICC
alternate taken. Those counts went into **two local `ColorDiagnostics`
values (`scratch_diag`, and the `TintCache`'s own `diag`) that were
constructed, written to, and dropped at the end of the function.**

The visible consequence: an image whose `/Separation` carries a broken
transform renders as `separation_to_rgb`'s **neutral stand-in** — a colour
the document never specified, whose own note says *"lightness preserved,
hue is not the document's"* — and **pdfce reported nothing at all.**

**This is a `CLAUDE.md` rule 4 violation, not a missing statistic**, and the
distinction is the entry. Rule 4 forbids **silence** about an inference, and
its own text says the obligation *"bites hardest on inferences the operator
**cannot see by definition**"* — naming a font substitution that renders
plausibly. **A substituted image colour is the same case**: a plausible grey
looks exactly like a grey the file might have asked for. The fix routes the
account off-canvas to the CLI's printed note, which is where rule 4 says it
belongs; nothing about the **rendering** changes.

#### Measured, before → after (engineer's figures, relayed)

On a purpose-built **image-only** page whose `/Separation` carries a
deliberately malformed transform (wrong arity, wrong output count):

| fixture | `tint_applied` before | after | `tint_not_applied` before | after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `image-only-good-tint.pdf` | 0 | **1** | 0 | 0 |
| `image-only-broken-tint.pdf` | 0 | 0 | 0 | **1** |

**Both counters read zero on both fixtures before the fix** — the good page
and the broken page were indistinguishable from a page with no spot content
at all. Per hard rule 10a the denominator is stated: these are **counts per
distinct sample tuple, not per texel**, because `TintCache` exists precisely
so that one broken transform reports **once per distinct colour** rather
than once per texel; on these two fixtures the palette is one entry, so 1
tuple = 1 image. The shortfall half also produces prose on the CLI's note:
*"1 spot-colour conversion(s) had no usable `/tintTransform` … the lightness
is right and the HUE IS NOT the document's"*.

**Why the GOOD fixture is asserted as well as the broken one, and is not
padding.** A fix that routed only **failures** to the caller would satisfy
the shortfall half and leave the **census** half still lying by omission.
Only the good page tells those two apart.

#### ★★★★ TWO CORRECTIONS TO `70c5919`'s COMMIT MESSAGE — AND THEREFORE TO THE 294th FILING, WHICH RELAYED BOTH

`70c5919` is **not amended**; its hash is cited by the 294th filing's
*Shipped* entry, by `SESSION_LOG.md` and by `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and this
project has direct evidence of what rewriting a cited commit costs
(`tools/check-cited-commits-exist.py`, `0d9f4df`, fourteen pre-existing
casualties). The corrections are recorded **here**, and a dated correction
note has been placed in-line at each site in `docs/` that repeated either
claim — **corrected in place with a visible note, never silently
rewritten** (append-only discipline, hard rule 1).

**(a) The cost figure was wrong, and the true statement is STRONGER.**
`70c5919`'s message said *"292 distinct tuples behind 25,870 texels"* on the
patch that opened `Pass 140.0`, attributing `tint_applied = 292` to that
image's `TintCache`. **That counter had no image contribution whatsoever**
— it was the page's **path fills** — because the decode's diagnostics
reached nothing, which is the very defect this Pass fixes. The engineer
wrote a number into a commit message by attributing a counter to a producer
**that could not have reached it.**

Corrected, and better than the figure it replaces: **both images on that
patch are `/Indexed` with 256-entry palettes**, so their tint work is
bounded by the **palette** — **≤ 256 conversions per image, at decode time,
independent of the image's pixel count** — and `TintCache` is not involved
at all. That is a *stronger* cost claim than "one evaluation per 88.6
texels", because it is bounded by a structural constant rather than by a
measured ratio on one page.

**The synthetic worst case stands unchanged**: 16 bpc × 5 colorants (an
**80-bit key** the cache cannot pack), **490,000 texels**, a type 4
PostScript transform, **~670 ms → ~925 ms median = 1.37 µs → 1.89 µs per
texel, about +38 %**, filed as a **range not a point** because run-to-run
spread on this machine is ~15 %. It was measured on a **direct `DeviceN`
image**, which is the genuinely unbounded shape — so the worst case was
never resting on the wrong figure.

**(b) ★★ ROUTE 4 ALONE ACCOUNTS FOR THE ENTIRE FIX ON THE REPORTED PATCH,
AND ROUTE 4 WAS NOT IN THE REPORT.** Ablated on a debug build:

| configuration | `cmyk_bridged_pixels` | `cmyk_native_image_pixels` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `/Indexed`-over-`DeviceN` ink table **reverted**, direct `Separation`/`DeviceN` route left in place | **25,870** | **0** |
| both restored (shipped state) | **0** | **25,870** |

Reading the table: with **only the route the bug report named** in place, the
patch is **fully bridged** — that is, **completely unfixed**. The two
counters are complements, so the same 25,870 pixels are the whole patch in
both rows; there is no partial credit anywhere in it.

⇒ **Had the engineer implemented only the route the bug report named, the
reported defect would not have been fixed at all.** The route that actually
carried the fix — `/Indexed` over a `Separation`/`DeviceN` base, a duotone —
was found **by walking `R219`'s own checklist**, not by the report, not by a
test, and not by the operator.

**This is the strongest datum this project has for `R219`**, and it has been
folded into `R219`'s own entry under *Standing rules* as well as recorded
here. It converts the rule from *"enumerating the siblings is cheap and
saves the next session a bug report"* into *"on this instance, enumerating
the siblings is the only reason the fix worked."* A standing rule whose
value has been demonstrated this concretely should say so **where the rule
is read**, not only where the Pass is filed.

#### ★★★ THE STALE-CLAIM SWEEP — FIVE SITES, AND THE 294th FILING'S SWEEP FOUND FOUR

The 294th filing's hard-rule-11 sweep reported **four survivors** at
`70c5919` and recorded them as owed work. **All four were real and all four
are corrected in `25d73d7`.** There was a **fifth**, found only by grepping
**format strings**: `crates/pdfce-cli/src/main.rs`'s runtime note — the class
the **288th** filing recorded as invisible to every gate and left unresolved.

**Three findings, all new, and none of them is "the sweep should have been
more thorough":**

**(i) A stale claim can be repaired by a CODE CHANGE rather than by an edit,
leaving no trace of ever having been wrong.** From `Pass 130.1` until `Pass
140.0`, a `Separation`/`DeviceN` image outside overprint **did** bridge, and
`interpret.rs`'s *"what is left"* enumeration did not mention it — **false
for ten Passes**. `Pass 140.0` removed that population, which made the
**unchanged** sentence true again. Nobody edited it, nobody noticed it, and
the repaired text carries no marker that it was ever wrong. **A `git blame`
on a true sentence is not evidence the sentence was always true.**

**(ii) Two copies of one population claim disagreed for ten Passes, and the
MORE VISIBLE copy was the accurate one — so recency and location are both
worthless as evidence.** The CLI's runtime note (operator-facing, printed on
every subtractive page) listed that population **correctly** over exactly the
period the rustdoc comment (internal, read by maintainers) had it wrong. Then
`Pass 140.0` made **the accurate one** false. The natural heuristics both
fail here: *"the internal comment is closer to the code, trust it"* is wrong,
and *"the operator-facing string is more exposed, so it gets corrected more
often"* is wrong in the other direction. **When two copies of a population
claim disagree, neither's recency nor its audience is evidence of which is
right — only the code is.**

**(iii) The format-string gap has now cost a SECOND occurrence.** The 288th
filing recorded this class — a claim living in a `println!`/`eprintln!`
template, invisible to every gate this project owns — and said *"a fourth
occurrence would argue harder for promotion"*. **This is the second for the
format-string half specifically**, counted separately and deliberately: the
288th filing's tally was for the broader stale-disclosure class, and
conflating the two would inflate the count.

**★ THE PROMOTION QUESTION, DECIDED: MINTED AS `R222`, AND THE ENGINEER'S
REASONING FOR *NOT* GATING IT IS ACCEPTED IN FULL.** The engineer's view,
relayed verbatim in the dispatch, was that this *"still cannot be gated
mechanically (no script can content-check a claim's truth)"* but that the
**habit** is now clearly worth a standing rule. Both halves are accepted:

- **The gate half is DECLINED, permanently, and should not be re-proposed.**
  A gate would have to know what the current behaviour *is* — which is the
  very fact the disclosure exists to report. This is the identical warrant
  on which three prior requests to gate the disclosure-staleness class were
  declined (librarian hard rule 11's own text), and it is not weakened by a
  second occurrence.
- **The habit half is MINTED as `R222`** — see *Standing rules*. It is a
  **procedural commitment on the engineer's side**, the mirror of librarian
  hard rule 11's commitment on the filing side, and like both of its
  siblings (`R219`, `R220`) it is **checkable after the fact**: a reader asks
  whether the change that corrected a doc comment also grepped the format
  strings. Minted at **n = 2**, the project's standing bar, with the second
  instance found by a sweep that had already run once and reported clean.

**Why a librarian hard rule was not sufficient on its own.** Hard rule 11
already names `eprintln!`/`println!` strings in its scope, and it is what
found survivors 1–4. But hard rule 11 runs **at filing time — one commit
later at best**, and it binds the librarian, not the engineer making the
edit. The gap `R222` closes is the window between *"the engineer corrects a
doc comment"* and *"the librarian sweeps"*, which is exactly where this
survivor lived.

#### ★ A SABOTAGE THAT SURVIVED, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER

Three sabotages of `Pass 140.2`'s two new tests (engineer's, relayed):

| sabotage | result |
|---|---|
| `decode` never merges its diagnostics into `notes` | **2 of 7 fail** |
| the interpreter drops what `decode` handed it | **2 of 7 fail** |
| only the **cache** is merged, not `scratch_diag` | **0 of 7 fail — SURVIVES** |

**The survivor is the entry, and it is a POSITIVE instance: the sabotage
caught a false claim in a CODE COMMENT, not a defect in the code.** The
engineer's first draft of that comment claimed the `scratch_diag` merge kept
*"every non-`Special` image"* from being silent. **That was false, and the
sabotage is what proved it** — deleting the merge changes no test because:

- `tint_cache` is `Some` **exactly when** the space is `Space::Special`, so
  the non-cache arm of the texel loop is reached only by `Gray`, `Rgb`,
  `Cmyk` and `Indexed` — whose conversions are **closed-form arithmetic that
  records nothing at all**. There is no shortfall for a non-`Special` image
  to report.
- `scratch_diag`'s **only** possible contribution is the `yields_cmyk` probe,
  and only for a transform that **LOADS** successfully and then **fails to
  EVALUATE** at an all-zero operand. A transform that fails to load leaves
  `tint: None` and `tint_to_cmyk` returns early without counting.
- **The fixtures' transform fails at LOAD**, which is the commoner
  malformation and the one worth pinning.

The comment now records the merge as **deliberately uncovered** and says
exactly why, rather than leaving it to read as tested. **A green sabotage
that is explained is a different artifact from a green sabotage that is
ignored**, and this project has a lesson on the distinction already
(`C:/personal_rag/pdf/lesson_20260819_green_sabotage_can_signal_fixture_insufficiency_not_just_untested_or_equivalent_code.md`).

#### ★ ONE OF THIS PROJECT'S OWN GATES BROKE ONE OF ITS OWN TESTS — filed as an OBSERVATION, not decided

`tools/check-image-colorspace-truth.py` writes a `_truth/` **subdirectory
beside the images it scores**. Pointing it at `fixtures/synthetic/images` —
the obvious thing to do, and what the engineer did while running the gate
sweep — made `every_fixture_either_imports_or_refuses_by_name` die on
`std::fs::read` of a **directory**, which on Windows is `PermissionDenied` /
*"Access is denied."*

**So the panic reads as a filesystem-rights problem and sends the reader
after their antivirus.** Fixed in `25d73d7`: the test now **skips
directories** and **names the failing path**.

**★ `.gitignore` would not have helped.** The failure is on **disk** and has
nothing to do with what is **tracked** — a distinction worth stating,
because `.gitignore` is the reflex answer to "a tool wrote a directory into
my tree" and it addresses a different problem entirely.

**⇒ OPEN OBSERVATION FOR THE ENGINEER, deliberately NOT decided by this
role:** *should the gate be writing into a fixture directory at all?* An
output directory beside the input is convenient and is why nobody noticed;
an output directory **outside** the fixture tree would make this class
structurally impossible rather than defended against per-test. That is an
engineering call about a tool this role does not own, and it is recorded
here so it does not evaporate — **not** promoted to a Pass, and **not**
answered.

#### ★ `ImageNotes` LOSES `Copy` AND `Eq` — a public type change, recorded, and a rule candidate at n = 1

`ImageNotes` is `pub` in `pdfce-render`; `Pass 140.2` drops `Copy` and `Eq`
from its derives, because `ColorDiagnostics` owns a deduped-and-capped
`Vec<String>` of notes and is neither. **This is a breaking change to a
public type's trait surface** and is filed as such rather than left to be
discovered.

The engineer's reasoning, relayed: keeping the derives would have meant
**leaving the field off the struct** — *which is the arrangement that made
this silent in the first place*. *"A diagnostics bag that grows is the
normal case; a `Copy` bound that decides what may be diagnosed is the tail
wagging the dog."*

**Recorded as a NAMED CANDIDATE at n = 1, not minted:** *a trait bound must
not decide what a type is allowed to record.* It is a real principle and it
is a sibling of `R221` (a parallel description of a capability drifts from
the capability); it is **one instance**, and this project's bar is two. If a
second derive-driven omission turns up, this is the entry to cite.

#### `Pass 140.0` — the image routes, and there are TWO of them

**Symptom, as reported.** A five-colorant `DeviceN` photograph rendered
visibly desaturated against the Acrobat reference — washed toward grey where
the reference is saturated green.

**Cause.** On a page compositing in a four-colorant buffer, a
`Separation`/`DeviceN` image resolved through its tint transform **to sRGB**
and never to its `DeviceCMYK` alternate, so it entered the buffer through a
`CMYK → sRGB → CMYK` round trip. **The two legs are different functions.**
The outbound leg is `Rgb::from_cmyk`, the calibrated conversion carrying a
rendering intent; the return leg is `overprint::rgb_to_cmyk`, naive
maximum-GCR — which is an exact inverse of `cmyk_to_rgb`, a *third* function
the paint colour never went through. **They are not an inverse pair, and code
that pairs them reads as an exact recovery.**

**Two routes were fixed, and only one was reported:**

3. a **direct** `Separation`/`DeviceN` image over a `DeviceCMYK` alternate — the reported one;
4. an **`/Indexed` image over such a base — a duotone** — **not in the report**, found by walking `R219`'s checklist.

Both now route through one new answer, `Space::to_cmyk`, so the per-texel path
and the palette-build path **cannot come to disagree**. (The numbering 3/4
continues the `R219` route enumeration below.)

**The trap the Backlog entry named is avoided.** The overprint colorant planes
are **not** reused. They hold `authored_tints`, which answers Table 149's
*"which components did the source SPECIFY"* — a different question — and they
return `None` for a spot-only `DeviceN`, where a plain render needs the
flattened tint and would otherwise paint **bare white paper**.

**Measured against the Acrobat reference on the patch that opened the Pass, at
scale 2** (engineer's figures, relayed):

| what | before | after | Acrobat |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| photograph region, dE | 33.06 | **16.85** | — |
| an inset patch of it, dE | 29.57 | **7.13** | — |
| saturation spread | 51.8 | **90.2** | 87.3 |
| `cmyk_bridged_pixels` | 25,870 | **0** | — |
| `cmyk_native_image_pixels` | 0 | **25,870** | — |

**The two counters are complements and moved as complements** — the same
25,870 pixels, relabelled from *"lost its ink on the way in"* to *"kept it"*.

#### ★ `Space::yields_cmyk` is a PROBE, not a structural predicate — and that was deliberate

The gate could have pattern-matched the colour space's **shape** (*is this a
`Separation`/`DeviceN` whose alternate is `DeviceCMYK`?*). It instead **asks
the real conversion function** with an all-zero operand, so there is **one**
answer to *"does this space have colorants"* rather than two descriptions that
can drift apart.

**A wrong probe cannot paint a wrong colour in either direction**, which is
what makes the choice cheap: a **false negative** bridges exactly as before
(the status quo, disclosed), and a **false positive** is caught by an
**all-or-nothing discard** that drops the planes for the whole image rather
than leaving a seam mid-photograph.

Standing rule **`R221`** is minted from this, at n = 2 — see *Standing rules*.

#### `Pass 140.1` — the path fill, and `Pass 140.0` is what exposed it

**It did not exist as a filed Pass before this session.** With only the image
half fixed, the new fixtures reported the **fill** and the **image** 8.3 to
9.0 mean levels apart on the same authored colour, and the **additive control
page** — which allocates no colorant buffer and therefore never took the round
trip — identified which half was wrong (engineer's figures, relayed; mean over
a 40×100 pt patch of each half, scale 2):

| page | fill | image | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Separation`, **additive** | 157,207,185 | 158,208,186 | agree — no round trip on this page |
| `Separation`, subtractive | 159,192,194 | 158,208,186 | ← the **FILL** is the outlier |
| `DeviceN`, subtractive | 160, 86,161 | 160,108,156 | ← likewise |

**The image agrees with its own additive rendering; the subtractive fill does
not.** So the fill was reconstructing its colorants from the already-resolved
sRGB by the same round trip. `Interpreter::authored_cmyk` now asks
`ColorSpace::to_cmyk` **first** and **falls through unchanged** for every
space that has no `DeviceCMYK` answer — a `Separation` over a `DeviceRGB`
alternate, a `DeviceGray` fill, a `Lab` fill: none of them reaches the early
return and none of their behaviour moves.

**★ Why nothing had ever reported this.** Before `Pass 140.0`, *both* halves
took the round trip and were wrong **together**. Fixing one half converts a
silent shared error into a visible disagreement, **and the disagreement is the
information** — the exact history `tests/shading_ink.rs` already records for
the shading half, one object type over.

#### Tests, and the sabotage that proves route 5 is genuinely covered

`tools/gen-devicen-image-fixtures.py` builds **four pages**; each draws the
same authored colour **twice**, once as a fill and once as an image, **so the
oracle is `fill == image` and needs no reference render at all.** The
`/DeviceN` page's tint transform is **deliberately not a pass-through**, so
*"what did the source specify"* and *"what does the transform produce"* have
different answers and a renderer cannot pass by confusing them.

Five integration tests plus two unit tests, **each sabotaged**:

| sabotage | tests failed, of 5 |
|---|---:|
| `carries_ink` loses the probe | 3 |
| indexed ink table only for `DeviceCMYK` | **1** (the duotone alone) |
| `Space::to_cmyk`'s `Special` arm → `None` | 4 |
| `Pass 140.1`'s early return removed | 4 |
| the `tinting` discriminator dropped | 3 |

**No two sabotages fail the same set**, and **the duotone route is caught by
exactly one test** — which is the evidence that route 5 is genuinely covered
rather than incidentally passing. A route covered by *zero* distinguishing
tests and a route covered by *one* look identical on a green run.

#### ★ A generator bug worth a line, because the error message names the symptom and not the cause

**A classic cross-reference table is written as ONE CONTIGUOUS SUBSECTION**, so
a gap in the object numbering **silently shifts every entry after it** and the
file dies with a message that names the symptom (a bad object at some offset)
and not the cause (a missing number, hundreds of bytes earlier). The fixture
generator now **asserts contiguity** rather than trusting it. This is the
write-side twin of §7.5.4's completeness requirement already recorded in
`C:/personal_rag/pdf/` — see *RAG escalation* in the session log.

#### ★★★★★ FIRST, THE CORRECTION, BECAUSE IT INVALIDATES A CLAIM IN THE COMMIT BEING FILED AND IN A DOCUMENT ALREADY SENT TO ANOTHER PROJECT

**`3ffd86f`'s §3.6 says bold and italic are unavailable on existing text.
They are not. They have shipped since 2026-08-03.**

The section's own table reads:

| the operator's button | field | works? |
|---|---|---|
| **face** | `set_font: Option<FontSelector>` | ⚠️ only to a font ALREADY a resource on the page |
| **bold / italic** | `set_font` | ❌ in general, for that reason |

**Both rows are about `set_font`, and `set_font` is not the only route.**
`FormatRequest` carries a **second** field for exactly this case:

```
pub set_synthetic: Option<StyleSynthesis>   crates/pdfce-core/src/text_edit/format.rs:677
FormatRequest::synthetic(self, StyleSynthesis) -> Self                            :773
pdfce-cli format-text --bold-synthetic --italic-synthetic
                                            crates/pdfce-cli/src/main.rs:4265, 4272
```

Shipped as **`Pass 19.2`** (`ebe35d8`, 2026-08-03, decision 019 §3.6,
standing rule **`R90`**), with **`Pass 19.3`** (`74052d3`) adding the
side-effect-free query `EditSession::preview_style_resolution`. Bold is
emitted as **§9.3.6 Table 106 text rendering mode 2** (fill-then-stroke) with
a user-space stroke width derived from the rendered size and the stroking
colour matched to the fill; italic as a **§9.4.2 Table 108 shear
premultiplied into `Tm`**. Neither writes a private marker — decision 019
§3.6 chose **P-selfevident**, so the result is re-detectable by inspection
(`synth::detect`), including **other producers'** faux styles.

**★★ AND THE GATE RUNS THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM THE ONE §3.6 DESCRIBES.**
`gate_synthesis` (`format.rs:2132`, read here) refuses with
`FormatError::RealFaceAvailable` **when a real bold/italic face IS already a
resource on the page**, because `R90` makes synthesis a *fallback*, never an
alternative to a real typeface. Its first branch is explicit:

```rust
// No font resources to search: nothing better exists, so the
// fallback is genuinely the only option. Proceed.
```

So on the very page §3.6 uses as its worked example — Helvetica-only, no
`Helvetica-Bold` resource — `--set-font Helvetica-Bold` is refused with
`TargetFontMissing` **and `--bold-synthetic` proceeds.** The two routes'
predicates are **exact complements.** Between them, **bold is reachable on
every page**, and italic on every page except one narrow case: a
`Td`/`TD`/`T*` next-line operator following the run inside the same text
object, refused by name because a shear left in `Tm` would propagate into
every later line (`format.rs:2712`).

**What is actually blocked by FF-C is narrower than either document says:
a REAL bold or italic FACE cannot be added to a page that does not already
carry one.** That is a typographic-quality gap, not a capability gap.

`D:/Dev/FeatureRequests/pdfce_FeatureRequests/open/reply_restyle_already_exists_and_the_real_gap_is_narrower_than_your_table.md`

#### `Pass 141.0` — `tools/icc-census/`, and a sibling project's constant now has a population behind it

**What it is.** A standalone binary at `tools/icc-census/` (`main.rs`
**1,060** lines, `tests.rs` **265**, plus a tracked `Cargo.lock` matching
every sibling census tool) that walks pdfce's rights-cleared corpus and
inventories every embedded ICC profile.

**Why it exists.** `iccce` filed two requests on 2026-08-17 with a reply owed
and never given — `request_profile_population_census.md` and
`request_header_tag_channel_disagreement.md`. Their stated reason is an audit
of their own load-bearing constant, in their words:

> *"iccce recommends a 33-node CLUT grid for 3- and 4-channel sources in its
> compiled fast path […] That evidence rests on ONE profile pair, ONE
> direction, ONE tag type […] I have no way to find out from inside this
> repository. Every profile iccce has ever been tested against was synthetic,
> OS-shipped, or standards-body issued."*

Twenty profiles from one publisher's test corpus is a **sample**. Four
thousand real-world documents is a **population**. This is the one question
in this ecosystem only pdfce can answer, which is the whole justification for
spending a Pass on a tool that ships nothing.

**★★ THE METHOD, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE OBVIOUS ONE, AND IT IS THE
DESIGN DECISION WORTH CARRYING.** The obvious census follows the references
the request enumerates — `/OutputIntents /DestOutputProfile`, `ICCBased`,
image `/ColorSpace`. **That design under-counts BY CONSTRUCTION:** it finds
only the paths its author thought of, and **a census whose error direction is
"silently missed some" is worse than useless, because the miss looks like a
finding about the population.**

`icc-census` instead decodes **every stream in every file** and treats one as
a profile **iff it carries `acsp` at offset 36** (ICC.1:2010 §7.2.6, fixed
for every conformant profile of every version). It cannot miss a profile
present as a stream, whatever names the file uses to reach it, and its error
direction is the safe one.

**The reference paths are still recorded — as a CLASSIFICATION of what was
found, never as the search.** Profiles reachable by no recognised path land
in `unclassified`, **a bucket that is itself the measurement of what a
reference-following census would have dropped.** It is **1 of 2,494**.

★ That bucket caught a defect in the tool on its first smoke run. The
classification walk originally inspected only top-level object values, and an
`[/ICCBased <stream>]` array is very rarely an indirect object — it sits
inline inside a page's `/Resources /ColorSpace`. It reported **1 of 2**
unclassified, *"which reads as a finding about the corpus and was a finding
about the loop"*. Now recursive, depth-guarded.

**What it found** (engineer's figures, relayed).

**4,023 files scanned; 3,912 parsed; 111 failed to load; 0 timed out; 0
panicked. 2,234 files carry at least one profile = 2,494 embeddings over 49
distinct profiles** — so **1.12 embeddings per profile-bearing file** and
**50.9 embeddings per distinct profile**, the two denominators the tool
prints every distribution over, because they answer different questions.

| axis | measurement |
|---|---|
| transform shape, **share of 2,494 embeddings** | 85.2 % `matrix+curv`, 9.3 % `kTRC`-only, 5.4 % `mft2`; **one each** of `mAB`, `matrix+para`, `mft1` |
| **CLUT grid nodes, share of 2,494 embeddings** | **94.6 % carry NO CLUT AT ALL**; 9 nodes 4.3 %, 11 nodes 1.0 %, 6 nodes 0.04 % |
| **★ maximum CLUT grid OBSERVED in the population** | **11 nodes** — not 33 |
| version, share of 2,494 embeddings | 99.1 % v2.1; **four** v4 embeddings; **two claiming v5.0**, which no published ICC spec defines |
| data colour space, share of 2,494 embeddings | 85.2 % RGB, 9.3 % GRAY, 5.4 % CMYK, plus non-conformant `LAB ` and `YYY ` signatures |
| request ask 3 — header/tag channel disagreement | **136 CHECKABLE embeddings of 2,494, ZERO disagreements**; the other 94.5 % carry no LUT tag to check |
| PDF `/N` vs profile header channel count | **2 disagreements of 2,493**, and **BOTH DIRECTIONS OCCUR** |

The two `/N` disagreements, named rather than counted (`96b6ded`):

```
profile says 4 channel(s), the PDF says /N 3  --  Coated FOGRA27
profile says 3 channel(s), the PDF says /N 4  --  Adobe RGB (1998)
```

**★ THE CAVEAT THE ENGINEER ASKED TO BE ON THE RECORD, AND IT IS THE
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A MEASUREMENT AND A DIRECTIVE.** The census measures the
grid **profiles CARRY**. `iccce`'s constant is the grid **`iccce` BUILDS**.
Those are different quantities, and 11-vs-33 fits *too* well to be acted on
without saying so. The reply says so rather than letting the number be
mistaken for an instruction, and it also records a **disagreement to
resolve**: `iccce`'s own evidence names `USWebCoatedSWOP.icc` as carrying a
33-node `lut8`, while the `U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2` in this corpus reports
**9**.

**Tests: 11, byte-authored, no ICC file on disk.** A parser of untrusted
input gets tests even when it is *"only"* a measurement tool, because its
numbers are about to be written into another project's `NUMERIC_CLAIMS.md`.
Three sabotages, **each failing exactly one test**:

| sabotage | tests failed | why it is a real trap |
|---|---|---|
| `B2A0` checked on its **INPUT** channels | **1** | `B2A0` runs PCS→device, so the **output** count is the data space's; checking byte 8 for both directions reports **every conformant CMYK `B2A0`** as a 3-vs-4 disagreement — a false positive **on the exact axis being measured** |
| version byte read **whole** rather than as BCD nibbles | **1** | §7.2.4 packs minor and bug-fix as two nibbles; reading the byte whole reports **v2.16 for v2.1** — plausible and wrong |
| matrix preferred over a LUT tag | **1** | §8.3 makes `A2B0`/`B2A0` the general path; a profile carrying both is using the tables, and preferring the matrix would misattribute **every CMYK profile that also carries one** |

Plus a truncation sweep over **every prefix** of a well-formed profile, and a
hostile tag count.

**Boundary.** See decision **093** below. Nothing here converts colour;
`tools/icc-census` is in the root manifest's `exclude`, so
`check-fmt-excluded.py` is clean at **13 crates** and the tool is absent from
`THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`. **No profile bytes are ever written** — `iccce`
asked not to receive them, citing the licensing on several. `--tsv` emits one
row per distinct profile so they can re-cut it without a re-run.

#### ★ THREE SELF-CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANYTHING LEFT THE REPOSITORY, AND THE THIRD IS THE TRANSFERABLE ONE

All three were caught by **reading the output**, not by a test — recorded
because a number that is wrong *and* internally consistent is exactly the
kind a test cannot see.

1. **An extrapolation reported as a measurement, wrong by 45×.** The
   embedding-weighted `/N`-disagreement count multiplied each **distinct**
   profile's first-seen `/N` by its embedding count — which silently assumes
   **every embedding of one profile declares the same `/N`**, the very thing
   the axis exists to test. **It said 91. The measured figure is 2.** Now
   tallied per embedding.
2. **A bucket that could not distinguish "checked and clean" from "not
   checked".** Ask 3 first reported *"100 % agree, or no LUT tag"* across
   2,494 embeddings — **which looks like a strong negative result and is
   equally consistent with the check never having run.** Split into three
   states; the honest answer is **136 checkable, all 136 agreeing.**
3. **★ THE SAME EXTRAPOLATION SURVIVING IN THE DETAIL EXPORT.** Fixing (1)
   in the **aggregate** did nothing about the `/N` column in the **TSV**,
   which is still one sample per fingerprint — and a sentence was then
   written from it (*"the single culprit is one Coated FOGRA27 stream"*) that
   the column could not support. It is **two profiles and two directions**,
   and the opposite direction is the more surprising half. Column renamed
   `pdf_n_FIRST_SEEN`, *"so that a reader cannot make the mistake I made,
   which is worth more than a comment saying not to."*

**Why (3) generalises:** the aggregate was corrected by adding a
per-embedding counter; the detail export went on presenting a first-seen
sample under a name that reads like a fact about the row; and **nothing
connected the two.** One assumption, two artefacts, one fix. Written up at
`D:/dev/rag/rust/correcting_an_extrapolation_in_the_aggregate_leaves_the_same_extrapolation_in_the_detail_export.md`.

#### Decision minted — **093**

**Reading a profile's header and tag table to COUNT things is inventory, not
conversion — permitted under decision 064, and it lives in `tools/`, never in
`pdfce-core` or `pdfce-render`.** Full text in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12;
decision **064** gains a third forward pointer to it.

The question is real rather than pedantic: 064 gives `iccce` *"profile
**parsing**"*, and that phrase is what a future session will grep. A tool
that decodes a stream, checks `acsp` and walks a tag table **is** parsing a
profile by that phrase. The discriminator written down instead: **could this
code be wrong in a way that shows up as a wrong PIXEL?** Every figure
`icc-census` produces is a count or a label; not one is a colour. And the
**placement is half the decision** — pdfce told `iccce` in writing on
2026-08-25 that *"nothing in pdfce has ever decoded an ICC profile"*, and
keeping the tool out of the workspace is what keeps that sentence true **of
the shipping engine**, which is the scope in which it was made.

#### Standing rule minted — **`R220`**

**A capability is documented where the reader's QUESTION lives, not only
where its MECHANISM lives; and a claim that pdfce has no verb for something
is checked against SOURCE before it is sent anywhere.**

Full text in *Standing rules*. Minted at **n = 2 in one day, with the second
instance found inside the repair for the first** — a stronger warrant than a
count, because it shows the failure survives being named.

**The mint is argued against the immediately preceding precedent, decision
092, which DECLINED a rule at n = 3.** That decline was correct and this mint
does not weaken it: 092's three instances were *"three sites of one design
question"* — a principle a reader is **sent to**, which a decision record
carries. `R220`'s two instances are **two independent recurrences**, in
different documents, by different authors, against different verbs, one of
which **left the repository as a false statement to another project**. It is
a **habit a filing must demonstrate**, not a principle to consult, and that
is the `R`-rule shape. **No gate can enforce it** —
`tools/check-core-api-verbs.py` fires on a verb being **absent**, and
findability is not a property any script can evaluate — which is exactly why
it belongs in the reading rather than in CI.

### `Pass 81.1` (`4eaea20`) — AUTHORING A MARKUP AT AN OPACITY TOOK TWO VERBS AND LEFT **TWO UNDO ENTRIES**, SO ONE `Ctrl+Z` GAVE THE OPERATOR AN OPAQUE HIGHLIGHT NOBODY ASKED FOR — ★★★★ **IT SHIPPED IN A DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM THE ONE FILED ON 2026-08-14, AND THE DIVERGENCE IS THE ENTRY** (`MarkupOptions`, an options struct, **not** `opacity` on `MarkupSpec`) — ★★★ **BOTH AUTHORING ROUTES IN ONE PASS**, because Table 164 is the **markup-annotation** entry list and a sticky note is a markup annotation — ★★ **REFUSE AT THE AUTHOR VERB, CLAMP AT THE RESTYLE VERB**, and the asymmetry is now decision **092** — ★ **DECISION 062 WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, AND A NAMED-BY-NAME STALE CLAIM IN `docs/core-api/` WAS CORRECTED** — 2026-08-27 (292nd filing)

#### ★★★★ FIRST, THE DIVERGENCE FROM THE FILED SCOPE, BECAUSE THE *Next up* ENTRY BELOW STILL SAYS SOMETHING ELSE

The 2026-08-14 scoping entry (hundred-and-forty-seventh filing) is headed
**"`opacity` on `MarkupSpec`"** and its acceptance criterion 1 says
`opacity: Option<f64>` **on `MarkupSpec`'s variants**. **That is not what
shipped, deliberately.** The scoping entry is kept verbatim in *Next up*
under a status banner rather than rewritten to match — house style, and the
same treatment `Pass 81.0` got when it shipped mid-filing.

**What shipped instead:**

```
MarkupOptions { opacity: Option<f64> }        a new public INPUT struct
MarkupOptions::validate()                     ONE validator, both routes
EditSession::add_markup_with(page_index, spec, options)
EditSession::add_text_annotation_with(page_index, spec, options)
EditError::MarkupOpacityOutOfRange { value: f64 }
pdfce-cli: `annotate --opacity ALPHA`         (rule 11)
```

**Two reasons, and the second is the structural one.**

1. **`MarkupSpec` is an enum of EIGHT geometric variants.** A field on "the
   variants" is **eight copies of one field**, which is `R92`'s failure mode
   written into a type rather than into a function.
2. **★ `/CA` is a WHOLE-ANNOTATION property and `MarkupSpec` describes what
   the APPEARANCE DRAWS.** `rect`, `border_width` and `endings` all answer
   *what marks go in the stream*. §12.5.2 Table 164 makes `/CA` the alpha
   with which **the annotation is composited onto the page** — it does not
   affect what the appearance draws at all, and pdfce's generated
   appearances deliberately leave their own graphics-state alpha at `1.0`
   so the two cannot compound. Putting `/CA` beside `rect` would have filed
   a compositing property under geometry, and the next reader would have
   reached for the appearance stream to implement it — which is precisely
   the Highlight-`ExtGState` shortcut the scoping entry warned against.

`MarkupOptions` is shaped to carry **`/T`, `/Contents`, `/NM` and `/M` as
they land** (`Pass 80.0` is the next claimant). It is **deliberately not
`#[non_exhaustive]`**, same reasoning as `MarkupStyle`: an **input** struct
a consumer constructs would be **unbuildable from outside the crate**.

`add_markup` is **exactly**
`add_markup_with(.., &MarkupOptions::default())`, and `add_text_annotation`
likewise — **pinned by a test**, because a delegation "simplified" into two
bodies is how the drift this Pass fixes started.

#### The defect, and it is an UNDO defect rather than an ergonomic one

`/CA` was reachable **only** through `EditSession::set_markup_style`, a
**restyle** verb, which by definition acts on an annotation that already
exists. Authoring a 40 %-opaque highlight therefore meant
author-opaque-then-restyle: **two verbs, two undo entries.**

**An operator who draws a translucent highlight and presses `Ctrl+Z` once
got an OPAQUE HIGHLIGHT** — a state they never asked for and **could not
have created by any other route**. That reads as a bug in undo, and it is
one.

**★ The requesting shell could have coalesced the pair on its own side. It
reported instead** — `D:/Dev/FeatureRequests/pdfce_FeatureRequests/open/request_authoring_a_markup_at_an_opacity_takes_two_verbs.md`,
2026-08-19, filed under **decision 058** as *"a boundary observation, not
urgent, not blocking"*. A shell-side coalesce would have worked **and left
every other consumer with the same defect.** That is decision 058 working
as designed, and it is worth saying: the report was filed as ergonomics and
turned out to be correctness.

#### ★★★ BOTH AUTHORING ROUTES, IN ONE PASS — and the reason is that the requester asked a NARROWER QUESTION than the standard answers

The requesting shell asked about **geometric markup only**. *"Which
annotations does `/CA` apply to"* **is not the same question**, and the
standard answers the second one: **Table 164 is the MARKUP ANNOTATION entry
list**, and `FreeText`, `Text` (sticky note) and `Stamp` are markup
annotations exactly as `Square` and `Highlight` are.

**Shipping one route would have reproduced the failure this project has hit
three times in three days** — fixing one route makes the others look broken,
and the shell finds out by pressing a control that works on a rectangle and
not on a sticky note.

**`/CA` goes on the PARENT annotation only, never on its `/Popup`.** A popup
is not itself a markup annotation — §12.5.6.14 gives it no `/CA` — it is
chrome the viewer draws.

#### ★★ THREE BEHAVIOURS, EACH DECIDED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED

| value | behaviour | why |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | **OMITS the key** | Table 164's default **is** 1.0, so writing it adds a key that changes nothing and makes a pdfce-authored opaque annotation **textually distinguishable from every other producer's**, for no gain. §5's *never normalize*. |
| `Some(1.0)` | **IS WRITTEN** | Renders identically to `None`; **is not the same bytes.** Collapsing it would be pdfce deciding what the caller meant. Inherited from `Pass 81.0`, which stores `Option<f64>` precisely so **absent** and **explicitly 1.0** stay distinguishable through a round trip. |
| out of range / `NaN` / `∞` | **REFUSED BY NAME**, nothing authored, session untouched | See below — this is the OPPOSITE of `MarkupStyle::opacity`, which **clamps**. |

#### ★★ THE REFUSE / CLAMP ASYMMETRY, WHICH IS NOW **DECISION 092**

`MarkupStyle::opacity` (the **restyle** verb) **clamps**. `MarkupOptions::
opacity` (the **author** verb) **refuses by name**. Both are correct, and a
reader who sees only one of them will "fix" the other.

- **A restyle corrects a value on an annotation the operator can SEE.**
  Clamping keeps it renderable and **visibly changes it** — the operator
  watches `4.0` become fully opaque and can undo.
- **An author call with alpha `4.0` is a caller BUG.** Clamping there would
  **put a fully opaque annotation on the page while returning `Ok`** —
  reporting success for a gesture whose entire point was the transparency,
  and the operator sees no annotation-shaped evidence that anything was
  corrected, because there was nothing there before.

The scoping entry predicted this asymmetry from the **read** side
(`Pass 81.0` clamps a foreign file's out-of-range `/CA`); the general rule is
now filed as **decision 092** in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12, with the revision-
cloud `/I` precedent (a file's out-of-range `/I` is clamped, an operator
typing the same value is refused) as its second instance.

#### ★ DECISION 062 WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED — AND A CLAIM THAT NAMED THIS VERB BY NAME WAS FALSIFIED

`docs/core-api/02-editing-and-saving.md` carried, on the `set_quad_point_
order` row: *"decision 062 fixes markup authoring at one entry point, so an
`add_markup_with` would be a second"*. **That sentence is now false, and it
named the verb.** It is **corrected in place in `4eaea20` with the old
wording kept struck through**, and a new **§1.15.1** reconciles the two.

**What 062 refused** was `add_markup_appearance` — a hatch letting a caller
hand the engine a **prebuilt annotation dictionary plus appearance stream**,
bypassing four guards, **three of which are document-safety properties whose
failure is SILENT IN THE SAVED FILE** (encrypted document; certified
document forbidding annotation; a `/Size` hiding objects).

**What `add_markup_with` does** is take **one more validated scalar**
alongside the same `MarkupSpec`. There is **ONE BODY**: `add_markup` →
`add_markup_with` → private `add_markup_inner`, which runs **all four
guards** and calls the same `annot_author::build_appearance`. Nothing is
bypassed; the Pass **adds a fifth validation.** 062's own test — *"a guard
that a second entry point can bypass is not a guard, it is a convention"* —
is satisfied.

**The quad-point-order ruling that sentence was attached to STILL STANDS**,
on its own ground rather than on the falsified premise: **quad order is a
DOCUMENT-WIDE CONVENTION**, so a per-call argument would let two annotations
in one file disagree about what UL/UR/LL/LR means. Decision 062 carries a
dated amendment recording this, so a reader arriving at 062 cold does not
hit the same apparent contradiction.

#### ★ ONE VALIDATOR, NOT TWO — and how it was found is the reusable half

`MarkupOptions::validate` is a **function** because **both routes call it**.
Written inline in each it would be **two expressions of one rule** —
`R92`'s failure mode, **and precisely the shape that let `/CA` be reachable
from the restyle verb and not the author verb in the first place.**

**Worth recording HOW it surfaced:** clippy's `collapsible_if` is what made
the engineer look at those lines. **The DUPLICATION was the real finding,
and clippy cannot see that.** A lint pointing at a line is sometimes only
useful as a reason to read it.

#### Acceptance criteria, against what was filed 2026-08-14

| # | filed criterion | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `opacity: Option<f64>` on `MarkupSpec`'s variants; `None` omits `/CA` | **DIVERGED on the carrier, MET on the behaviour** — the field is on `MarkupOptions`, not on the enum (see above); `None` omits the key, asserted against saved bytes. |
| 2 | **Refuse by name**, do not clamp, outside `0.0..=1.0` | **MET**, and widened: `NaN` and `±∞` are refused too, and nothing is authored — the session is left byte-identical. |
| 3 | **No `ExtGState` is written** — asserted against the saved appearance stream | **MET** (`the_appearance_stream_can_carry_no_alpha_of_its_own`). |
| 4 | Highlight's multiply-blend `ExtGState` unchanged; a Highlight authored with opacity carries **both** | **MET** — pdfce's generated appearances leave their own graphics-state alpha at 1.0, so annotation `/CA` and the blend `ExtGState` cannot compound. |
| 5 | A **render** test proving the written `/CA` is honoured by `Pass 81.0`'s reader | **MET end to end on real files through the CLI**, not only in tests — see the verification block. |
| 6 | `pdfce-cli` gains `--opacity` (rule 11) | **MET** — `annotate --opacity ALPHA`. |
| 7 | `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean | **MET**, workspace-wide, `--all-targets`. |
| — | *not filed:* the **text-annotation** route | **ADDED** — see the both-routes section. |

#### ★ A GATE FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THE NEW TEST — `n = 7` on a family this project has now hit seven times

`check-string-gaps.sh` caught a **wrapped string literal in
`tests/markup_opacity.rs` that had lost its continuation backslashes** while
being patched through a shell heredoc. It would have shipped an assertion
message with **13-space gaps**.

**The new datum, and the reason it is recorded rather than silently
incremented:** every prior occurrence was in **shipped** code — a `println!`,
a doc comment, an operator-facing status line. **This one was in a TEST's
assertion message**, which surfaces **only when the test fails** — i.e. at
exactly the moment someone is trying to read it. The gate does not care
where the literal lives; a human re-reading the diff would not have thought
to look there.

The finding's home is

### `Pass 139.0` + `Pass 139.1` + `Pass 139.2` (`c362b6b`) — TEXT EXTRACTION PUBLISHED THE ADVANCE AS A LENGTH AND THREW THE DIRECTION AWAY, SO EVERY CAD TITLE BLOCK CAME BACK ONE LETTER PER LINE — ★★★★ A PASS-ID COLLISION IS RESOLVED IN THIS FILING AND THE BACKLOG `Pass 139.0` FILED YESTERDAY IS RENUMBERED `Pass 140.0` — ★★★ THE SECOND COPY OF THE ASSUMPTION LIVED IN A SECOND MODULE AND ITS TESTS WENT ON PASSING FOR A DIFFERENT REASON — ★★ THREE FIXTURES BECAUSE SABOTAGE PROVED THE FIRST COVERED NOTHING — ★ FIRST FILED ENUMERATION UNDER `R219` — 2026-08-27 (291st filing)

#### ★★★★★ FIRST, THE PASS-ID COLLISION, BECAUSE IT RENAMES AN ENTRY CITED IN THE TWO FILINGS DIRECTLY BELOW THIS ONE

**`Pass 139.0` names two different features as of this dispatch, and that
is a hard-rule-2 violation that had to be resolved before anything else
could be filed.**

- **`c362b6b`** — pushed to `origin/main`, its commit message titled
  *"Pass 139.0/139.1/139.2 — text extraction publishes the writing
  direction…"*, and `docs/core-api/01-reading-and-model.md` §8.4.1 inside
  that same commit headed *"Text is not always horizontal — `direction`
  (`Pass 139.0`)"*.
- **The Backlog entry opened yesterday by the 289th filing** — a
  `Separation`/`DeviceN` image bridging through sRGB — also headed
  `Pass 139.0`, and cited as `Pass 139.0` at four places in
  `SESSION_LOG.md` and three in this file.

**Resolution: the shipped work keeps `139.0`/`139.1`/`139.2`; the
un-started Backlog entry is renumbered `Pass 140.0`.** The reasoning, so
a later session does not re-open it:

1. **A commit message is immutable and a Backlog heading is not.** The
   shipped ID is written into a pushed commit's subject line, its body,
   and a committed document inside the same diff. Renumbering *that* half
   would either require rewriting published history — categorically
   forbidden by `CLAUDE.md` rule 8, and the exact mechanism
   `tools/check-cited-commits-exist.py` (`0d9f4df`) was built after
   fourteen casualties of — or leave a permanent, unfixable disagreement
   between `ROADMAP.md` and a commit anybody can read on GitHub.
2. **The Backlog entry has shipped nothing, cites no hash, and is one
   day old.** Every citation of it is in this project's own documents,
   all of which this filing can reach and amend in the same edit.
3. **`140` was free** — `python tools/check-ledger-numbers.py`, run this
   filing, reported *"Pass families with headings : up to 139"* and did
   not list `140` among the thirty CLAIMED-BUT-NOT-YET-HEADED ids
   (`5, 9, 9c, 10, 13, 22, 31, 54…129`). Verified before the renumber,
   not assumed.

**★ This is still a reuse, and it is recorded as one rather than tidied
away.** Hard rule 2 says a Pass ID is never reused for a different
feature; between the 289th filing and this one, `139.0` named the
`DeviceN` image defect, and it now names rotated-text extraction. The
rule was broken by the *allocation*, not by this repair — and the repair
that costs least is the one that leaves the immutable half alone. Every
document that said `Pass 139.0` and meant the `DeviceN` defect carries a
dated pointer to `Pass 140.0` as of this filing: the Backlog heading
itself, the 289th filing's ROADMAP entry (amendment footer), `R219`'s own
amendment text in *Standing rules*, and the 289th/290th `SESSION_LOG.md`
entries (amendment footers).

**★★ The mechanism, because it will recur and is cheap to prevent.** The
Backlog opener and the shipped work were allocated by two different
readers of the same ceiling within about twenty hours. `check-ledger-
numbers.py` reported the ceiling as *"up to 138"* at both moments,
because **the gate reads headings, and a number claimed in a Backlog
heading is only visible once that heading exists** — the engineer
allocating `139.0` for a code Pass had no way to see that the librarian
had allocated `139.0` for a Backlog entry unless he read the Backlog. The
gate did not fail: it reported *"clean — no duplicate Pass, rule, or
decision numbers"* on the pre-collision tree, because only one of the two
`139.0`s was written down at that point. **Not promoted to a standing
rule this filing** (`n = 1`), but recorded as a named candidate: *a
number allocated in one document and consumed in another is allocated
twice unless the allocator is the same role.* The cheap habit that would
have caught it: re-run `check-ledger-numbers.py` at the moment of
allocation, not only at the moment of filing.

#### The defect

`ExtractedGlyph` published `advance` and `size` as **magnitudes** — the
lengths of the two transformed basis vectors of ISO 32000-1 §9.4.4's text
rendering matrix — and discarded their **directions**. `x`/`y` were exact
and orientation-independent; everything downstream then had no choice but
to assume the text ran along the page's `+x` axis.

True of virtually every word-processor page. **False of every CAD title
block**, which stamps its source path with `Tm = [0 1 -1 0 e f]` — that
is ordinary horizontal-mode text placed by a rotated matrix, **not**
§9.7.4.3 vertical writing mode (`/WMode 1`), which is a different feature
and is still not implemented.

Every derived-layout threshold in `text_extract::layout` was stated in
page axes, so a rotated line failed them in **two independent ways**:

| angle | what happens | clause that fires |
|---|---|---|
| **90° / 270°** | one advance lands entirely in `Δy`, exceeding `line_gap_ratio × size` for any glyph wider than a third of an em | the **baseline** clause |
| **180°** | the step is in `−x` while `advance` is a positive magnitude, so `Δx − advance ≈ −2·advance` | the **backward-jump** clause |

Either way, the verdict was **a derived line break between every letter**.

**Measured on the operator's own SOLIDWORKS drawing set** (`SW41177.pdf`,
page 36, title-block source path stamped vertically): **82 glyphs in 72
runs separated by 71 derived line breaks, for one line of text** — 71
breaks over 81 inter-glyph steps, **88 %**. It pasted into a text editor
as one character per line. Acrobat returns one line.

The same assumption corrupted **every box**. For a 90° glyph at
`(100, 300)` with `advance 8.7` and `size 12`, `min(x, x + advance)` gives
`x ∈ 100..108.7` while the ink is at `x ∈ 91..103` — a box overlapping its
own glyph by about a third and hung off the wrong corner.
`EditableTextModel::hit_test` uses those boxes, so a press on the middle
of a rotated letter was **outside every line box** and the nearest-line
fallback decided. Driven by the consuming shell: a sweep down a
six-letter 90° string selected **five of six**; a sweep along an
eight-letter 180° string selected **none of eight**, both ends having
collapsed onto one caret slot.

**Origin:** an open request on the `pdfceGUI` channel,
`D:/Dev/FeatureRequests/pdfce_FeatureRequests/open/request_extraction_drops_the_writing_direction.md`
(from `pdfceGUI`, 2026-08-26), carrying two asks plus a doc-comment
correction reported alongside. **All three shipped.** The empirical half
is filed at
`C:/personal_rag/pdf/lesson_20260826_rotated_text_extraction_axis_aligned_segmentation.md`
(updated this filing to record the resolution) — it is not duplicated
here.

#### `Pass 139.0` — publish the direction

```
ExtractedGlyph::direction: (f32, f32)   normalised x basis of Trm
ExtractedGlyph::up() / advance_end() / cell()
TextRun::direction() -> (f32, f32)
text_extract::glyph_cell(x, y, advance, size, direction) -> Rect
text_extract::SAME_DIRECTION_COS: f32 = 0.999_39      (≈ 2.0°)
ExtractOptions::same_direction_cos                    (new knob)
```

`(1.0, 0.0)` for ordinary horizontal text **and for a degenerate matrix**,
so a consumer that ignores the field is unchanged.

**★ NOT via `capture_provenance`, and the reason is a design principle
worth recording.** `GlyphProvenance` carries `text_matrix` and `ctm`, from
which the direction **is** derivable — but provenance is the **editing**
substrate, is **off by default**, and costs an owned font-resource name
plus an `Arc` clone **per glyph**. A reader that only wants to know which
way a line runs should not pay the surgery's price. **Direction is a
property of the glyph's placement, exactly like the four numbers beside
it.** Minted as **decision `091`** (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §12), first half.

**★ `glyph_cell` is a function because the expression it replaces was
written out four times** — in `layout`, in `page::extend_covered`, in
`text_edit::model`'s line accumulator, and in the CLI — each time
assuming `(1, 0)`. That is `R92`'s failure mode exactly: one question
answered in four places, drifting into being wrong **together**, with no
single place to fix it.

**★ `advance`'s doc comment was wrong on both its claims** and is
corrected. It read *"Horizontal advance in default user space, including
`Tc`, `Tw`, `Tz` and any `TJ` adjustment attributed to this glyph."* It
is not horizontal, **and `TJ` is not in it** — `show_array` applies the
adjustment to the text matrix **before** the glyph is placed (Table 109:
the number *"shall be subtracted from the current horizontal
coordinate"*), so it is already visible in `x`/`y`. **Two readers
believed that sentence and lost time to it.**

**★ `advance` stays unsigned, and that limit is now named rather than
hidden.** A glyph whose §9.4.4 displacement came out negative steps
*backward* along `direction`, and the sign is not published. The
alternative — a signed advance with `direction` flipping 180° mid-run —
is worse for every consumer that wants to orient a caret, and no such
glyph exists in the corpus.

#### `Pass 139.1` — segment in the line's own frame

`layout::classify` resolves the step from the previous glyph's **end**
into the line's frame: `along = d · dir`, `perp = d × dir`. **No new
ratio and no threshold retuned** — for `dir = (1, 0)` these are
`Δx − advance` and the `|Δy|` term, term for term, so a horizontal page's
output is **unchanged**. The cursor now carries the end **point** (origin
advanced along its own direction) rather than a scalar.

**One rule is new: a direction change is itself a line break, tested
first.** Without it, a horizontal run ending exactly where a vertical run
begins has `along = 0` and `perp = 0` and would merge — and **the merged
run would publish one direction for glyphs that do not share one.**

The `/ActualText` boundary test **deliberately stays in page axes**, and
says so at its call site: a replacement publishes an axis-aligned box and
no baseline at all (§14.9.4 N4 forbids per-character correspondence), so
**there is no frame to resolve into**.

#### `Pass 139.2` — the editable model, which was a second copy of the assumption

`EditableTextModel`'s Stage-1 defensive baseline-jump split was **also**
written in page axes, so with the extraction already fixed it
**re-fragmented the runs immediately — 16 lines for four lines of text**
on the new fixture. Now measured perpendicular to the line, plus the same
direction-change rule: **4 lines for four lines of text.**

```
Line::direction                                   (new pub field)
Line::bbox                                        via glyph_cell
hit_in_line                                       projects the point onto the line's direction
EditableTextModel::caret_point(pos) -> Option<(f32, f32)>
EditableTextModel::caret_on_line_nearest_point(line_index, x, y)
BlockRecognitionOptions::same_direction_cos       (new knob)
```

**★ `caret_x` and `caret_on_line_nearest_x` are kept and NOT
deprecated.** A scalar returning the same number for every slot on a
vertical line is the honest answer a scalar can give, and for horizontal
text — which is what Up/Down "desired column" *means* — it is exactly
right. **The fix was to publish the pair, not to redefine the scalar.**
Same shape as `Pass 138.0`'s `PickedLine::object_index`: an answer made
unrepresentable by its own type. Minted as **decision `091`**, second
half.

**★ Block and column recognition are NOT rotated**, and `Line::direction`'s
doc comment says so. Those stages stack lines by page-space `y` and band
them by page-space `x` — a model of laid-out prose, not of a title block.
**A rotated line is recognised as a line and is hit-testable; it is not
meaningfully assigned to a paragraph.**

#### CLI (rule 11)

`extract-text --json` emits `direction` per glyph **and** once per
glyph-bearing run. **Omitted for a glyph-less run** — derived whitespace
and `/ActualText` have no baseline, and printing `[1, 0]` there would be
inventing one.

#### Fixtures: three, and sabotage is why

`tools/gen-rotated-text-fixtures.py`, byte-authored, no PDF library,
`LEGAL.md` §5 category (a), **capitals throughout**:

| fixture | bytes | what it holds |
|---|---:|---|
| `fixtures/synthetic/text/rotated-text.pdf` | 777 | 0°/90°/180°/270°; **22 derived breaks → 3**. The horizontal block is a **control**. |
| `fixtures/synthetic/text/rotated-text-abutting.pdf` | 668 | a horizontal run whose end is **exactly** where a vertical run begins: `perp = 0`, gap `= 0`, so **only the direction rule can separate them**. |
| `fixtures/synthetic/text/rotated-text-columns.pdf` | 712 | a **3.332 pt** gap *along* a vertical baseline (a word space a page-axis reader drops entirely) and a second column **30 pt** *across* it with `Δy = 0` exactly (a line break a page-axis reader calls a word space, joining two columns). **Both wrong answers are quiet** — neither fragments visibly. |

**★★ The second and third fixtures exist because sabotage proved the
first did not cover what it appeared to.** Deleting the direction rule
outright left **all nine** of its tests green — its four blocks sit far
apart, so the perpendicular clause separates them regardless. Then
reverting `perp`/gap to page axes left **all fourteen** green, because
within a run the glyphs abut and `Δy` is zero, so **both formulas agree**.

**★★★ The Stage-1 defect in `139.2` was found the same way, and is the
sharper case.** With the extraction already fixed, the hit-test tests
passed **for the wrong reason** — every glyph of a vertical run had
become its own line, so every probe trivially found "its" line.
**Reverting the glyph-cell fix changed nothing**, which is what gave it
away.

> **When a fix upstream makes a downstream test start passing, the test
> may now be passing for a different reason than it was written for, and
> only sabotage distinguishes those.**

**Recorded as a named candidate for a standing rule at `n = 1`, mint
deliberately declined this filing** — the mint is the operator's/
engineer's act, this project's bar is two occurrences, and the class is
already covered in general terms by `R162` (*"could my assertion ever
have come out false?"*) and by
`D:/dev/rag/rust/prove_test_suite_non_vacuous_by_deliberately_breaking_the_thing_it_tests.md`.
What is **new** here, and is why it was written up rather than folded
into either, is that the vacuity was **acquired later**: the test was
sensitive when written and was rendered insensitive by a fix in a
*different module* three hours afterwards. Filed ecosystem-wide as
`D:/dev/rag/rust/a_test_can_become_vacuous_later_when_an_upstream_fix_changes_why_it_passes.md`.

**★ Capitals deliberately.** At 12 pt Helvetica every capital's advance
exceeds `line_gap_ratio × size = 3.6 pt`, so under the old rule **no run
held two glyphs**. A fixture of narrow lowercase letters hides that. The
consuming shell learned it the expensive way: it built a workaround
recovering the direction from the vector between a run's first and last
glyph — **sound reasoning and useless**, because on the real file only
**10 of 72 runs (13.9 %)** held two glyphs at all. **The segmentation was
so thorough on rotated text that it destroyed the evidence needed to undo
it.** That workaround — ~400 lines in `canvas::textsel::writing`, which
existed only because eight bytes were not published — can now be deleted.

### `cde21f5` — CI went red on `4c32afe` because two unfiled commits stacked, not one; `R217`'s closing sentence corrected for the second time by an actual occurrence — no Pass ID, memory/docs only — 2026-08-27 (290th filing)

**What happened.** `tools/check-commits-filed.py` failed CI on `4c32afe`,
naming **`51c30d6`** — the commit *behind* `4c32afe`, not `4c32afe`
itself — as unfiled. Nothing was wrong with either commit's content.
`51c30d6` was filed by this role's own 289th filing (`e3b4536`), which
landed **after** `4c32afe` had already been pushed as the tip; between
those two events, CI ran on `4c32afe` with `51c30d6` still owing a
filing, and hard-failed.

**The mechanism — a sharpening of `R217`, not a new fact about the gate.**
`R217` defers exactly the **tip**, on every run, because a commit cannot
cite its own hash and its filing is necessarily a later commit. That
deferral is correct and was working as designed. **`51c30d6` was
deferred, correctly, for exactly one CI run — the run on `51c30d6`
itself.** The moment `4c32afe` landed on top of it, `51c30d6` stopped
being the tip, lost its deferral, and was checked in full: unfiled, hard
fail. ⇒ **One unfiled commit may sit at the tip. Never two.**

**Second confirmed occurrence of a shape this project already named and
declined to promote.** The 271st filing (`v0.14.0`, `ffe9d4c`/`b135dec`
chain, `ROADMAP.md` lines ~3787–3835) hit the identical shape — a clean
17-gate sweep followed by two more commits, `check-commits-filed.py` red
on the tag — and recorded it as a **named candidate under `R217`, at
`n = 1`, explicitly declined to mint** ("the mint is the operator's
act"). This filing is `n = 2` of the same shape, which is this project's
usual two-occurrence promotion bar. See `Standing rules` below for the
amendment made in response — `R217` itself is corrected in place, not
re-minted, because the gap is in that rule's own closing sentence, not a
new mechanism.

**★ Why decision `090` ("always push") is not the thing to narrow, stated
plainly because a future reader could reach for exactly that repair.**
Decision `090` grants standing authority to **push**. It says nothing
about pushing **twice** before `pdfce-librarian` has run, and this
failure is a fact about a **gate's deferral width**, not about whether
pushing was permitted. Narrowing an operator's ruling to compensate for
a habit `090` never asked about would be the same mistake decision `061`
was written to warn against (narrow the rule that is actually wrong, not
the nearest one that happens to be adjacent). The repair here is
`R217`'s own text, and a re-affirmed habit — **file before a second code
commit lands, or don't push a second one until the filing is in** — not
anything about push authority itself.

**★★ The self-correcting property is the trap, and is worth naming on its
own.** `HEAD` goes green on the very next run (this filing cites
`51c30d6` and `4c32afe`, both now joined), the tree is clean, every local
gate passes, and the only surviving evidence is a **permanent red run on
an intermediate commit** on a public repository — costing nothing now,
which is exactly how "CI is green" stops being a claim anyone checks. A
gate that always heals by the next commit is a gate whose failures are
easy to stop reading.

#### Ledger

No new decision (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §12 unchanged at decision `090`, next
free `091`; **decision `090` is unaffected** — see above). No new
standing rule minted; `R217` **amended in place** (its closing sentence
corrected, not re-minted — see *Standing rules*, below). Ceiling: rules

unchanged). Not re-derived by shell this filing (hard rule 8; this

#### `51c30d6` — the sixth stale copy of one claim, and the first found by running the program

The `render-page` metrics-line note printed to the operator's terminal
read: *"images and shadings resolve their colour to sRGB before any
canvas sees them, so bridging them is the only information that reaches
the compositor."* True of every image until `Pass 130.1`, every shading
until `137.0`, every mesh until `137.1` — **stale since the first of
those three, discovered on the fourth commit that should have caught
it.**

of how it survived is the finding.** Three copies were fixed in

and the engineer discharged in `Pass 138.0`'s own filing; **this one

**Nothing in this repository checks operator-facing strings for claims
about implementation state.** Every existing gate (`check-ui-strings.sh`,

11's own sweeps) looks at code, documents, or commit metadata — none

the implementation changes under it. Recurrence count for the underlying
stale-claim problem: **six**. Recurrence count for this specific
gate-shaped gap (a claim invisible to review because it prints rather
than documents): **one**, this filing. **Not promoted to a standing rule

mechanical gate can content-check a disclosure, because such a gate would

exists to report (the same reasoning `CLAUDE.md` rule 11's derivation
already gives for declining a gate on doc-comment disclosures). The
cheaper fix offered: when a doc-comment claim is corrected, grep the
format strings for the same wording too. Left as a live question rather
than settled either way — a fourth occurrence would argue harder for
promotion.

`D:\Dev\FeatureRequests\pdfce_FeatureRequests\open\note_all_three_form_gaps_closed_and_one_judgement_made.md`.
No pre-existing Backlog bucket covered any of the three — requested and
