| **232nd** (`R215` minted) | `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md` §9 prose, as a **result** | not found — the mint swept `docs/`, not `tools/` |
| **233rd** | the same file, **still** — reported, not repairable by this role | **reading the file** |
| **234th** (this one) | the **table header** in the same section (`1b` above), and **two** boundary claims still wrong | **reading the file again, after the repair** |

**The diagnosis, stated so it is actionable rather than rueful: minting a rule
about a number is itself a MEANING-CHANGE EVENT, and hard rule 11 already
obliges the sweep for those — it was simply never read as applying to a mint.**
Hard rule 11 fires when *"a filing records that a counter or capability CHANGED
MEANING"*. `R215`'s mint recorded exactly that: `11 of 11` stopped being the
right answer and `2` became it. **The sweep was performed over `docs/` and did
not extend to `tools/`**, and the number was sitting in `tools/`.

⇒ **RECOMMENDED AMENDMENT TO HARD RULE 11 of `.claude/agents/pdfce-librarian.md`:
a mint or amendment of a standing rule is a meaning-change event for the number
the rule is about, and the sweep covers every tree the project writes prose in —
`docs/`, `crates/`, `tools/`, `.github/`, `README.md` — reported, not edited.**
**Filed as a recommendation, not applied.** That file is amended by the
engineer; the precedent is hard rule 11 itself, whose text records that this
role *"proposed accepting this and correctly declined to amend this file
unilaterally."* Same restraint, same reason.

**★ Why this is not a new standing rule.** It is a **procedural** commitment on
this role's own behaviour, which is the shape hard rules 8, 10 and 11 already
have and the shape `R210`'s minting test refuses for `ROADMAP.md` rules: no gate
can ask *"did the sweep cover every tree?"* without knowing what the rule is
about. **The right home is the agent file, not this section.**

#### ★ THE ID RULING — A **NEW** ID (`74.10`), NOT AN AMENDMENT TO `74.7`, AND THE DISPATCH LEANED THE OTHER WAY

**The engineer wrote *"I lean amendment, but you have the better view of the
numbering."* The ruling is a new ID**, and it is worth arguing because the
amendment case is genuinely strong: `d8f3020` completes a guarantee `74.7`
stated, and `74.7`'s own entry two commits ago set the precedent that *"the
scope grew to cover its own stated exclusion inside one Pass, so one ID covers
both."*

**Three grounds decide it the other way.**

1. **`PASS 74.7` IS ALREADY FILED AS SHIPPED, WITH A COMMIT TABLE AND A LEDGER
   ROW.** `74.7` grew across two commits *before it shipped*, at filing time,
   which is grouping. Growing a **shipped** entry two filings later makes
   *"`Pass 74.7`"* a moving target: a reader who cited *"`74.7`, shipped
   2026-08-23 across `1d6db9e` + `5b0d885`"* would find a third commit under the
   same name and no way to tell when it arrived. Hard rule 1 (*Shipped is
   append-only; history does not get rewritten*) and hard rule 2 (*Pass IDs are
   stable*) both point here.
2. **★★ THE SEQUENCE IS THE LESSON, AND FOLDING IT IN DESTROYS IT.** `74.7`
   **created** this defect — it moved the interpreter to `f64` and left the
   recorder in `f32`. Filed as one Pass, *"a precision fix opened a precision
   divergence"* becomes invisible: the entry would read as one clean piece of
   work. Filed as two, the sequence is legible and checkable — `74.7` shipped,
   it left a second path behind, **the filing of `74.7` flagged the question**,
   and `74.10` closed it. **That is the audit trail the append-only rule exists
   to produce**, and it is exactly the shape `R211` and `decision 081` are
   about: *moving one caller falsifies a claim in a file nobody edited.*
3. **The two Passes deliver different kinds of thing.** `74.7` **raises** a
   ceiling; `74.10` **refuses** past one. A reader following *"see `74.7`"*
   wants *how deep zoom became precise*; a reader following *"why did the
   recorder refuse at scale 5 000?"* wants a different story, with a different
   mechanism and a different caller obligation (fall back).

**`74.10` was the next free in the family** and the two-digit sub-ID is house
style (`Pass 47.10`/`47.11`, already on disk). **Next free in the family is now
`74.11`.** **A dated amendment is appended to `PASS 74.7`'s Shipped entry**
pointing forward to this one, so neither entry can be read alone and get the
wrong picture — the same forward-pointer convention the decision log uses for a
superseded decision.

#### ★★★★★ THE DEFECT — TWO RENDERING PATHS, ONE `f64` AND ONE `f32`, AGREEING EVERYWHERE ANYONE LOOKED

**What `PASS 74.7` changed:** the interpreter carries the CTM in `f64` through
content-stream composition (`Mat64`) and builds paths relative to their own first
point when `needs_precise_paths` fires.

**What it did not change:** a recorded `DisplayList` stores **every op's CTM as
an `f32` `Transform`**, and `replay_region` post-translates that by the region's
device origin, **also in `f32`**. Neither narrowing has anything to widen back
to — the precision is gone at record time.

**★ And nothing bounded the recorder, deliberately.** `record_page`'s own
comment reads:

> *"a recording allocates no raster, so the `MAX_PIXMAP_EDGE` ceiling does NOT
> apply here — that is the point of recording at a deep zoom."*

**Deep zoom is the INTENDED use of a recording**, which is why the absence of a
bound is a defect rather than an untested corner.

**Measured cost of the `f32` translation, filed per-scale beside its cause (hard
rule 10 (a)):**

| recording `scale` | letter-page translation carried in the op's CTM | error in device pixels |
|---:|---:|---:|
| `5 000` | `~4 × 10⁶` | **half a device pixel** |
| `500 000` | `~4 × 10⁸` | **47 px** |

⇒ **after `74.7`, a page replayed from a list and the same page rendered fresh
were the same picture at ordinary scales and different pictures at deep zoom**,
with nothing on either path saying so. That is `R211`'s condition — *two code
paths that owe each other byte-identical output* — and `decision 081`'s subject,
one level down: `081` gave the two paths **one `f64` entry point for region
GEOMETRY**; nothing had been said about **content**.

---

#### ★★★★★ THE FIX — A REFUSAL, AND THE THRESHOLD IS A **SHARED PREDICATE** RATHER THAN A CHOSEN LIMIT

**`PoisonReason::ScaleBeyondF32`.** `record_page` returns
`RenderError::PageNotRecordable`, and the caller falls back to a direct render
that is correct at any scale — **the same fallback `pdfce-cli` already performs
for the seven capability refusals** (`sh`, shading patterns, overprint composites,
soft masks and the rest). No new caller shape, no new failure mode for a consumer
to learn.

**The module's own documentation had already argued for exactly this**, before
the defect existed:

> *"a display list that is subtly wrong is strictly worse than no display list.
> Refusing is loud, cheap, and correct."*

**★★ THE CONSTRUCTION THAT MAKES IT A BOUNDARY RATHER THAN A COMPROMISE, AND IT
IS THE PART TO CARRY FORWARD.** The threshold is **`Mat64::needs_precise_paths`
— the SAME predicate the interpreter consults to decide whether it needs its
`f64` route.** Consequently:

- **Below the predicate**, both paths do **identical `f32` arithmetic** and agree
  exactly — the recording is admissible because the thing it would have to match
  is itself `f32`.
- **Above the predicate**, one path switches to `f64` and the other **refuses**.

⇒ **There is no scale at which they quietly disagree.** That is the property
`R211` asks of a second rendering path, and it is obtained **by construction
rather than by testing**.

**★ Why a shared predicate beats two limits that happen to match.** Two
independently-chosen constants can agree today and drift apart in either
direction on any later edit, and **the band between them is a region where one
path is precise, the other is not, and both believe they are in agreement**.
Nothing reports that band; it has no error message and no counter. A shared
predicate makes the band **not exist** — it cannot open, because there is one
number and one place it is decided. **The next person adding a third rendering
path should reach for this**: *two paths that must agree share the predicate that
decides when they CAN, rather than each picking a limit.* Escalated to
`D:/dev/rag/rust/` (file named in the RAG list below) and minted as **decision
084**.

**★ The test asserts BOTH halves — refused by name at `5 000`, and still records
at `4.0`** — *because a guard that refuses everything is not a guard*, and the
engineer **verified it bites by disabling the condition**. That is `R162`'s
obligation (establish the positive case over the same container) met on a refusal
rather than on an absence.

---

#### ★★★★ THE ORACLE THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, AND THE RULE JUDGEMENT THE DISPATCH ASKED FOR

**`crates/pdfce-render/tests/region_matches_full_page.rs` is the differential
oracle for exactly this contract** — it is the artefact `R211` was minted on the
strength of. **It runs at scales up to `220`. The divergence begins near `530`.**
So it agreed everywhere it was asked, and everywhere it was asked it was right.

**The engineer asked whether this earns a rule or an `R215` amendment, and
recorded honest uncertainty about whether it is one mechanism or two.** It is
**two**, and the ruling is **neither of those**: it is an **amendment to `R211`**.

**Why it is NOT `R215`.** `R215` binds the **target** a test is written against,
and its mechanism is a **wrong expected value** produced by attribution — *the
oracle demands a number that a correct fix cannot produce*. Its failure mode is a
**false alarm on a correct fix**. Here every expected value is **right**; the
failure mode is the opposite — **a silent pass over a broken system** — and it is
produced by the **sampled domain**, not by the expectations. `R215`'s own scope
paragraph already refuses this: *"it does not bind on tests themselves."*

**Why it is not a new number either, which is the closer call.** The condition
that makes the sampling gap dangerous is **`R211`'s condition, verbatim** — two
code paths that owe each other byte-identical output. And `R211` already **names
`replay_region`** as one of the two call sites whose *"these cannot disagree"*
comment went false when a caller moved. **This is not a new surface for `R211`;
it is the surface `R211` was minted on, and did not finish.** Specifically,
**clause (c) under-delivered**: it obliges a *"cannot disagree"* comment to
**name the test that would go red**. Here the test was named, it existed, it ran,
it was green — **and it was silent**, because naming a test says nothing about
the domain the test samples. **A rule whose remedy can be satisfied while the
defect ships is an incomplete rule**, and the completion belongs in the rule, not
beside it.

**Minting `R216` would also split one mechanism across two numbers** — a reader
holding `R211` would have discharged it by naming a test, and a reader holding
`R216` would have no reason to consult `R211`'s asymmetric-narrowing analysis to
know **where** to sample. **They are the same obligation**: the narrowing
boundary is what must be sampled across.

⇒ **`R211` AMENDED with clauses (d) and (e). Ceiling UNMOVED — `R215` stands,
next free `R216`.** Full text under *Standing rules*; in one line: **(d)** where
one path *cannot* meet the contract past some magnitude, **both consult the SAME
predicate** to decide where, and the losing path **refuses** rather than
approximating; **(e)** the differential test that guards the contract **samples
on both sides of that predicate** — *it proves agreement only over the range it
samples, and a range is a claim.*

**★ The honest cost of amending rather than minting, recorded so it is a ruling
and not an oversight.** The (e) half **generalises past precision** — any
parameterised differential test (page sizes, colour spaces, font sizes, core
counts) proves agreement only over its sampled domain, and binding it inside
`R211` hides it from someone writing a non-precision differential test.
**Mitigated the way `R211` mitigated its own declined sibling**: the general form
is filed as a fact in `D:/dev/rag/rust/`, where the test-methodology findings
already live, rather than as a rule nobody's condition matches. **★★ And
`Pass 122.0` is where it will bite next** — *"byte-identical output at any core
count"* is a differential contract over a parameter, and *"any"* is the word this
finding is about.

**The 232nd filing flagged `93 s` as a figure it could not disambiguate, filed
both ratios beside their pairs, and reported it as owing one sentence.** The
engineer supplied it. **Stated once, here, so the number has a home:**

| figure | what it is | zoom |
|---:|---|---:|
| **`31 s`** | the same CAD region with **algorithm B disabled entirely** — i.e. the **baseline** | `100 000×` |
| **`93 s`** | the **REJECTED device-space attempt** | `100 000×` |
| **`1.3 s`** | **shipped** | `100 000×` |

⇒ **`31 s → 1.3 s` = `23.8×` is the speed-up**, and it is the figure the 232nd
filing headlined. **`93 s` against `31 s` = `3×` is the rejected attempt's
penalty**, and it is the figure that justified deleting the device-space
scaffolding.

**★★ AND THE PART THAT IS A CORRECTION RATHER THAN A COMPLETION.** The `PASS
74.7` entry below also filed **`93 s → 1.3 s` = `71.5×`** as a second speed-up
*"at `100 000×` zoom"*. **With the provenance known, that ratio compares the
shipped result against a REJECTED IMPLEMENTATION, not against a baseline** — it
is not a speed-up of the feature at all, and reads as one. **A dated amendment is
appended to that entry**; the entry itself is append-only and the original
sentence stays, per hard rule 1. **The `23.8×` headline is unaffected**, exactly
as the 232nd filing predicted — but *"unaffected either way"* was true of the
headline and **not** of the second ratio, and that distinction is the reason the
figure was worth chasing.

**★ This is hard rule 10 working in the shape it was written for.** The ambiguity
was survivable for one filing precisely because **both ratios were filed beside
their operands** — `93 s → 1.3 s = 71.5×` and `31 s → 1.3 s = 23.8×` — so the
correction required **no new measurement, only the referent**. Had either been
filed as a bare *"`71.5×` faster"*, nothing in the record could have been
repaired without re-running a `93`-second render.

#### `FEATURES.md` — ROW 202 IS **DECIDED**, WHICH IS THE THING THE LAST FILING COULD NOT DO

**The 232nd filing left row 202 alone and said so out loud**, on the ground that
it could not tell whether replay carried the content-side precision and that a
claim in either direction would be a guess. **The answer is in**, and it is
recorded as a ruling rather than only as an edit:

- **Replay does NOT carry the content-side precision.** Recorded ops hold `f32`
  transforms; `replay_region` post-translates in `f32`. **Row 202's existing
  sentence about the `f64` entry point stays, unchanged and still correct** — it
  is a claim about **region geometry** (`decision 081`), and this finding is
  about **content**. Two different quantities, which is `R213`'s whole subject,
  and the row now names both.
- **The row gains the precision refusal.** Its refusal list previously named only
  the **seven capability refusals** (`sh`, shading patterns, overprint
  composites, soft masks …) with their measured `77 of 3,222` fallback rate.
  **`ScaleBeyondF32` is a different KIND of refusal** — not *"this page contains
  an operator I cannot record"* but *"this SCALE is one I cannot record
  truthfully"* — and a reader scanning for *"when do I not get a list?"* must
  find both. **The `77 of 3,222` figure is left untouched and its scope named**,
  because it measures capability refusals over a corpus at ordinary scale and is
  **not** a measurement of the new refusal's frequency.
- **No box changes.** `[x] core · [x] cli · [ ] gui`. The refusal ships in
  `pdfce-render` and is reached by `pdfce-cli`'s existing fallback; **no GUI code
  path calls the display list at all**, which was already the row's stated
  position and is not rounded up.
- **No new row.** `74.10` adds no capability an operator can *ask for* — it
  removes a way to get a wrong picture. That is the same test that gave
  `Pass 74.8` no row and gave `--fast-subpixel` one: **`--fast-subpixel` is
  something an operator types; this is not.**

#### `PASS 74.7`, FIRST ALGORITHM (`1d6db9e`) — `Mat64`: the CTM carried in `f64` and narrowed only at the leaf

**Three sites had to change together and each was load-bearing alone**: `cm`
concatenation, a Form XObject's `/Matrix`, and — the one that took longest to
find — **the BASE transform**, which `RegionGeometry` was handing over **already
narrowed**. **Widening an `f32` back to `f64` carries its rounding forward**, so
the fix is to keep the `f64` coefficients rather than to widen the `f32` ones.
That sentence is the transferable half and it is the same trick `Pass 74.2` used
one level up.

**Why the symptom was never distortion.** A translation error moves *every*
point of a form equally, so the drawing stayed correctly shaped and correctly
proportioned and sat **hundreds of pixels away, or off the canvas entirely**.
Nothing looked broken; things were simply absent.

**Measured — forms rendered of the `11` in view, 1600 px framed on the banana's
water molecule:**

| `scale` | before | after | correct answer | why |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `2 × 10⁶` | 11 of 11 | **11 of 11** | 11 | all eleven still in frame |
| `1.25 × 10⁷` | 7 of 11 | **2 of 11** | **2** | the box plus the one molecule in frame; the other nine leave the viewport and `Pass 74.4` culls them **exactly** |
| `2.5 × 10⁷` | 3 of 11 | **2 of 11** | **2** | as above |
| `5 × 10⁷` | 1 of 11 | **2 of 11** | **2** | as above |
| `1.6 × 10⁹` | — | **2 of 11** | **2** | a single water molecule renders sharply at **≈ 190 billion percent**; before, everything above `≈ 5 × 10⁶` vanished |

**★★ ORDINARY RENDERING IS UNAFFECTED, WHICH WAS THE OPERATOR'S OWN
CONSTRAINT.** The `f64` composition happens **once per `cm`, not once per
pixel**: banana whole page **1430 / 1458 ms against 1487 / 1532 ms before** —
two runs each, i.e. noise, and the *after* pair is the faster of the two.

#### ★★★★★ `R215`'s INSTANCE — THE ACCEPTANCE ORACLE THIS FILE FILED IN ADVANCE DEMANDED THE WRONG ANSWER

**The Backlog entry for `Pass 74.7`, written by the 230th filing, carried a
column headed *"required after `74.7`"* reading `11 of 11` at every one of the
five scales.** The correct post-fix answer is **`2`** at every scale from
`1.25 × 10⁷` up. **A fix that satisfied the filed oracle would have been a
BUG** — it would have meant nine forms outside the viewport were being painted.

**How the oracle got it wrong, which is the reusable part.** The engineer
measured `11 → 7 → 3 → 1` across rising zoom and read it as **one curve produced
by one defect**. It is **two curves superimposed**:

- the **precision** defect, losing forms to a quantised translation — the thing
  being hunted; and
- **`Pass 74.4`'s `/BBox` viewport cull**, losing forms because they genuinely
  left the frame — **exact, correct, and shipped by this same project five
  commits earlier**.

The oracle attributed **all** of the decline to the first, and therefore
predicted the *un-culled* count as the requirement. **Its own healthy row —
`11 of 11` at `2 × 10⁶` — was extrapolated to every other row**, which is the
mechanism: *the healthy end of a curve read as the target for the whole curve.*

**★★ AND THE PART THAT MADE IT AUTHORITATIVE.** The 230th filing headed that
table ***"ACCEPTANCE BASELINE — ALREADY MEASURED, WHICH IS RARE ENOUGH TO
NAME"*** and wrote *"this Pass has a pass/fail oracle **before a line is
written**"*. **The praise is what made it hard to question.** An oracle
introduced as unusually rigorous is one a later reader has less reason to check,
not more — and this one was **measured**, which is exactly the property that
made its wrongness invisible: every number in it was correct as an observation,
and the *column heading* was the claim.

⇒ **`R215` MINTED.** Full text under *Standing rules*. In one line: **an
acceptance oracle states the EXPECTED value and the MECHANISM that produces it,
per row; where two mechanisms move the same number, it decomposes them or says
it cannot.** A row that says `11 of 11` and cannot say *why 11* is a
transcription, not a prediction.

**Recorded honestly: no harm resulted**, because the engineer measured the
delivered behaviour and reasoned about what `2` meant instead of matching the
table. **That is care, not machinery**, and the rule exists because the next
session may match the table.

#### `PASS 74.7`, SECOND ALGORITHM (`5b0d885`) — differencing, and the result that was not the goal

**`Mat64` cannot fix a path whose OWN coordinates are large page numbers.** An
`f32` near `x = 90 pt` has a spacing of `7.6 × 10⁻⁶ pt`, so **a rectangle
`8 × 10⁻⁶ pt` wide is one representable step** and is destroyed when the
operands are narrowed. **No precision in the CTM recovers it** — the information
is gone before any matrix applies. This is limit **1** of the three, which the
Backlog entry had recorded as out of scope.

**The fix.** When the magnitude gate `needs_precise_paths` fires, the
interpreter builds the path **relative to its own first point**, differencing in
`f64`, so what reaches `tiny_skia` is a set of **small offsets** instead of
nearly-equal large numbers. The CTM alongside keeps its linear part and carries
the origin's mapped position. **Gated on magnitude alone, decided once per
path**, so ordinary rendering never enters it: **CAD at scale 1.0 is `1086 ms`
against a `980–1040 ms` baseline; banana page `1442 ms` against `1430–1538 ms`.**

##### ★★★ THE REJECTED FIRST ATTEMPT IS THE MORE USEFUL RECORD

**Building the path in DEVICE space with an identity transform was CORRECT, and
`3×` SLOWER at extreme zoom** — **`93 s` against `31 s`** on a stroke-heavy CAD
sheet.

**The cause is a rasteriser fact, not a PDF one: `tiny_skia` flattens curves to
a tolerance expressed in the PATH'S OWN UNITS.** A path whose coordinates are
millions gets subdivided accordingly, so moving coordinates into device space
buys precision and pays for it in segment count. **This is the finding most
likely to be re-derived by a future session** and it is escalated to
`D:/dev/rag/rust/` for that reason.

**It also forced a similarity restriction**, since an identity transform cannot
scale a pen — which meant a `similarity_scale` helper, a stroke-width multiplier
and a dash rebuild. **Differencing removed all four at once**: coordinates stay
at user-space magnitude so flattening is unchanged, the linear part still
reaches `tiny_skia` so strokes and dashes need no adjustment, and **any affine
CTM is admissible** rather than only a similarity. **The helper and the stroke
plumbing were DELETED rather than left as archaeology**, which is worth naming —
a rejected approach that leaves its scaffolding behind is read by the next
reader as a live constraint.

##### ★★★★ THE FINDING WORTH ESCALATING, AND IT WAS NOT THE GOAL OF THE WORK

**The same CAD region went `31 s → 1.3 s`.** Divided: **`23.8×`**. And at
`100 000×` zoom, **`93 s → 1.3 s` = `71.5×`**. The engineer's headline figure is
the conservative one, **`23×`**.

> **★★ AMENDED 2026-08-23 (233rd filing): the `71.5×` in the sentence above is
> NOT a second speed-up.** The engineer supplied `93 s`'s provenance — it is the
> **rejected device-space attempt** at `100 000×`, not a baseline; the baseline
> at that zoom is **`31 s`** (the same region with algorithm B disabled
> entirely). ⇒ **`31 s → 1.3 s` = `23.8×` is the speed-up**, at both zooms;
> **`93 s` against `31 s` = `3×` is the rejected attempt's penalty.** Nothing
> above is deleted, per hard rule 1. Full table in `PASS 74.10`'s Shipped entry.

**Deep zoom was never slow BECAUSE it was imprecise — it was slow FOR THE SAME
REASON**: large magnitudes reaching a rasteriser that reasons in **relative**
tolerances. **Fixing where the numbers are large fixed both.**

⇒ **The generalisable shape: a precision defect and a performance defect with a
single cause will look unrelated until one of them is fixed — and the
performance one is the half nobody attributes correctly**, because *"deep zoom
is slow"* sounds like an inherent cost of deep zoom. Nobody opens a ticket
against physics. Escalated to `D:/dev/rag/rust/`.

**★ A FIGURE THIS FILING COULD NOT DISAMBIGUATE, FLAGGED RATHER THAN GUESSED
(hard rule 10's corollary — a correction is a claim).** `93 s` appears **twice**
in `5b0d885`'s message with two possible referents: once as **the rejected
device-space attempt's time** (*"three times slower … 93 s against 31 s"*) and
once as **a before-figure at `100 000×`** (*"at 100 000×, 93 s → 1.3 s"*). Those

**Verified in both directions**, per the commit: the three-ways synthetic now

**including the one drawn in absolute coordinates that neither fix reached

#### `PASS 74.9` (`296a23e`) — `--fast-subpixel`, the opt-in lossy cull

**`--fast-subpixel` on the CLI, `RenderOptions::subpixel_culling` in the
library, OFF by default.** A Form XObject whose transformed `/BBox` is under
**half a device pixel in BOTH axes** is not executed.

**Both axes, not either** — so a **hairline** (thin but long) still paints. That
is the difference between a fidelity trade and a bug.

**Tested after the exact `/BBox` cull and counted on a SEPARATE key**, because
**merging them would let a fidelity trade hide inside a correctness
optimisation**: `forms_culled` changes no pixel, `subpixel_culled` does. This is
the mechanism `decision 083` records.

**MEASURED — whole page, `gen-scale-demo` banana:**

**`1 468 ms → 108 ms` = `13.6×`, with ZERO of `1 242 640` pixels different
(`0.0 %`)** — at that zoom each dropped object is `1/70` of a pixel and
contributes nothing a raster can hold.

**And the measurement that keeps that honest, because "zero" would otherwise
read as "free".** The loss appears as objects **approach** the threshold rather
than sitting far below it. **Same page, a 1 pt window, ≈ `339 of 342` forms
dropped each time:**

| `scale` (× ; 1 pt window, ≈ 339 of 342 forms dropped each row) | pixels differing, of the window | share of window | worst channel delta, of 255 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `20` | 18 of 400 | **4.5 %** | 16 (**6.3 %**) |
| `35` | 47 of 1 296 | **3.6 %** | 54 (**21 %**) |
| `60` | 82 of 3 600 | **2.3 %** | **62** (**24 %** — a quarter of a channel) |
| whole page, page-fit | **0 of 1 242 640** | **0.0 %** | 0 |

⇒ **It is genuinely lossy; the loss is largest exactly where the speed-up is
smallest; and where the speed-up is enormous the loss happens to be nil.** That
shape — **the error and the benefit anti-correlated across the parameter that
triggers both** — **is why it is a switch and not a heuristic pdfce applies on
its own judgement.** A heuristic would have to pick a threshold, and every
threshold sits somewhere on that curve.

**`decision 082` is SATISFIED, NOT OVERRIDDEN.** 082 says a lossy speed-up is
the operator's call. The operator called it. **Rule 4 is honoured in both
positions**: `subpixel_culled` prints **whether or not the flag is set**, so a
raster always carries the count of what it left out and an operator comparing
two renders can see which one paid for its speed.

#### DECISION 083 MINTED — the SHAPE a lossy render option takes

Full text in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12. In one line: **a lossy render option is
carried in `RenderOptions`, defaults OFF, and gets its OWN metrics key; an exact
skip and a lossy skip never share a counter.**

**Why this is not already `082`, since that is the obvious objection.** `082`
answers **who decides** — *a render may skip work only where skipping is exact;
a lossy speed-up is the operator's call.* It says **nothing about what the
answer looks like once the operator says yes**, and the two available shapes
were genuinely different: a flag, or a merged counter with a threshold. **The
merge was available and was refused with a reason**, which is a choice, which is
what a decision record is for. `082` is *whose call*; `083` is *what the call
produces*. Cross-referenced in both directions, deliberately not merged — the
same disposition `R213`/`R214` got one filing ago.

**Body-section updates:** §4.1 gains sync entry **(AB)**; §4's *Numerical reach
of PAGE-SPACE CONTENT* paragraph gains its dated discharge; §(H)'s key count
moves `89 → 90`.

**The dispatch proposed:** *a regression test is not a regression test until you
have watched it fail* — offered on four instances in this batch, each of which
failed differently at first and each caught by a **deliberate sabotage run**
(restoring from file copies rather than `git checkout`):

| # | the test | why it could not fail | the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the `Mat64` unit test | its first fixture used **round numbers**, and `f32` gets the right answer because **two *equal* large numbers cancel perfectly** — a cancellation only loses precision when the operands are large and **merely NEARLY equal** | a fixture whose operands are large and unequal |
| 2 | the `Mat64` integration test | sampled a few points and passed with **HALF the fix removed** — 10 px of error does not flip a sample taken 160 px from an edge | measures **four edges to a 3 px tolerance**; fails on either half alone (**48 px** from the base seed, **112 px** from the `cm` composition) |
| 3 | the sub-ulp test | sampled the **middle row**; the rectangle sits in a **corner** | scans the whole raster |
| 4 | the `--fast-subpixel` test | asserted **a counter moved** | asserts the **two rasters DIFFER** — without which it passes against an implementation that counts the form and paints it anyway |

**MINT DECLINED, and on coverage rather than on count.** Three standing rules
and one RAG file already carry it, and they carry it **as CONDITIONS**, which is
the form this section's own ruling requires (`R164`'s objection 1: *"standing
rules in this section name CONDITIONS, not mechanisms"*):

- **`R87`** — *was the instrument pointed at the thing?* Covers instance **3**
  outright, and instance **1** (the fixture cannot exhibit the defect).
- **`R162`** — *could my assertion ever have come out false?* Covers instances
  **2** and **4**: an assertion whose tolerance or whose quantifier cannot
  reach the defect.
- **`R164`** — *does this verdict depend on anything other than its subject?*
  Covers instance **4**'s deeper form: a counter is the implementation's own
  claim about itself.
- **`D:/dev/rag/rust/prove_test_suite_non_vacuous_by_deliberately_breaking_the_thing_it_tests.md`**
  (2026-08-12) states the prescription **verbatim** and prescriptively —
  *"write the test, confirm it passes, then deliberately mutate the
  implementation … and confirm the existing suite fails"* — with
  `a_sabotage_that_does_not_compile_or_change_behavior_measures_nothing_verify_the_mutation_before_trusting_the_catch.md`
  as its guard.

**★ The decisive ground: the proposal prescribes an ACTION, and every rule in
this section names a CONDITION.** *"Watch it fail"* is a method, and a method
with no condition attached cannot tell you **which** tests need it — so it reads
as *sabotage everything*, which is work rather than care, the same ground on
which three mints were declined this week. `R87`/`R162`/`R164` each name the
condition under which the method is owed. **Adding a fourth rule that says "do
it always" would weaken them**, because a reader with a blanket rule stops
asking which condition applies.

**★★ What IS new here is a fact, not a rule, and it is escalated as one.**
Instance **1** — *two EQUAL large `f32` values cancel perfectly, so a
round-numbers fixture makes a float-precision test vacuous; the defect needs
operands that are large and merely NEARLY equal* — is a crisp, checkable,
transferable arithmetic fact that no rule in this section states. **It goes to
`D:/dev/rag/rust/` as its own file.** Recording it as a rule would have buried
an arithmetic fact inside a methodology prescription.

**★ `R215` was minted instead, on a different candidate the dispatch did not
propose** — the acceptance-oracle finding above. It is a **condition**
(*two mechanisms move one number and the oracle names one*), it is **new**
(nothing in `R87`/`R162`/`R164`/`R210`–`R214` reaches it — those govern
**tests**; this governs the **oracle a test is written against**, which is
written **before** the test and by a different person), and its instance is
**this role's own filed artefact**, which is the strongest warrant available: a
rule whose founding defect the rule-writer committed is one nobody can claim was
minted defensively.

#### ★★★★★ `PASS 74.8` — THE DISCLOSURE GAP, AND WHY IT WAS A RULE-4 DEFECT RATHER THAN A MISSING FEATURE

**What was wrong.** `Diagnostics::annotations_out_of_scope` and
`Diagnostics::page_content_suppressed` existed, were incremented, were merged
across pages, were documented in rustdoc **and were covered by unit tests in
`pdfce-render`** — and appeared in **no** `pdfce-cli` output at all: not on the
stable metrics line, not on stderr. So the operator running
`render-page --no-annotations` saw:

```
annots=1 annots_painted=0
```

and **that line is identical to the line a file with one broken annotation
produces.** *"I withheld it because you asked"* and *"I tried and could not
paint it"* want **opposite** reactions from the operator — one is the flag
working, one is a bug report — **and separating them is the entire reason the
two counters are split in the first place.**

**Why rule 4 and not tidiness.** Project rule 4 binds hardest on *"inferences
the operator cannot see by definition"*, and **content that was deliberately not
drawn is the limiting case**: there is no artefact on the page to notice, no
glyph to squint at, no outline to hover. In the CLI *"the invocation IS the
commit"* (rule 11 / `ARCHITECTURE.md` §7), so the CLI **prints** or it is
silent, and silence is the one thing the rule forbids. ⇒ **A counter that
exists, is merged, is documented and is never emitted is worse than one that
was never written: it makes the gap look measured.** The rustdoc says the
number is available; nothing downstream says it is unreachable.

**What shipped.** Both keys print, **inserted beside the annotation family
rather than appended at the tail** — which matters because the metrics line's
published contract promises **name**-stability, not ordinal stability
(`f9dc007`, `R212`), so grouping by meaning is free and grouping by
chronology is not. Regression test
**`no_annotations_says_how_many_it_withheld`** asserts the withheld annotation
**stays in the census AND is attributed** — i.e. it pins the conjunction, not
either half, which is the assertion that would have caught the original defect.

**Measured, on `fixtures/synthetic/annot/ap-resources-own-font.pdf`** (the
engineer's figures, marked as his):

| invocation | census | painted | withheld |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | `annots=1` | `annots_painted=1` | `annots_out_of_scope=0` |
| `--no-annotations` | `annots=1` | `annots_painted=0` | **`annots_out_of_scope=1`** |

**The census does not move.** That is the property worth naming: the file's
annotation count is a fact about the file and must not change because a flag
changed, so the withheld count is an **additional** number rather than a
subtraction from an existing one. A shell that subtracted instead would have
made `--no-annotations` report a *different document*.

**★ One key spelling is recorded and one is deliberately NOT.**
`annots_out_of_scope=<n>` is quoted above because it appears in the engineer's
measured output. **The metrics-line spelling of `page_content_suppressed`'s key
is not printed anywhere in this entry, because this role did not open
`crates/`** (docs-only filing, `d4721d8`) and the gate reports a *count*, not
a key list. Field name: `Diagnostics::page_content_suppressed`. **Naming the
edge of the evidence rather than guessing the string** — hard rule 8's
discipline pointed at a two-word claim.

#### ★★★ THE GATE'S FIRST LIVE CATCH — WHICH IS DISTINCT EVIDENCE FROM ITS FOUNDING CASE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT

`tools/check-metrics-line-contract.py` was built by `ea413a4` (230th filing) to
close a **known** gap: 28 template keys missing, 43 table rows missing, all of
it debt that already existed when the gate was written. **A gate built against
known debt and then run against that debt has demonstrated exactly one thing —
that it can see what its author was looking at.**

**`PASS 74.8` is the first change it acted on that it was not built for**, and
it forced **all three copies** of the contract — the doc template, the per-key
explanation table, and the test's key list — on an ordinary two-key addition.
**87 → 89 keys**, measured by running it:

```
metrics-line-contract: OK — 89 keys; the template matches the println and every key has a table row.
```

**★ Why this is worth a record rather than a shrug.** `R212`'s whole mechanism
is that *the test forces its copy and nothing forces the other*. A gate that
has only ever run against its founding debt is **indistinguishable from a gate
that hard-codes that debt's shape** — both are green afterwards, and neither
has been asked a question it did not already know the answer to. **The first
unrelated change is the first evidence the gate generalises**, and it is cheap
to record and impossible to reconstruct later. Cross-reference
`ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md` (this project's own finding): that
one says a gate red at baseline enforces nothing; **this one says a gate that
has only ever been green at baseline has not yet been shown to enforce
anything either.** The two are the same axis, at opposite ends. Escalated:

#### ★★★★ STANDING RULE `R214` — MINTED, AND THE ENGINEER'S OWN READING IS CONFIRMED

Full text under *Standing rules*. **Ceiling moves `R213` → `R214`; next free
`R215`.**

**The dispatch asked for a ruling and offered three options — a rule, an
amendment to `R212`, or a decline — and volunteered that it might be splitting
too finely.** It is not. **Minted, and here is the warrant, argued rather than
asserted.**

**What happened.** `transparency_groups_special`'s doc opened **"Of those"** — a
back-reference to whichever field happened to be declared before it. The 230th
filing reported it as a **broken** back-reference: a later field
(`soft_masks_on_group_result`) had been declared in between, so the antecedent
had moved. **That report was true and it was half the defect.** Checking the
increment site (`is_transparency_group && (knockout || isolated)`, **no
flattening condition**) showed **the original antecedent was wrong too** — the
counter was **never** a subset of the flattened count. **The first repair
restored the "obvious" neighbour and had to be corrected by reading the code.**

**⇒ The generalisable half, in one sentence:** **a doc that cites a NEIGHBOUR
rather than a NAME gives no way to tell a broken reference from a wrong one —
and repairing the reference without checking the referent silently converts the
second into the first**, producing a sentence that is *newly* wrong, *looks*
repaired, and now has a plausible antecedent to protect it from the next reader.

**Why it is NOT `R212`, which is the ruling the dispatch specifically asked
for.** `R212` requires **two written copies of one contract, one of them
asserted by a test**, and its remedy is to name the authoritative copy or gate
the other. **"Of those" has no second copy and no test asserts anything about
it.** Its defect is a pointer with **no target written down anywhere** — the
opposite failure from duplication, which has the target written down *twice*.
Amending `R212` to reach it would also break its own scope paragraph (*"does
not bind on ordinary duplicated prose"*) one filing after that paragraph was
written. **The engineer's reading is confirmed: distinct mechanism, distinct
remedy.**

**Why it is not `R213` either, which is the closer call and the reason a future
session will try to fold them.** The resemblance is real — both are *the subject
went unstated and the reader supplied it from context, and nothing disagrees*.
But `R213`'s scope binds it to **bounds and magnitudes**, stated explicitly one
filing ago precisely so it would not be over-read; and `R213`'s remedy — *name
the quantity in the label* — has **nothing to say about the repair**, which is
where this defect does its real damage. **`R213` prevents; `R214` prevents AND
governs the fix.** Recorded as neighbours with a cross-reference in both
directions rather than merged.

**Why it clears `R210`'s minting test, and clears it more cleanly than `R213`
did.** The question *"does this doc comment resolve its referent by NAME?"* is
answerable from **one span of one file**, with **no knowledge of current
behaviour** — the same standard that minted `R211` and `R212` and that the 228th
filing's declined sibling failed. Note the split, because it is `R212`'s
enforcement-layer clause exactly: **whether the reference is RIGHT is
undecidable** (it requires reading the increment site, which is behaviour);
**whether it is NAMED is a grep over a closed vocabulary** — *of those*, *the
above*, *the former*, *the latter*, *this slice*, *the next slice*, *as above*,
*see below*, *the previous field*. ⇒ **A gate is available and is recommended,
not built here** (`tools/` is outside this role's remit). **Sequencing, per
`ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`: the baseline is UNMEASURED from
this side** — this filing did not open `crates/` — **so measure the baseline
first, repair, then wire. Do not wire it red.**

**Occurrence warrant, stated honestly rather than inflated.** **n = 1 for the
doubly-wrong form** (`transparency_groups_special`), **n = 4 in this commit
alone for the pointing-without-naming mechanism** (items 2, 3, 4 and 8 of the
table above), with a named prior cousin already on disk in this project's
record: `Pass 74.0`'s `MAX_PIXMAP_EDGE` doc comment, justified by *"beyond any
plausible viewing zoom"* — a pointer at a predicted future rather than a named
fact. **The mint rests on the decidability warrant and on the demonstrated
repair hazard, not on the count**, which is the standard this project set when
it declined three mints *"on a better warrant than an occurrence count"*.

**★ And the repair-hazard half is NOT new — it is two existing corollaries
meeting a new surface, which is why `R214` cites them instead of restating
them.** Hard rule 10's corollary: **a correction is a claim**, and it must name
its world-source *in the correction itself*. Hard rule 11's corollary: **check a
draft claim of your own against live source before publishing it** — earned when
a draft asserting a survivor at `main.rs:7057` was wrong and checking it turned
up the real one at `main.rs:7027`. **Both fired here, on the engineer's side,
and both were paid before the commit rather than after it.** What `R214` adds
that neither says: *with a positional reference you cannot even tell which kind
of correction you are making*, so the check is not optional diligence — it is
the only thing that distinguishes a repair from a new defect.

#### `FEATURES.md` — NO NEW ROW, ROW 161 REPAIRED, AND THE `gui` BOX IS NOT ROUNDED UP

**The dispatch's reading is confirmed and the ruling is stated out loud**,
because *"did not open the file"* and *"opened it and judged"* are different
facts a silent absence cannot tell apart.

- **No new row.** `PASS 74.8` did not add a capability to the project; it made
  an existing one **honest**. pdfce could already narrow annotation scope, and
  could already count what it withheld — **what it could not do was say so.**
  A disclosure is part of the capability it discloses, not a capability of its
  own, and giving it a row would imply pdfce has *two* annotation-scope
  features. Precedent followed, not re-argued: `ea413a4` got no row on the
  same reasoning (*"a gate is not a capability"*).
- **Row 161 repaired — the sentence REPLACED, never appended to**, per the
  file's own header rule. It said *"Gap, disclosed: what is WITHHELD is not
  counted anywhere a shell can see it"*; it now says the withheld count is
  reported on `render-page`'s metrics line beside the census, and that the
  census **does not move** when the flag does.
- **★ BOXES: `core [x] · cli [x] · gui [x] · Acrobat [x]` — UNCHANGED, and the
  `gui` box is NOT a claim about the new counters.** The dispatch asked for this
  explicitly and it is the right call. The row's headline capability —
  *render and count annotations* — **is** reachable in a real `pdfceGUI` build,
  which is what ticks the box under this file's stated bar. **The counters are
  not**: they are computed in `pdfce-render` and read only by `pdfce-cli`. So
  the qualification goes **in the sentence**, where rows 202/203/207/216
  already put it (*"no GUI code path reads the counter"*), rather than by
  unticking a box that is true of the row's subject. **Unticking `gui` would
  have been the other error** — it would report a working GUI capability as
  missing, which is precisely the `[ ]`-versus-`—` confusion this file's legend
  exists to prevent, in its third form.

**No new row; one row now says what a narrowed scope reports and who can read
it.**

#### ★★★★★ THE FINDING — A CEILING FILED AGAINST THE WRONG QUANTITY

**This is the entry's headline and it is not the molecule box.** The box is
what made the difference *measurable*; the finding outlives it.

**What was claimed.** `PASS 74.1`/`74.2` (`bd9844d`, `71f7055`, 226th filing)
established that *"deep zoom holds its viewport to a trillion percent"*. **That
sentence is TRUE and it has always been true.** It is a claim about
`render_page_region`'s returned pixmap: a requested 800 × 600 viewport comes
back 800 × 600 out to `1 × 10¹² %`.

**What it was read as.** The ceiling of pdfce's deep zoom. Nothing in
`ROADMAP.md`, `SESSION_LOG.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` or `FEATURES.md`
distinguished *the viewport* from *the geometry drawn inside it*, and there was
no reason for anyone to look for the distinction, **because there was no
disagreement anywhere to notice.** Two different quantities, one number, and
the number was correct for the one it was measured on.

**The three `f32` limits under the CONTENT** — the engineer's, measured this
session:

| # | limit | the number | consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **path coordinates** | an `f32` near `x = 540` has a spacing of **`6.1 × 10⁻⁵ pt` = 21.5 µm** | any feature smaller than that, **written as an absolute page coordinate**, is quantised away before the renderer ever sees it |
| **2** | **the placement matrix** | concatenating a `cm` that carries a page coordinate leaves the CTM's translation as the **difference of two large nearly-equal `f32` values**; drift ≈ **`page_x × scale / 16 700 000` px** | **~5 px** at the mitochondrion tier, **~400 px** at the box tier, **past the viewport entirely above `scale = 5 × 10⁶`** |
| **3** | **consequently, device position is QUANTISED** | **~500 px steps at `scale = 8.1 × 10⁶`** | the content cannot be moved by less than one step, whatever the caller asks for |

**Checked by this role rather than relayed** (hard rule 10 — a figure filed in a
form that can disagree): limit 1's constant is the `f32` ulp at 540. `540 ∈
[2⁹, 2¹⁰)`, so `ulp = 2⁹ × 2⁻²³ = 6.104 × 10⁻⁵ pt`; at `25 400 / 72` µm per
point that is **21.53 µm**. ✔ Limit 3 likewise: `540 × 8.1 × 10⁶ = 4.374 × 10⁹
∈ [2³², 2³³)`, so `ulp = 2³² × 2⁻²³ = 512 px`. ✔ **Both derive from the
magnitude of the page coordinate, not from any pdfce code**, which is why this
went to `C:/personal_rag/pdf/` as a PDF-domain fact rather than staying here.

**The measurement, the engineer's** — 1600 px framed on the water molecule, on
the box's own eleven forms:

| `scale` | forms rendered | of |
|---|---|---|
| `2 × 10⁶` | **11** | 11 |
| `5 × 10⁶` | **11** | 11 |
| `1.25 × 10⁷` | **7** | 11 |
| `2.5 × 10⁷` | **3** | 11 |
| `5 × 10⁷` | **1** (the box alone) | 11 |

**Two independent confirmations, and the second is the stronger one.**

1. **Deliberate.** A synthetic page drew the same square three ways — absolute
   coordinates, a `cm` translation, a scaled `cm` — and **all three were lost at
   the same magnification, including the one that uses neither `cm` nor a
   form.** That rules out the Form XObject path and rules out `PASS 74.4`'s
   viewport cull, which were the two obvious suspects and the two the project
   had most recently touched.
2. **★★★ Accidental, and it is the better evidence because nobody was testing
   for it.** The box renders off-centre, so the obvious move is to nudge
   `--region`. **Two successive nudges gave byte-identical framing.**
   `--region` is `f64` and stays `f64` through `region_base_geometry_of`
   (that is `PASS 74.2` + decision 081 working exactly as designed), **so the
   viewport moved and the content did not** — a 76-pixel correction is below the
   `f32` ulp of the `540 × scale` term it is added to. **The saved render is
   left off-centre on purpose: that framing is the evidence**, and
   `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md` carries the command to reproduce it.

**★ Why the accidental confirmation matters beyond this bug.** The deliberate
test was designed by someone who already believed the hypothesis. The nudge was
someone trying to make a picture look right and being told *no* by the bytes.
**An instrument built to test a hypothesis shares the hypothesis's blind
spots** — which is `R210`'s mechanism arriving from the opposite direction, and
worth noticing that it arrived twice in one week.

#### ★★★★ STANDING RULE `R213` — MINTED, AND THE WARRANT IS n=2 WITH A NAMED FIRST INSTANCE

Full text under *Standing rules*. **Ceiling moves `R212` → `R213`; next free
`R214`.**

> **A MAGNITUDE CLAIM IS A CLAIM ABOUT ONE QUANTITY. NAME THE QUANTITY IN THE
> CLAIM ITSELF — IN THE LABEL, NOT IN THE PROSE BESIDE IT — BECAUSE WHEN IT IS
> MISSING THE READER SUPPLIES THE BROADEST ONE AVAILABLE AND NOTHING
> DISAGREES.**

**Checked against `R210`'s minting test, and the answer needs care**, because
the honest answer to *"is a mechanical oracle available?"* is **no** — and
three of this week's six declines were made on exactly that ground. The mint
survives anyway, on a distinction the project has already drawn once:

- **`R210` itself was minted with no gate**, on an *instrument* warrant.
  **`R213` is the same species** — it is a rule about the SHAPE a figure is
  filed in, not about a property of the code. The gateable-rule test
  (`R211`, `R212`) applies to rules that prescribe **behaviour of the tree**;
  it does not apply to rules that prescribe **how a record is written**, which
  is why hard rule 10 exists in the agent file with an explicit *"no checker
  exists and none is coming — this is deliberate, so do not propose one."*
- **The 228th filing's decline was on a different ground.** *"A cull is worth
  only what it skips"* was declined as **engineering method, not project
  policy.** `R213` is not method: it binds the record, which is precisely what
  standing rules are for.

**n=2, and the first instance is already on disk**, which is what lifts this
above the 227th filing's n=1 decline:

| # | date | the claim | the quantity it was about | the quantity it was read as | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | 2026-08-07 (hard rule 10's founding instance) | `mask.fill_path` at **`5.24 s`** and at **`8.3 µs`** | **5.24 s over 24 128 clips = 217 µs each** vs **8.3 µs page-sized** | one figure for "the cost of `fill_path`" | **26× contradiction carried openly for two filings**, the two figures **217 lines apart in one `index.md`**; ranked a work order and **dispatched a fork on a false premise** for six hours |
| **2** | 2026-08-22 (this filing) | *"deep zoom holds to a trillion percent"* | **the returned viewport** | **pdfce's deep-zoom ceiling**, i.e. page-space geometry too | carried across **four documents and three Pass entries** for one day; surfaced only when an artefact needed **both** quantities at once |

**★ Why these are one mechanism and not two coincidences.** In both, **every
figure was measured correctly, every sentence was true, and no two records
disagreed.** Hard rule 10's remedy — *file a total beside its per-item form* —
catches instance 1 and **cannot catch instance 2**, because a viewport size and
a coordinate precision are not two forms of one number; they are two numbers.
**What they share is that the SUBJECT of the bound went unstated and the reader
supplied it.** That is the rule, and it is why `R213` is a mint rather than an
amendment to hard rule 10: hard rule 10 (b) already says *put the qualifier in
the label*, and `R213` is the reason that clause is not merely stylistic.

**★★ Why it is not an amendment to `R210` either**, which is the disposition
the 227th filing chose in the analogous case. `R210` is about an **instrument
that is silent on what it did not adjudicate** — the failure is inside the
measuring apparatus. Here **nothing measured anything wrongly**; the failure is
entirely in the scope of a sentence. Folding this into `R210` would put a
*claim-shape* rule under an *instrument* rule and make both harder to apply.

#### `PASS 74.6` (`950e3af`) — the molecule box: ten molecules at 1:1 below the cells

**What shipped**, the engineer's account, not restated from the commit message
(`git log -1 --format=%B 950e3af`):

- **`tools/gen-scale-demo/molecules.py`** — a **50 × 35 nm** box below the
  cells, reached by a tapering dart of the same kind that points at the cells,
  holding the **ten most abundant molecules in a banana cell at 1:1 with
  everything else on the page.**
- **Authored in PICOMETRES**, because that is the unit bond lengths and atomic
  radii are published in: **O–H `96`, C–C `154`, oxygen's van der Waals radius
  `152`, potassium's ionic radius `138`.** Every number checkable against a
  reference table **without arithmetic**, which is the point — a unit choice
  that removes a conversion removes a class of silent error.
- **Eleven Form XObjects** — ten molecules plus the box that invokes them — so
  the page now contains **nested forms**, which it did not exercise before.
  This is not incidental: `PASS 74.4`'s cull and `PASS 74.5`'s shared organelle
  module both operate on forms, and until now every form on this page was
  invoked from the page's own content stream.
- **Space-filling rather than ball-and-stick, as a correctness call**: a stick
  model is mostly empty space and this box exists to state **size**. The cost
  is stated rather than hidden — rings come out as lumpy blobs and connectivity
  is sacrificed, with bonds drawn underneath so they still show in the gaps.
- **Water's label reads `0.37 nm`, not the `0.28 nm` everybody quotes**, and
  the commit message argues why: `0.28` is the **kinetic diameter** — the hole
  it fits through — and `0.37` is the **space it occupies**. ★ **This is the
  same defect class as the headline finding, caught before it shipped**: two
  numbers, both correct, about two different quantities. The box draws at 1:1
  and invites the reader to measure it, so **the label that disagrees with the
  drawing is the wrong one to quote**, and which one that is depends on what
  the drawing is of.
- **The scale chain is unbroken**: the banana is **412 585 829 water molecules
  long**, and both are drawn in one coordinate system **with no scale break
  anywhere between them.** (Sanity-checked here rather than relayed: a 152.7 mm
  banana at `0.37 nm` per molecule is `1.527 × 10⁻¹ / 3.7 × 10⁻¹⁰ =
  4.13 × 10⁸`. ✔)
- **The whole box is readable at ~`1 500 000 000 %`**, which is what it was
  built for. **A single molecule filling the viewport is past the ceiling** —
  and that sentence is now filed with its quantity, per `R213`.

#### `PASS 74.6b` (`65e1910`) — the percentages, and the ranking that followed them

**Three label lines under every molecule**: what it is, **how much of a banana
it is by mass**, and how big it is. The share sits **above** the size because
it is what orders the grid — a reader wondering why cellulose comes before
protein finds the answer on the line under both of them.

**★★ Adding the numbers RE-ORDERED the list, which is the point of adding
them.** The prior order was *"ranked by a remembered impression"*, in the
engineer's own words:

| rank | before (remembered) | after (by mass) | share of fresh mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | water | **water** | **74.9 %** |
| 2 | starch | **starch** | **5.4 %** |
| 3 | sucrose | **glucose** | **5.0 %** |
| 4 | glucose | **fructose** | **4.9 %** |
| 5 | fructose | **sucrose** | **2.4 %** |
| 6 | pectin | **cellulose** | **1.2 %** |
| 7 | cellulose | **protein** | **1.1 %** |
| 8 | protein | **pectin** | **0.7 %** |
| 9 | malic acid | **malic acid** | **0.4 %** |
| 10 | potassium | **potassium** | **0.36 %** |

**Five of ten moved.** The footer's **`96.4 %` of the fruit** is *derived
rather than typed* — checked here by addition rather than trusted:
`74.9 + 5.4 + 5.0 + 4.9 + 2.4 + 1.2 + 1.1 + 0.7 + 0.4 + 0.36 = 96.36`,
displayed as **96.4**. ✔ (hard rule 10 (a) — the total is filed beside its
per-item form, and the per-item form is the table above.)

**★ The measure is named because a top ten with no unit is a claim with no
content.** By molecule **count** the ranking is neither close nor interesting —
water is ~99.5 % of them. **The box says which measure it uses.** This is
`R213`'s obligation being honoured *inside the artefact* on the same day it was
minted from a failure to honour it in the record, and that coincidence is the
best argument for the rule that this entry contains.

**★★ The ripeness seam is DISCLOSED, not tidied.** These are **ripe** figures.
An unripe banana is a different list — green pulp is **20–25 % starch and
1–2 % sugars**, so ripening drops starch **fourfold** while glucose and
fructose rise **tenfold**, and **rows 2 through 5 are the same carbon before
and after.** The page draws a **yellow** banana beside cells with **green**
chloroplasts and packed starch grains, so the document contains a genuine
inconsistency. **The subtitle names which state the numbers describe.** That is
rule 4 applied to a `tools/` artefact that has no operator and no session:
the disclosure has nowhere off-canvas to go, so it goes in the subtitle, and it
goes in rather than the seam being quietly removed.

#### Backlog opened — `PASS 74.7`, and the ruling on whose call it is

Full entry under *Backlog*. **`PASS 74.7` — carry the CTM in `f64` through
content-stream `cm` concatenation and narrow only at paint**, extending
`PASS 74.2`'s base-CTM fix one level down. **The acceptance baseline is the
measured table above** — 11/11 at `2 × 10⁶` and `5 × 10⁶`, 7 at `1.25 × 10⁷`,
3 at `2.5 × 10⁷`, 1 at `5 × 10⁷` — so the Pass has a pass/fail oracle before a
line is written, which is rare enough to be worth naming. **`PASS 74.8` is
opened alongside it** — the `--no-annotations` disclosure gap, promoted out of
the owed-comment list below because it is a rule-4 defect rather than a stale
sentence.

**★ Ruled: the engineer's to take, NOT an operator question**, which is the
disposition the dispatch asked for and it is worth arguing rather than
asserting. **Decision 082** says `pdfce-render` may skip work only where
skipping is **exact**, and that a **lossy** speed-up is the operator's call —
which is what turned the sub-pixel-geometry item into open question `(br)`.
**`PASS 74.7` is the opposite sign.** It does not trade fidelity for speed; it
**removes a fidelity loss**, at a cost in code and probably in time. **Decision
082 does not gate it** and no new decision is minted, because **no choice is
being made** — nobody wants the quantisation.

**What Ken should nonetheless know, and it is in `NEXT_SESSION.md` for that
reason:** the cost is large — every `cm` concatenation in the interpreter, plus
the narrowing point moved — and `R211` binds the narrowing (*narrow exactly
what the path you must stay byte-identical with narrows*), so the round-trip
obligation makes this harder than "change `f32` to `f64`". **Queued, not
blocked.**

★ **Why that is a one-directional law and not bad luck.** The test asserts the
key list by equality, so **adding a key to the `println!` without adding it to
the test turns `render_page.rs` red.** The test's copy is therefore updated
*by force*. The template's copy is updated only *by care*. **The two copies do
not drift apart at random — they drift in exactly one direction, and it is
always the published one**, which is the copy a consuming script's author
actually reads and the only copy with the words *"the **fixed order shown**"*
next to it.

## `PASS 74.4` — Form XObject viewport culling

`do_form` now skips a `Do` whose `/BBox`, mapped through the CTM, lands
entirely outside the canvas or outside the clip in force.

**The cull is EXACT, and that is a consequence of the spec rather than an
assumption.** ISO 32000-1 **§8.10.1**: the form XObject's bounding box *"shall
be used to clip its contents"*. A clip, not a hint — so no operator inside a
form can mark a pixel outside its transformed `/BBox`, so a form whose box
misses the viewport **cannot contribute a pixel**. Nothing here trades fidelity
for speed.

**Two tests, and the pair is the acceptance criterion, not either one alone:**

| test | what it forbids |
|---|---|
| `form_whose_bbox_misses_the_canvas_is_culled_not_executed` | that the cull be **observable** — asserts `forms_culled == 1`, `forms_rendered == 0`, **and** that the raster is byte-identical to the same page with the `Do` removed entirely |
| `form_partly_on_canvas_is_not_culled` | that the cull become **greedier than §8.10.1 allows** — a form straddling the edge still executes |

The second is the one that will matter in a year. A cull with no
complement test drifts toward eagerness under every later "optimisation",
and its failure mode is a **seam at a tile edge** — the signature artefact
of a culling bug and among the hardest to attribute months later. The
implementation is deliberately **one pixel too generous** at the boundary
for the same reason: a shape whose edge lands on the boundary can still
tint the boundary pixel through anti-aliasing.

**The clip box is consulted only when there is no soft mask.** Further down
`do_form`, a transparency group with a soft mask has its clip **replaced** by
the wider pre-mask clip (§11.4.5/§11.6.6); testing against the narrower clip
in force at the cull could then discard a form the widened clip would have
shown. Canvas bounds are always safe; the clip box is used only where no such
widening can happen. **That asymmetry is in the code's own comment**, which is
where it belongs.

### ★★★ The position mattered more than the cull, and the counter could not tell

The first version sat **beside the `/BBox` clip** — one concept in one place,
the natural-looking home, and it passes review.

| placement | forms culled | deepest tier |
|---|---:|---:|
| beside the `/BBox` clip (after stream slice → flate-decode → parse) | **339 of 342** | **802 ms** |
| ahead of the stream slice, first thing in `do_form` | **339 of 342** | **120 ms** |

**Same predicate, same count, same output bytes, 6.7× apart.** The late
placement was still paying **~110 kB of inflate per instance × 342 instances ≈
37 MB of decompression per render for content it was about to discard.**

★ **The instrument added to prove the optimisation works is structurally
incapable of detecting that it barely works**, because the counter is
incremented on the same branch in both placements. *A cull is worth only what
it skips; a counter that reads identical either way is what makes the wrong
version convincing.* Same family as
`a_diagnostic_inside_the_guard_it_reports_can_only_report_true.md` — the
instrument sitting inside the thing it is meant to adjudicate.

### Measured tier timings (same machine, same session, ~1600 × 1000 viewport per tier)

| tier | forms executed | forms culled | time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| whole page, scale 1.6 | 342 | 0 | **1 487 ms** |
| cells, ~62 000 % | 342 | 0 | 1 603 ms |
| pulp cell, ~90 000 % | 342 | 0 | 1 417 ms |
| skin cell, ~420 000 % | 3 | **339** | **120 ms** |
| easter egg, ~360 000 % | 325 | 17 | 1 175 ms |
| mitochondria, ~2 600 000 % | 40 | 302 | 243 ms |
| one organelle, ~16 000 000 % | 1 | **341** | 182 ms |

Per hard rule 10(a), the total beside its per-item form: **342 instances from
12 shared Form XObjects = 28.5 instances per form**; **7 571 ATP synthase F1
heads across the form library = 631 per form**; the 37 MB of avoided inflate is
**~110 kB × 342**. The denominators are recorded because without them the
division is impossible, not merely unperformed.

**Read the table the right way round.** The rows where the cull fires are
**the fast ones**, and they are the *deepest* zooms — cost falls as
magnification rises, because most of the page has left the viewport. The rows
still at ~1.5 s are the ones where every form is genuinely on screen, which is
what the next section is about.

### The new counter, and where it sits

`Diagnostics::forms_culled`, surfaced as **`forms_culled` on `pdfce-cli
render-page`'s stable metrics line, placed BESIDE `forms` rather than appended
at the end** — a deliberate departure from that line's append-only habit,
argued in a comment in `crates/pdfce-cli/tests/render_page.rs`: the metrics
half is parsed as `key=value` pairs so a consumer keying off ordinal position
is already broken, and *"342 forms executed, 0 culled"* only reads as a pair
when the two are adjacent. The stable-key-order contract test was updated in
the same commit.

**Counted separately from `forms_rendered` rather than folded into it**, and
the field's own rustdoc says why: *"342 forms executed"* and *"342 forms in the
page, 1 of them on screen"* are different answers to an operator asking why a
render was slow — **and the first is what pdfce used to report while doing the
second's work.**

### ★★ NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY — and it is an OPERATOR question, not a backlog item

At **page-fit zoom all 342 forms ARE on the canvas**, each ~**1/70th of a pixel**
across, and pdfce still rasterises every path inside them: **~1.5 s for a
whole-page render, against ~110 ms before this page gained ~1 000 000 path
operators.**

Skipping sub-pixel geometry would fix it and **would be lossy** — those paths do
contribute anti-aliased coverage, so the raster would change. **pdfce does not
silently trade fidelity for speed**, so this is Ken's call. Filed as open
operator question **`(br)`**, not as a Pass the engineer can take alone. The
architectural half is **decision 082**.

## `PASS 74.5` — `tools/gen-scale-demo/mitochondrion.py`

New module, **603 lines**. Every mitochondrion on the banana demo page is now
drawn to its real internal anatomy instead of as an ellipse with one to three
chords ruled across it.

**Why chords were wrong, and it is a correctness claim rather than a taste
one.** A crista is not a chord; it is an **invagination of the inner membrane**
joined to it through a narrow neck, and the space inside a crista is continuous
with the **intermembrane space**, not with the matrix. Chords get the
**compartment topology backwards** — which is the one thing a section view
exists to convey.

**Authored in NANOMETRES; emitted as shared Form XObjects.** Contents: outer
membrane (**5 nm**), intermembrane space (**24 nm**), an inner membrane built
as **ONE closed path** that runs the boundary and dives inward to form each
crista through its own junction (**18 nm** neck, **26 nm** lumen), ATP synthase
F1 heads (**10 nm**) at the real density gradient (**11.5 nm** pitch on crista
faces and rims, **62 nm** on the flat boundary membrane), mitoribosomes
(**26 nm**), matrix granules (**36 nm**), mtDNA nucleoids (**210 nm**) drawn as
tangled closed loops.

**All FOUR populations now share the module** — **14** in the pulp cytoplasm,
**3** in the skin cell, **325** beaded into the easter-egg heart and letters;
**342 instances from 12 shared forms**, **7 571 F1 heads** across the form
library. **Before this they were three independent copy-pastes that had
DRIFTED**: three cristae in the pulp cell, one or two in the easter egg, and
**none at all in the skin cell**.

★ **That is the finding worth carrying, and it is not about mitochondria.**
Three copies of one drawing, authored from one intent, diverged to *three
cristae / one or two / none* without anybody deciding anything — and the
divergence was invisible because **no two of the three were ever on screen at
the same magnification at the same time.** A duplicated *drawing* has no
compiler, no test and no diff that anybody reads; sharing it is the only
mechanism that makes the three agree.

**Smallest feature 10 nm = 2.835 × 10⁻⁵ pt, first readable at ~35 000 000 %.**
The demo's scale chain went **from six tiers to eight**.

### ★★ Two bugs found by RENDERING, not by reading — and both were silent

**(1) `PT_PER_NM` written as a division where it needed the reciprocal.**
`25.4/72/1_000_000` where `1/(25.4/72*1_000_000)` was meant — off by
`0.3528²` = **8.03×**. Every organelle came out **an eighth of its size,
correctly placed and correctly shaped**, which reads as a drawing choice rather
than a unit error. No clip, no overflow, no NaN, no missing mark. **PDF's user
space has no declared unit** (§8.3.2.3; `/UserUnit` optional and rare), so the
file carries nothing that can contradict a wrong scale, and **no downstream
validator — veraPDF, `qpdf --check`, pdfium — can flag a shape as the wrong
physical size**, because size is the thing being asserted.

**(2) The crista path left one lip of its junction and dived in on the WRONG
lateral side**, so it crossed its own junction mouth twice — a **bow tie**.
Every membrane was still the right shape and **the stroked outline looked
perfect**; nonzero winding (§8.5.3.3.2, `f`'s default) then filled **every
crista lumen with matrix colour** — i.e. *the exact compartment error the
module exists to correct, one layer down.* Catching it required a
**160 000 000 % render of a single crista**, because at less magnification the
lumen is too narrow to read a colour out of at all.

★ **The shape both share:** a defect that produces a **plausible picture**.
Neither raised an error, moved a counter, or dropped a mark. **Stroke and fill
read one path object through two unrelated rules**, so reviewing the outlined
drawing is *not evidence about the filled drawing* — and the outlined drawing
is the one that looks diagnostic. Both are filed to `C:\personal_rag\pdf\`
(paths at the foot of this entry).

### Why Form XObjects rather than inline geometry

Size, and **precision**: a 10 nm feature expressed as an absolute page
coordinate near `x = 540` needs **eleven significant figures**, past the
**five** ISO 32000-1 **Annex C** requires. A form's own coordinate system keeps
the numbers small; the CTM carries the magnitude.

## Decision minted

**Decision 082 — `pdfce-render` may skip work only where skipping is EXACT; a
lossy speed-up is an OPERATOR decision, not an engineering one.** Full text in
`ARCHITECTURE.md` §12; §4 gains sync entry **(AA)** for
`Diagnostics::forms_culled` in the same filing.

## ★ Standing-rule disposition — MINT DECLINED, and the decline is argued

***"A cull is worth only what it skips, and a counter that reads identical
either way is what makes the wrong version convincing"*** is **engineering
method, not project policy.**

**The warrant is impossibility, not the instance count**, which makes this a
stronger decline than the 227th filing's. `R210`'s own minting test asks
whether a mechanical oracle exists that works **from artefacts alone**. Here it
does not, and the reason is structural rather than incidental: deciding whether
an early-out is placed above the work it makes unnecessary requires knowing
**which work the predicate needs in order to be evaluated** — that is the
function's data-flow, per call site, and it is exactly the judgement being
made. A gate could at best grep for a `return` above a `decode`, which is not
the property.

Note the asymmetry with **`R211`**, minted five commits ago on the same kind of
question: *"do these two paths still produce the same bytes?"* had an oracle
already sitting in the tree. *"Is this early-out in the right place?"* has no
artefact at all — only a wall clock, and only on a workload where it fires.

**Filed to `D:/dev/rag/rust/` instead, where it is reachable by any project**
(path at the foot of this entry). This is the sixth consecutive filing to
decline a mint on an argued warrant rather than a shrug.

this page paint"* and is now *"how many were executed"* — a form that is culled
increments neither. Searched for: the **shape of `render-page`'s stable line**
as a claim about which keys appear and in what order; **"every `Do` is
executed"** as a claim about the renderer's behaviour; and **`forms=`** as a
claim about a page's form population, across `crates/`, `tools/` and `docs/`.

#### ★★★ WHY IT WAS UNFILED, AND THE GENERALISATION

`check-commits-filed.py` counts a commit as owing a filing when it touches
`crates/`, `tools/` or `fixtures/`. `c24ad7a` touches `crates/pdfce-cli/src/main.rs`
and `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md`. So it is a **code commit**, and a code
commit named in no filing is precisely what that gate exists to catch.

**It is not a false positive, and the gate's own docstring predicted this
exact case.** Its exclusion list was corrected on 2026-08-11 — *"a commit with
code in it is checked whatever else it touches, which is the whole of the
correction: a mixed commit is precisely where code hides"* — after `b4a66ed`
was caught **self-certifying by containing the very record files it was never
described in**. `c24ad7a` is the same shape with the roles reversed: it
contains the record files **and is described in them**, for three *other*
commits, and not for itself.

**★ The structural fact, stated as generally as it deserves:**

> **A filing commit that also carries a code change CANNOT FILE ITSELF.** The
> filing's text is written before the commit exists; the hash it would need to
> cite does not exist until the commit is made. So a filing-plus-code commit
> **manufactures exactly one new unfiled commit per filing** — the loop does
> not terminate on its own, and the next filing inherits it.

**The remedy is procedural and it is the ENGINEER'S, not this role's.**
`crates/`, `tools/` and `.claude/` are outside the librarian's remit by
construction, so when a sweep reports survivors there the librarian *must*
report rather than edit — and the engineer then has a free choice of **when**
to commit the fix. The whole remedy is:

> **Repairs go in their own commit. Before the filing is fine, after the
> filing is fine, INSIDE the filing is not.** A filing commit that is
> docs-only is not counted by the gate at all, and the loop terminates in one
> step.

**★ This is already written down, by the engineer, and it is UNTRACKED.**
`.claude/agent-memory/pdfce-engineer/feedback_never_bundle_code_into_a_filing_commit.md`
exists in the working tree (`git status --porcelain` → `??`) and states the
rule, the instance and the application correctly, including the right refusal:
*"do not reach for `tools/commits-filed-baseline.txt`."* **A memory file that
is untracked is one `git clean` from not existing**, and `.claude/` is not
code, so committing it cannot trip the gate this entry is about. **Recorded
here as owed work, not as done.**

##### What it would take to make this a RULE rather than a note

**Mint DECLINED at n = 1** — consistent with the five declines of the past
four filings, all of which held that one occurrence is a finding and the
project does not number findings. **But the decline is weaker here than
those**, and saying so is the honest form:

- Four of those five were declined on **impossibility** — *"there is no
  artefact to check"*, *"no gate can content-check a disclosure"*. **That
  warrant does not apply here.** The question *"does this commit's diff touch
  code while its subject says `librarian:`?"* is answerable from artefacts
  alone: `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r <sha>` and the subject
  line. That is exactly the test `R210` names for when a gate is possible, and
  `R209`'s test too.
- So the warrant for declining is **only the instance count**, and it is the
  weaker of the two warrants.

**What would convert it:** either (a) a **second instance** — a second
`librarian:` commit whose diff reaches `crates/` or `tools/` — at which point
it should be minted as a standing rule with the gate wired at the same time;
or (b) the engineer wiring the check **now** without a rule, which is the
cheaper path and needs no number. Both are the engineer's to take. **The
predicate, written out so nobody has to re-derive it:** *fail when a commit's
subject begins `librarian:` (or its diff contains both `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`
and `docs/ROADMAP.md`) **and** its name-only diff contains any path under
`crates/`, `tools/` or `fixtures/`.* No knowledge of current behaviour is
required, which is what separates a buildable gate from the disclosure-truth
gates this project has correctly refused four times.

**Ceiling therefore unchanged: `R211` stands, next free `R212`.**
