- **R207 — CONTENT ROUTED THROUGH A SHELL COMMAND LINE OR STRING (A CI
  `run:` STEP, A `git commit -m` CALL, ANY INTERPOLATED PROSE) IS LIVE
  SHELL TEXT, NEVER INERT DATA; WRITE IT TO A FILE OR PASS IT VIA A
  NATIVE ARGV API INSTEAD OF INTERPOLATING IT INTO A SHELL STRING
  (2026-08-21; librarian-minted, two-hundred-and-fifteenth filing;
  tooling rule, second confirmed occurrence across two media, ten days
  apart, root cause identical both times).** A backtick inside a
  double-quoted or unquoted shell string is not punctuation, it is
  **command substitution**: `` `word` `` runs `word` as a command and
  splices its STDOUT in place — silently, because a missing command
  prints to *stderr* and substitutes the *empty string*, and the
  enclosing command's own exit status stays `0`, so `set -e` never
  fires. The failure is not an error; it looks exactly like text the
  author might have written.
  **Two instances, ten days apart, same mechanism, two different hosts:**
  (1) `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`5047cb9`, 2026-08-11) built an
  `::error::` string containing a backtick-quoted word meant as a
  Markdown code span; the printed message lost the one word it existed
  to name — `::error::pdfce-core  enables an extra feature on the
  crate.` (2) a `git commit -m` call in this project's own librarian
  dispatch (interactive Bash-tool call, 2026-08-21) had a backticked
  phrase splice a fifteen-line file listing into the middle of a
  commit-message sentence. **Neither was found by a gate — both were
  found by a person reading the printed string back and noticing it was
  short a word or long a paragraph.**
  **The rule is about the MECHANISM, not the trigger character, and
  that is deliberate — the dispatching engineer's own framing, adopted
  verbatim: *"it wants to be about content passing through a shell, not
  about backticks or backslashes specifically — the whole lesson is
  that the trigger keeps changing and the mechanism does not."*** A
  sibling, pre-existing finding
  (`D:\dev\rag\rust\a_multiline_string_literal_that_loses_its_trailing_backslash_bakes_a_visible_gap_mid_sentence.md`,
  footer (b)) already carries the same mechanism under a **different**
  trigger — escape-sequence collapsing (`\t`/`\n`) inside a shell
  heredoc, rather than command substitution inside a shell string — and
  is cited here as the rule's other confirmed shape, not folded into a
  single instance count: two triggers, one class, now two write-ups.
  **Fix, in order of preference:** (a) write the content to a file and
  reference the file (`git commit -F`, a CI step that `cat`s a
  generated artifact) — a file is inert to every downstream reader; (b)
  if a string must be built inline, use a native argv API with no
  shell in the loop (`subprocess.run([...])`, `Command::new(...).arg(...)`)
  rather than string-interpolating into a shell command line; a
  single-quoted heredoc delimiter (`<<'EOF'`) is the fallback when
  neither is available, because it suppresses all expansion including
  backticks — an *unquoted* delimiter does not. **Never trust `set -e`
  to catch this** — the failure is a silently shortened string, not a
  non-zero exit.
  **Why no gate is proposed, and why that is not an oversight.** The
  same warrant hard rule 10's corollary already gives for stale
  figures: checking *"is this string what the author meant"* requires
  knowing the author's intent, which is the very fact the defect
  destroys. A tool cannot tell a deliberately short sentence from a
  splice-shortened one without an oracle it does not have.
  New RAG file:
  `D:\dev\rag\rust\prose_with_backticks_through_a_shell_string_undergoes_command_substitution_silently.md`.
  ~~**Ceiling moves `R206` → `R207`; next free `R208`.**~~ **Superseded
  by `R208`, below (2026-08-21, same day).**

- **R208 — A GRAPHICS-STATE FIELD WHOSE DEFAULT MATTERS MUST BE FINDABLE
  *FROM THE FIELD*. ADDING ONE OBLIGES YOU TO A SINGLE NAMED PREDICATE
  EVERY "IS THE STATE STILL DEFAULT?" SITE CALLS — NEVER TO REMEMBERING
  THE SITES (2026-08-21; librarian-minted, two-hundred-and-sixteenth
  filing; THIRD occurrence, over this project's two-instance promotion
  bar; the dispatching engineer proposed the mint AND the useful form,
  both adopted).**

  **The mechanism, and it is not "somebody forgot".** `pdfce-render`'s
  graphics state has a growing set of fields whose **default value is
  load-bearing** — a fast path is taken *only if every one of them is
  still at its initial value*. Each new field must therefore be added to
  **every predicate that asks "is the state still default?"**, and those
  predicates are **scattered by construction**: they live at the call
  sites that benefit from the fast path, not next to the field. **Nothing
  makes them findable from the field.** So adding a field is a change
  whose full obligation is **invisible from the place the change is
  made** — the definition of a defect that recurs.

  **Three occurrences, one shape, all in `pdfce-render`:**
  1. `nonseparable` omitted from `outer_is_neutral` — a group with a
     non-separable blend mode took the inline path.
  2. `nonseparable` omitted **again**, from the **reset list** — a
     different predicate, same field, same session-class.
  3. **`soft_mask` omitted from `outer_is_neutral` (`Pass 97.0d`,
     `86a7b70`)** — a masked group with a `Normal` blend and alpha 1 took
     the inline path and **had its mask applied per object with no result
     to apply it to**, which is exactly the §11.4.5 defect `97.0d`
     existed to fix, re-entering through the predicate that decides
     whether `97.0d`'s code runs at all.

  **★ WHY THIS IS MINTED AND NOT LOGGED, and it is the whole warrant: the
  comment directly above `outer_is_neutral` had ALREADY NAMED THE
  MECHANISM TWICE, IN PAST TENSE** — *"a new graphics-state field has to
  be added to every predicate that asks 'is the state still default?',
  and nothing makes those sites findable from the field."* **A comment
  that correctly predicts its own next defect, and is then not acted on,
  is a design note, not a guard.** The failure is not that the mechanism
  was unknown; it is that **knowing it was left as a thing to remember**.
  This project has ruled repeatedly (`R193`, `R194`, decision 075) that a
  count alone does not warrant a mint — here the warrant is stronger than
  the count: **a documented, correctly-stated warning failed to prevent
  the very instance it described.**

  **THE RULE IS THE REMEDY, NOT THE REMINDER, and that distinction is the
  engineer's own framing, adopted verbatim:** *"the useful form is not
  'remember to update the predicate' but 'a graphics-state field whose
  default matters must be findable FROM the field'."* Concretely: **one
  `GraphicsState::is_transparency_neutral()` (or equivalently named
  single predicate) that every such site calls**, so that adding a field
  means editing **one function whose body enumerates the fields** — a
  place the compiler and an ordinary reader both reach from the field's
  own definition. A site that needs a *narrower* question asks it **beside**
  the shared predicate, never instead of it.

  **What this rule does NOT claim.** It does not say a fast path is wrong,
  and it does not forbid additional per-site conditions. It says the
  *neutrality* half must have exactly one definition. **And it is not
  `R151`** (a core API with no caller): that is about a capability nobody
  reaches; this is about **one capability reached from several places
  that must agree**, where the defect is disagreement, not absence.

  **No gate is proposed, and that is deliberate rather than an
  oversight.** A checker would have to know which fields' defaults are
  load-bearing — the very judgement the rule exists to centralise. **The
  centralisation IS the enforcement**: once every site calls one
  predicate, a missing field is a missing line in one function, which is
  the kind of omission ordinary review catches. Same warrant hard rule
  10 and `R207` already give for declining gates whose oracle is the
  fact being checked.

  **Ceiling moves `R207` → `R208`; next free `R209`.**
  ~~**next free `R209`**~~ — **claimed by `R209`, below (2026-08-21, same
  day, next filing).**

- **R209 — "ALL GATES GREEN" NAMES A SET, AND THE SET SOMEBODY RUNS IS NOT
  THE SET CI RUNS. A CI JOB WITH NO LOCAL RUNNER IS UNOBSERVED, NOT
  PASSING — SO EVERY CI COMMAND OWES A NAMED LOCAL STAND-IN, OR AN
  EXPLICIT CI-ONLY JUSTIFICATION, IN WRITING (2026-08-21;
  librarian-minted, two-hundred-and-eighteenth filing, the dispatching
  engineer having explicitly left the disposition to this role; tooling
  rule, second confirmed occurrence across two media, sixteen days apart,
  THE SAME CI JOB BOTH TIMES).**

  **The mechanism.** The habit this project calls *"run the gates"* is
  `for g in tools/check-*` — **sixteen scripts** as of `5884ed1`, each one
  command with a pass/fail line. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` defines
  **nine jobs / ten runs** (`test` is a two-OS matrix, `ci.yml:73`), and
  that entire sweep is **ONE** of them. `cargo +nightly fuzz build`, the
  wasm32 leg of `cross-check`, `no-network`'s denylist and
  `third-party-licenses`' `cargo about` regeneration have **no local
  equivalent anybody runs by habit**. A green local sweep and a red CI are
  therefore **not a contradiction and never were** — and **neither signal
  is wrong**, which is what lets this survive for days.

  **Two instances, two media, sixteen days apart, same job:**
  1. **2026-08-05, agent memory** —
     `.claude/agent-memory/pdfce-engineer/feedback_gates_i_owe_myself.md`,
     *"The cargo-fuzz gate is the one that gets skipped"*: `Pass 36.1`
     shipped with fmt, clippy, tests, ui-strings, ledger and cargo-tree
     all run and the Pass reported complete **without the fuzz arm**;
     *"the librarian caught it, not me."* Its stated reason is this rule's
     whole mechanism: *"the other gates are one command with a pass/fail
     line. Fuzzing needs a DLL on PATH, a minute of runtime, and a
     judgement about which branches to drive — so it reads as optional in
     a way `cargo clippy` never does. It is not optional."*
  2. **2026-08-21, CI** — `fuzz-smoke` **red on every push for three
     days** (`MarkupSpec::Square` gained `border_effect` on 2026-08-19 and
     `fuzz/fuzz_targets/annot_author.rs` was not updated), found only
     while verifying CI before tagging `v0.7.0`. **Not one local signal
     disagreed, because none was looking.** See `fb06d93` and `5884ed1` in
     the 218th filing's Shipped entry.

  **★ "UNOBSERVED, NOT PASSING" is the load-bearing phrase, and it makes
  this a rule about CLAIMS rather than about fuzzing.** Nobody believed a
  false thing about the job — nobody believed anything about it; it
  produced no local evidence in either direction. What failed is that
  *"all gates green"* was written, and read, as though it **ranged over
  CI** when it ranged over **one job of nine**. **A claim about a set is
  only as good as the enumeration of the set**, and nobody had enumerated
  this one: the dispatch opening the 218th filing said *"nine jobs green,
  one red"* — **ten**, against a nine-job workflow, arithmetically
  impossible and unnoticed for an hour.

  **What the rule obliges, in three lines.**
  (a) **Never write *"all gates green"* unqualified** — name the set
  (`tools/check-*`, the `cargo` trio, or CI) and say which you mean.
  (b) ***"CI green"* is assertable only from an OBSERVED CI run on the
  commit in question** — never inferred from a local sweep, never from CI
  on the parent commit.
  (c) **Every CI `run:` command is classified `LOCAL` / `LOCAL-VIA` /
  `CI-ONLY` with the stand-in command WRITTEN DOWN**; `CI-ONLY` stays a
  small, individually justified set, never a default.

  **★★ WHY A GATE IS THE RIGHT ANSWER HERE, WHEN `R207`, HARD RULE 11 AND
  THE ABSENCE-PHRASING FINDING ALL REFUSED ONE — do not over-read this as
  a reversal.** Those three declined on one shared warrant:
  content-checking a claim requires knowing the author's intent or the
  current behaviour, **the very fact the claim exists to report**, so
  there is no oracle. **This one HAS an oracle.** *"Is every `run:`
  command in the workflow accounted for?"* is a property of a text file,
  answerable against a written table, needing no reference to today's tree
  or to anyone's intent — which is precisely why `tools/check-ci-parity.py`
  could be **sabotage-verified** (a fake job with an unrecognised command
  appended to `ci.yml`; the gate failed and named it by file and line; the
  workflow restored byte-identical, confirmed by `git diff --exit-code`
  rather than by eye) and the other three could not be built at all.
  **The refusals were a diagnosis of missing oracles, not a policy against
  gates.**

  **The mechanical half: `tools/check-ci-parity.py` (`5884ed1`)** —
  classifies every `run:` command in `.github/workflows/*.yml`, **fails on
  anything unrecognised**, and deliberately **runs nothing** (one that ran
  the jobs would take CI's fifteen minutes, so nobody would run it, and
  the question is a property of the workflow file, not of today's tree).
  At mint: **19 `LOCAL` / 11 `LOCAL-VIA` / 3 `CI-ONLY` = 33 commands, 0
  unaccounted**. Its `LOCAL-VIA` entry for the offending job is the
  finding turned into a runnable line: **`cd fuzz && cargo check --bins`**
  — no nightly, no ASan DLL, and it catches *"a fuzz target that no longer
  compiles against the spec it constructs"*, **the entire class that has
  ever broken that job**, in seconds. `python tools/check-ci-parity.py
  --list` prints the whole local command set. ★ *The stand-in does not
  have to be the job; it has to catch the job's observed failure class.*

  **★ The rule is NOT discharged by that script — which is why it is a
  rule and not a closed ticket.** The script makes a new **unaccounted**
  job impossible. It **cannot make anybody run the stand-in**. The
  obligation to name which set you mean by *"green"* is a commitment on
  behaviour, in hard rules 8 and 10's family — checkable after the fact,
  enforced by nothing.

  **What this rule is NOT.** Not `R205`: that is a gate which **runs and
  under-reports**, surfaced by an independent forecast disagreeing with
  its output; this is a gate **never consulted**, which does not
  under-report because it does not report. Different remedies (widen the
  class vs. write down a stand-in), different detectors (a forecast vs. an
  enumeration). Not `R106` (a ledger green because its input was narrowed)
  for the same reason one layer up. **Where they meet, recorded so the
  boundary stays legible:** the `.github/` widening (215th filing) and the
  `fuzz/` widening (218th) are `R205`'s *input-list-too-narrow* species
  applied to **a gate's** input list; `R209` is that species applied to
  **the human's** gate list — the one no gate was watching.

  Cross-references: `R205`, `R106`, `R174` (read the tool's own output,
  not a test asserting on it), `R207` and `R208` (the two previous mints,
  and two of the three gate-refusals this rule's oracle argument
  distinguishes itself from). New RAG file:
  `D:\dev\rag\rust\the_local_gate_sweep_is_a_subset_of_ci_and_nothing_compares_the_two.md`
  — **amended the same day** with this rule's claim-scope half, its
  2026-08-05 second instance, and the oracle argument. (A second file
  was started for those and **deleted as a duplicate**; see the
  filing's RAG section.)

  > **★ THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is why this is worth writing down rather

  > when it finds **nothing**, which is the **passing** condition. So the
  > authoritative list printed a command that **reports failure on a healthy

- **R210 — A CONFORMANCE FIGURE IS FILED WITH THE *CRITERIA* THE HARNESS
  IMPLEMENTS, NOT ONLY ITS DENOMINATOR. A HARNESS THAT SCORES A SUBSET OF A
  SUITE'S PASS CRITERIA REPORTS `clean` FOR THE REST, WHICH IS
  INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PASS (2026-08-21; librarian-minted,
  two-hundred-and-twenty-fifth filing; instrument rule, SECOND confirmed
  occurrence on the SAME instrument producing the SAME headline number four
  days apart).**

  **The mechanism.** Hard rule 10 already forces the **denominator** — the
  figure is `X of 51`, never bare `X` — and a denominator answers *"out of how
  many?"*. It does **not** answer *"by what test?"*, and a harness that
  implements one of a suite's criteria is **not wrong about the patches it
  scores**; it is silent about the ones it does not, and **silence is emitted
  as `clean`**. Nothing in the figure, the denominator, or a re-run
  distinguishes *"this patch passed"* from *"this patch was never
  adjudicated"*.

  **Two instances, same instrument, same number, four days apart:**
  1. **2026-08-17, `tools/suite-check.py`'s FIRST RUN — `29 of 51`.**
     **13 of the 51 patches use REFERENCE STRIPS, not X-shaped traps**, and an
     X-detector cannot adjudicate them. **Caught before the number was
     reported as final** (148th filing) — a near-miss, not an incident.
  2. **2026-08-21, the same harness — `29 of 51` again.** **Seven patches use
     the suite's POSITIVE marker** (*"if no check mark appears then DeviceN
     colour was transformed to CMYK (= ERROR)"*) — PCS `050`, `080`, `081`,
     `082`, `150`, `151`, `152` — and the harness **hunts only for a cross that
     should not be there**. All seven have been reported `clean` **for the
     harness's entire life**; at least three are failures. Filed, published and
     propagated across three documents for a day before the **operator** read
     the render cell by cell. Corrected standing: **26 pass at minimum**.

  **★ WHY A RE-MEASUREMENT CANNOT DISCHARGE THIS, and why that makes it a rule
  rather than a caution.** The *suite standing board* already carries the right
  caveat for a **stale** figure — *"staleness is a relation to the world and a
  document has no access to that; only re-measuring does"*. **That is false for
  a MIS-SCORED figure.** Every suite number this project has filed came from
  **the harness scoring itself**, with thresholds calibrated against **one**
  patch whose answer was already known from a code change. **An instrument that
  agrees with itself returns the same number forever.** Re-measurement checks
  freshness; only an **oracle** checks correctness, and R210's job is to make
  the *absence* of one visible in the figure itself.

  **What the rule obliges, in three lines.**
  (a) **State the criteria beside the count** — *"26 pass of 51 **by the
  negative-marker criterion**; 7 patches use the positive criterion and are
  **unadjudicated**"* — so a reader can see the gap without reading the
  harness.
  (b) **An unadjudicated patch gets its OWN verdict**, never folded into
  `pass` and never into `FAIL`. `Pass 122.2` builds `MISSING-MARK` for exactly
  this. **★ AMENDED 2026-08-24 (243rd filing, `Pass 122.2` shipped,
  `f6457ee`): the verdict that shipped is named `MARK?`, not `MISSING-MARK`,
  and it is honest UNCERTAINTY rather than a detected absence** — a
  colour-keyed presence detector was built, caught producing a false
  positive (see the RAG finding this Pass filed), and thrown away rather
  than shipped. Clause (b)'s obligation is satisfied either way: the point
  is that the four patches get a THIRD verdict distinct from `pass`/`FAIL`,
  which `MARK?` is.
  (c) **Name the calibration source of every threshold**, and **how many
  independent cases it was calibrated against.** *"Calibrated on one patch
  whose answer was known"* is a sentence that would have prevented both
  instances, and it is one line.

  **★★ THIS HAS AN ENFORCEMENT LAYER, which is why it was minted rather than
  filed only as a finding** — the test this project applies before minting
  (see the 224th filing's two declines, and `R209`'s own §on when a gate is
  possible). **The question *"which criteria does this harness implement?"* has
  an ORACLE: the suite's own ReadMes.** `grep`ping them for *"check mark"*
  returns the seven-patch family mechanically, with no knowledge of pdfce's
  current behaviour required — unlike a disclosure's *truth*, which is what
  hard rule 11 and `R207` correctly refuse to gate. **Do not generalise those
  refusals into a policy against gates; the test is whether the question can be
  answered from artefacts alone, and this one can.**

  **★ Scope note, so it is not over-read.** This binds on **conformance-suite
  and corpus figures** — the print-conformance suite, veraPDF, `fixtures/external` — not on ordinary
  test counts, where the criterion is the assertion and there is nothing to
  omit.

  **★★ AMENDED 2026-08-22 (two-hundred-and-twenty-seventh filing) — THE SCOPE
  NOTE ABOVE IS TOO NARROW BY ONE CLASS: THIS ALSO BINDS ON A CLAIM ABOUT A
  GATE'S OWN HIT RATE.** The note is kept above rather than rewritten, because
  it was right about what it excluded (ordinary test counts) and wrong only
  about what it forgot.

  **The second class, and why it is the SAME rule rather than a neighbouring
  one.** `bd9844d` (2026-08-22) wrote of `tools/check-string-gaps.sh`: *"Third
  time this project has hit that; **the gate has caught it every time**."*
  **False.** `ae06440` (2026-08-20) is titled *"the string-gap gate reported
  **two of three**, and the one it could not see had a `{placeholder}` on the
  other side of the gap"* — and that third hole was found **by a human who knew
  independently how many there were**. Record: **three episodes, one
  under-report.** The **ordinal** survives (*"third time"*, correct on
  `git log -- tools/check-string-gaps.sh`); the **absolute** does not.

  **Line up the two instances and they share every step:**

  | | the suite, `29 of 51` | the gate, *"every time"* |
  |---|---|---|
  | who produced the figure | the harness scoring itself | the gate's green runs, read as a complete history |
  | the silent part | 7 positive-marker patches emitted as `clean` | one episode the gate could not see |
  | why a re-run cannot find it | an instrument that agrees with itself returns the same number forever | a gate blind to a hole is byte-indistinguishable from a gate with nothing to find |
  | what found it | the **operator**, reading cell by cell | a **human** with an independent count; then `git log` |
  | survives | the **relative** movement between runs | the **ordinal** |
  | does not | the **absolute** pass count | the **absolute** "every time" |

  **One sentence covers both:** *an instrument's misses live inside its own
  denominator, so its silence is emitted as success — which makes a
  self-report valid for **differences** and invalid for **absolutes**, and only
  an oracle outside the instrument can tell you which you are holding.* That is
  the paragraph already in this rule (*"re-measurement checks freshness; only an
  oracle checks correctness"*), applied to a gate instead of to a harness.

  **What the amendment adds to (a)–(c) above:** **(d) A claim about a gate's
  own performance is a claim about the GATE'S HISTORY, and that history is in
  `git log` — cite it or drop the absolute.** *"It has caught every one"*
  requires knowing the misses, which is the one thing the gate cannot report;
  *"it has caught every one since `<sha>` widened it"* is checkable in one
  command. **Ask before writing the claim: what would a MISS have looked
  like?** If the answer is *"exactly like a pass"*, the absolute is unearned.

  **★ Why this was amended rather than minted as `R212`.** The mechanism is
  already stated here in full; only the scope note excluded the second
  instance, and a scope note is the part of a rule a new instance is entitled to
  widen. Minting would have put **one mechanism under two numbers** — the
  fragmentation the 220th, 222nd and 223rd filings each declined to commit —
  and a reader arriving at the gate-history rule would have had no route back to
  the suite derivation that explains it. **Ceiling unmoved: `R211` stands, next
  free `R212`.**

  **★ The asymmetry, so the amendment is not over-read.** In the suite case an
  *instrument* produced the wrong number; here a *human sentence in a commit
  message* made an absolute claim about an instrument. Clause (d) is therefore a
  question to ask **before writing the claim**, not a change to any gate. The
  two are joined by the fact that **the sentence was believable only because the
  gate's misses are invisible** — the property this rule exists to name.

  **★ And the interval is the finding.** The suite over-count was written down
  on 2026-08-21; *"has caught it every time"* was written **the next day, by the
  same project, in a commit message**. Four days separated the two corrections.
  **A rule recorded is not a rule internalised**, and the second instance came
  from the shape being filed under a subject heading (*conformance figures*)
  narrow enough that nobody recognised it in a different setting. That is the
  argument for widening a scope note as soon as a second setting appears,
  rather than waiting for a third.

  **★★★ INSTANCE-NOTE, 2026-08-24 (243rd filing, `Pass 122.2`, `f6457ee`) —
  THIS IS `R210` BEING ACTED ON, NOT MERELY RESTATED, AND IT FOUND THE RULE'S
  OWN FOUNDING DOCUMENT MIS-STATING THE CRITERIA SET IT WAS WARNING ABOUT.**
  `docs/suite-operator-review-2026-08-21.md` — the calibration set this rule

  claim (an area term repairs the contrast floor) also did not survive
  re-measurement — see the suite standing board's 2026-08-24 correction,
  `Pass 122.2`'s *Shipped* entry, for both corrections in full. **The

- **R211 — WHEN TWO CODE PATHS OWE EACH OTHER BYTE-IDENTICAL OUTPUT, THAT IS A
  *PRECISION* CONTRACT, NOT ONLY AN ARITHMETIC ONE: NARROW EXACTLY WHAT THE
  OTHER PATH NARROWS, KEEP FULL PRECISION ON THE INTERVAL ONLY THIS PATH SEES —
  AND A COMMENT ASSERTING THAT TWO CALLERS *"CANNOT DISAGREE"* MUST NAME THE
  TEST THAT WOULD GO RED IF THEY DID (2026-08-22; librarian-minted,
  two-hundred-and-twenty-sixth filing; `Pass 74.2`, `71f7055`).**

  **The mechanism, in three sentences.** A byte-identity obligation between a
  narrow path (one region) and a broad one (the whole page) is usually written
  down as an *arithmetic* claim — *"same formula, same answer"* — and it is
  not. **The two paths see numbers of different MAGNITUDE**, and a float's
  error is a function of magnitude, so identical arithmetic on differently
  scaled inputs is **not** identical output. The contract is therefore about
  **where each path narrows**, and it is **asymmetric by construction**.

  **The worked instance, and both halves cost a red test to establish.**
  `region_base_geometry_of` must produce a rectangle byte-identical to a crop
  of `page_device_geometry`'s output:

  - **The PAGE BOX is narrowed to `f32` FIRST**, deliberately, *because the
    other path does*. Computing from the `f64` box instead is **more accurate
    and wrong** — it shifts corners by a pixel on some pages, and the poster
    tiling test that asserts reassembly went red on exactly that.
  - **The REGION's corners keep full `f64`**, because a deep-zoom region is **a
    tiny interval around a large coordinate**: at scale 4.3 M an 800-pixel
    viewport is **1.86e-4 pt** wide, while `f32` near 100 has a spacing of
    **7.6e-6** — one part in twelve of the half-width. Narrowing there was
    tried and returned a **790 × 526** raster for a requested 800 × 600.

  ⇒ **Narrow what the other path narrows; keep full precision on what only this
  path sees.** *More precision* is not the fix and is sometimes the regression.

  **★ WHY THE SECOND CLAUSE IS PART OF THE SAME RULE RATHER THAN A SEPARATE
  ONE.** The commit that introduced the `f64` path broke **two** call sites
  that each carried a comment promising they could not break — poster tiling's
  *"read from the SAME function the renderer uses to place it, never recomputed
  here, so the two cannot disagree about the origin"*, and `replay_region`'s
  equivalent. **Both sentences stayed true-looking and became false in the same
  edit**, because a shared-implementation claim is invalidated by **moving a
  caller**, not by editing the comment's own file. **A comment is not an
  invariant; a test is.** So the comment must cite the test — which converts an
  unfalsifiable assurance into a grep that leads somewhere.

  **What the rule obliges, in three lines.**
  (a) **Name the path you must match, and match its NARROWING, not only its
  formula** — in the code, in a comment at the narrowing site.
  (b) **State which quantity keeps full precision and why**, in terms of the
  magnitude it must resolve (*"a tiny interval around a large coordinate"*),
  not in terms of "being careful".
  (c) **Every *"these cannot disagree"* comment names the test.** If no test
  exists, the sentence is deleted rather than kept — an assurance nothing can
  refute is worse than silence, because it discourages the check.

  **★★ ENFORCEMENT LAYER, which is why this was minted while its sibling
  finding was DECLINED the same day.** The question *"do these two paths still
  produce the same bytes?"* **has an oracle already in the tree** —
  `tiles_rendered_as_regions_match_the_whole_page_crop` — and it answers
  deterministically from artefacts, with no knowledge of intent or of current
  behaviour. That is `R210`'s minting test satisfied. The sibling finding
  (*"an identical failure count across three different fixes means you are
  fixing the wrong thing"* — 5,841 bytes, three times, unmoved) has **no
  artefact to check at all** and was filed to `D:\dev\rag\rust\` instead, on the
  same warrant the 224th and 225th filings declined four candidates.

  **★ The transferable half, which is the part a future session will need and
  is not about floats at all.** The defect's signature was that **the width was
  exact and the height was 128 px wrong — because the test point was near
  `x = 100` and near `y = 700`.** **Fidelity depended on WHERE YOU WERE**, so
  the bug reproduced on one axis and not the other, which reads as an axis-swap
  or a `/Rotate` fault. ⇒ **A per-axis asymmetry with no per-axis code is a
  MAGNITUDE symptom, and the first thing to print is the coordinate, not the
  formula.**

  Cross-references: `R210` (the minting test this rule satisfies and its
  sibling fails), `R193`/`Pass 74.0` (a limit justified by a prediction about
  use), `R151` (a core API no shell reaches — `Pass 74.1` closes one). New RAG
  files:
  `D:\dev\rag\rust\an_f32_error_is_a_magnitude_problem_not_a_precision_one.md`
  and
  `D:\dev\rag\rust\an_identical_failure_count_across_three_different_fixes_means_you_are_fixing_the_wrong_thing.md`.

  **Ceiling moves `R210` → `R211`; next free `R212`.** *(Superseded by later
  mints — next free is now `R216`. Left in place because this line is a record
  of what was true when `R211` was written, per the append-only convention.)*

  ---

  **★★★★ AMENDED 2026-08-23 (librarian-amended, two-hundred-and-thirty-third
  filing; `PASS 74.10`, `d8f3020`). TWO CLAUSES ADDED — (d) and (e) — AND THE
  CEILING DOES NOT MOVE. `R215` STANDS; NEXT FREE IS STILL `R216`.**

  **What forced the amendment.** `PASS 74.7` moved the **interpreter** to `f64`
  and left the **display-list recorder** in `f32`: a recorded op stores its CTM
  as an `f32` `Transform`, and `replay_region` post-translates by the region's
  device origin, **also in `f32`**. The two paths then agreed at ordinary scales
  and disagreed at deep zoom — **half a device pixel at recording scale
  `5 000`, `47 px` at `500 000`** — which is **this rule's condition, exactly**.
  `R211` was already in force, was already cited by `decision 081`, and
  **already names `replay_region` by name** as one of the two call sites whose
  *"these cannot disagree"* comment went false when a caller moved. It did not
  prevent this. **The two clauses below are why.**

  **(d) ★★ WHERE ONE PATH CANNOT MEET THE CONTRACT PAST SOME MAGNITUDE, BOTH
  PATHS CONSULT THE *SAME* PREDICATE TO DECIDE WHERE — AND THE PATH THAT CANNOT
  MATCH *REFUSES* RATHER THAN APPROXIMATING.** `R211`'s original three clauses
  all assume the contract **can** be met and ask *where to narrow*. Sometimes it
  cannot: a recorded display list has **no `f64` to keep** — the precision is
  gone at record time and no later care recovers it. The obligation in that case
  is **not** "pick a sensible limit". It is:

  - **One predicate, consulted by both paths.** `PASS 74.10`'s threshold is
    `Mat64::needs_precise_paths`, the **same** predicate the interpreter uses to
    decide it needs its `f64` route. **Below it, both paths do identical `f32`
    arithmetic and agree exactly. Above it, one switches to `f64` and the other
    refuses.** ⇒ **No magnitude exists at which they quietly disagree.**
  - **The losing path refuses by name and the caller falls back.**
    `PoisonReason::ScaleBeyondF32` → `RenderError::PageNotRecordable` → a direct
    render that is correct at any scale. The module's own doc block had already
    argued it: *"a display list that is subtly wrong is strictly worse than no
    display list. Refusing is loud, cheap, and correct."*

  **★ Why a shared predicate is strictly stronger than two limits that happen to
  agree, which is the transferable half.** Two independently-chosen constants
  can match today and drift apart in either direction on any later edit, and
  **the band between them is a magnitude range in which one path is precise, the
  other is not, and both believe they agree.** Nothing reports that band: it has
  no error, no counter, no failing test — it is defined by the *absence* of a
  disagreement anybody checks for. A shared predicate makes the band **unable to
  open**, because there is one number and one place it is decided. ⇒ **Two paths
  that must agree share the predicate that decides when they CAN, rather than
  each picking a limit.**

  **(e) ★★ THE DIFFERENTIAL TEST THAT GUARDS THIS CONTRACT SAMPLES ON BOTH SIDES
  OF THAT PREDICATE. A TEST PROVES AGREEMENT ONLY OVER THE RANGE IT SAMPLES, AND
  THE RANGE IS PART OF THE CLAIM.** `crates/pdfce-render/tests/region_matches_full_page.rs`
  is the oracle this rule was minted on the strength of. **It runs at scales up
  to `220`. The divergence begins near `530`.** Every assertion in it is
  correct, non-vacuous and independent — **it simply never asked at a magnitude
  where the answer changed.** So a *"these cannot disagree"* comment naming that
  test was **true about the test and false about the world**.

  **★ This is why clause (c) was not enough, and the distinction is the reason
  this is an amendment rather than a new number.** Clause (c) obliges the
  comment to **name the test that would go red**. Here the test was named, it
  existed, it ran, and it was **green** — naming a test says nothing about the
  **domain** the test samples. **A rule whose remedy can be satisfied while the
  defect ships is an incomplete rule.** (d) supplies the sampling point (the
  shared predicate) and (e) obliges the test to straddle it, which is the only
  form of "sample more" that is bounded rather than infinite.

  **★★ WHY THIS IS NOT `R215`, AND NOT `R216`, STATED SO THE RULING IS
  CHECKABLE.**
  - **Not `R215`.** `R215` binds the **target** (an acceptance table's expected
    values) and its mechanism is **attribution producing a WRONG expected
    value**; its failure mode is a **false alarm that would reject a correct
    fix**. Here every expected value is **right** and the failure mode is the
    **opposite** — a **silent pass over a broken system**, produced by the
    sampled domain. `R215`'s own scope paragraph disclaims tests: *"it does not
    bind on tests themselves."*
  - **Not a new number.** The **trigger condition is this rule's own opening
    sentence, verbatim** — *two code paths that owe each other byte-identical
    output* — and nothing new has to be defined to state it. Minting `R216`
    would **split one mechanism across two numbers**: a reader holding `R211`
    would discharge it by naming a test, and a reader holding `R216` would have
    no reason to consult `R211`'s asymmetric-narrowing analysis to learn **where
    to sample.** They are one obligation; the narrowing boundary is the thing to
    sample across.
  - **Not `R87`/`R162`/`R164`.** `R87` asks *was the instrument pointed at the
    thing?* — it was. `R162` asks *could the assertion ever come out false?* —
    it could, and did, once asked. `R164` asks *does this verdict depend on its
    neighbours?* — it does not. **All three were satisfied.**

  **★ The honest cost, recorded so this is a ruling and not an oversight.**
  Clause (e) **generalises past precision** — any parameterised differential
  test (page sizes, colour spaces, font sizes, **core counts**) proves agreement
  only over its sampled domain — and burying it inside a precision rule hides it
  from someone writing a non-precision differential test. **Mitigated the way
  this rule mitigated its own declined sibling**: the general form is filed as a
  fact in `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_differential_test_proves_agreement_only_over_the_range_it_samples.md`,
  where the test-methodology findings already live. **★★ `Pass 122.0` is where
  it bites next** — its acceptance criterion is *"byte-identical output at any
  core count"*, which is a differential contract over a parameter, and **"any"
  is the word this clause is about.**

  **Enforcement layer, per `R210`'s minting test.** (d) is **decidable from
  artefacts**: *do the two paths reference the same predicate, or two constants?*
  — a grep, no knowledge of intent. (e) is **weakly decidable**: *does the
  differential test sample a value on each side of that predicate?* — decidable
  once the predicate is named, which (d) guarantees. **Neither is wired as a
  gate and neither should be wired red**
  (`D:/dev/rag/rust/ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`); recorded as
  decidable so a future session knows the option exists.

  **Cross-references added by this amendment:** **decision 084** (§12 —

  parent), `R215` (the neighbour it is deliberately **not**), `R214` (the
  positional-reference species that turned up in the same sweep), `PASS 74.10`
  (`d8f3020`). New RAG files:
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/two_paths_that_must_agree_share_the_predicate_that_decides_when_they_can.md`
  and
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_differential_test_proves_agreement_only_over_the_range_it_samples.md`.

  **★ CEILING UNMOVED: `R215` STANDS, NEXT FREE `R216`.** An amendment that
  moved the ceiling would be a mint wearing an amendment's name.

- **R212 — A CONTRACT WRITTEN DOWN IN TWO PLACES, ONE OF WHICH IS UNDER TEST,
  DRIFTS IN THE OTHER — ALWAYS, AND IN ONE DIRECTION: THE TEST *FORCES* ITS
  COPY TO BE UPDATED AND NOTHING FORCES THE PUBLISHED ONE. NAME WHICH COPY IS
  AUTHORITATIVE, AND EITHER GENERATE THE OTHER FROM IT OR GATE THE TWO AGAINST
  EACH OTHER (2026-08-22; librarian-minted, two-hundred-and-twenty-ninth
  filing; `f9dc007`, discharging `Pass 74.4`'s two survivors).**

  **The mechanism, in three sentences.** When one copy of a contract lives in
  an assertion, changing the contract **turns a test red**, so that copy is
  updated as a condition of the change landing at all. When the other copy
  lives in a doc comment, a README or a published template, **nothing goes red**
  and it is updated only if somebody remembers. The two copies therefore do not
  drift apart at random — **they drift in exactly one direction, and it is
  always toward the copy that is enforced**, leaving the *published* copy — the
  one a consumer actually reads — as the stale one.

  **★ Why this is worse than ordinary duplication, and it is the load-bearing
  half.** The updated copy is **evidence of nothing.** A reviewer sees the test
  change in the diff and reads it as *"the change was propagated"*; it is
  actually *"the change was compelled."* **A well-argued change is not a
  self-propagating one** — and the better argued it is, the more convincing the
  test comment that carries the argument looks, and the less anyone thinks to
  ask where else the same sentence lives.

  **The worked instance, and the numbers are the warrant.** `pdfce-cli
  render-page`'s stable metrics line has **two** written contracts: the module
  doc block's `//! render-page:` template (published; the same block calls it
  *"the **fixed order shown**"*) and `crates/pdfce-cli/tests/render_page.rs`'s
  ordered `keys` assertion (enforced).

  - `Pass 74.4` inserted `forms_culled` **beside** `forms` rather than
    appending it. The reasoning — *"342 executed, 0 culled only reads as a pair
    when the two are adjacent"* — was written out **in the test comment**,
    correctly and at length. The doc block's *"existing keys … never move"*
    sentence, which that reasoning refutes, was not touched.
  - Sweeping for the same shape found it is not an incident but a **regime**:
    the `println!` emits **87** keys, the test asserts **87**, and the published
    template shows **59** (53 named plus six covered by its one `annots=…`
    elision). **28 of 87 — 32.2 % — are undocumented**, contiguous at the tail,
    `blend_modes_applied` → `cmyk_unbridged_images`.
  - The template's last extension is **`1e7a0be` (2026-08-17)**. The very next
    slice, **`bd244d9` the same day**, added keys to the `println!` and the test
    and not to the template. **16 commits have edited the test's key list
    since; none edited the template**
    (`git log --oneline 1e7a0be..HEAD -- crates/pdfce-cli/tests/render_page.rs`).
    **Sixteen opportunities, zero propagations, and no red anywhere.**

  **What the rule obliges, in three lines.**
  (a) **When you change a contract, the test edit does not count as
  propagation.** Ask separately, before the commit: *where is this contract
  PUBLISHED?* — doc comment, README, `--help` text, a template a script author
  reads.
  (b) **Name the authoritative copy IN the other copy.** `f9dc007` does this
  and it is the minimum: the docstring now says `tests/render_page.rs` is what
  enforces the order, so a reader who needs certainty has a route instead of a
  promise.
  (c) **Where the published copy is a literal template of what the code emits,
  GATE IT** — that is generation's cheap cousin and it is mechanical. Where it
  is prose, (a) and (b) are the whole of the remedy; do not pretend otherwise.

  **★★ ENFORCEMENT LAYER — the reason this was minted while the 228th filing
  declined its sibling one commit earlier, on the same day.** `R210`'s minting
  test is *"can the question be answered from artefacts alone?"* The **generic**
  question — *"does this doc block state a contract that some test file also
  states?"* — **cannot**, and the 228th filing was right to decline it. The
  **specific** question — *"does the `render-page` template list exactly the
  keys the `println!` emits?"* — is two regexes over two spans of **one file**,
  with no knowledge of pdfce's behaviour required. **The predicate was written
  and run before this rule was minted, and it found the 28-key tail that
  reading had missed.** ⇒ **A finding whose general form is undecidable can
  still have a decidable instance, and the instance is where the gate goes.**
  Do not let an undecidable generalisation talk you out of a two-regex check.

  **★ And the sequencing constraint, which is part of the rule rather than an
  aside.** The gate is **RED at baseline** — 28 keys missing at `HEAD`. Wiring
  it before the repair would make it a permanent warning, which is
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`, this project's
  own finding. **Repair first, wire second.** A rule that prescribes a gate
  owes the order in which it becomes real.

  **★ Scope, so it is not over-read.** This binds where a contract has **two
  written copies and one is asserted by a test** — stable output lines, wire
  formats, `--help` text against `clap` definitions, a schema doc against a
  serde struct. It does **not** bind on ordinary duplicated prose, which is
  hard rule 11's territory (sweep on a *meaning change*), nor on an instrument
  under-reporting itself, which is `R210`'s. **`R212` fires on an ordinary
  ADDITION** — nothing changed meaning, no instrument said anything, and that
  is exactly why the other two do not reach it.

  Cross-references: `R210` (the minting test this rule satisfies, and the
  decline it is the counterpart to), `R211` (minted on the same test five
  commits earlier), hard rule 11 in `.claude/agents/pdfce-librarian.md` (the

  `docs/decisions/004` §6.4 / `R20` (why the metrics line exists at all). New

  `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_contract_with_a_tested_copy_and_a_published_copy_drifts_in_the_published_one.md`.
  Related and deliberately not merged with:
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/the_cheapest_moment_to_delete_a_duplicated_formula_is_while_it_still_agrees.md`
  (that one is about two copies of an *implementation*; this is about two copies
  of a *contract*, where deletion is not available because one copy's job is to
  be readable by someone who will never run the test).

  **★ SECOND INSTANCE OF THE ENFORCEMENT-LAYER CLAUSE, added 2026-08-22 (230th

  **★★★ NAMED CANDIDATE, RECORDED 2026-08-26 (270th filing) — NOT MINTED, NOT
  AN AMENDMENT, AND THE CEILING DOES NOT MOVE. `R212` STANDS UNCHANGED; NEXT
  FREE IS STILL `R219`.** Recorded against `R212` rather than at a fresh number
  because it is a defect in `R212`'s own prescribed remedy — *"gate the two
  against each other"* — not a new pattern. n = 1; below this project's
  two-occurrence bar. **The mint is the operator's act.**

  **The candidate, in one line:** ⇢ ***A GATE BETWEEN TWO COPIES OF A CONTRACT
  MUST COMPARE THE TWO COPIES. A GATE THAT COMPARES EACH COPY TO A TOLERANCE
  BAND INSTEAD PASSES WHEN BOTH ARE WRONG, AND A BAND CHOSEN TO SURVIVE
  ROUNDING WILL ALSO SURVIVE BEING WRONG.***

  **The instance, and it is `Pass 132.0`'s own headline test.**
  `the_settings_file_describes_the_ceiling_the_renderer_actually_enforces` was
  written — correctly, and as a genuine `R212` discharge — because
  `pdfce-core` writes an operator-facing settings file quoting a number that
  lives in `pdfce-render`, a crate it cannot see. The test lives at the one
  boundary that can see both. **Its two halves then check different things and
  never meet:**

  | half | what it does | what it would catch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `assert!(text.contains("about 530% zoom"))` | pins the **prose** to a string literal | the sentence being **deleted or reworded** |
  | `(500.0..560.0).contains(&zoom_percent)` | pins a **recomputed** figure to a band | the **constant moving** far enough |

  **Neither half compares the prose to the recomputation.** The recomputation
  yields **517.6 %**; the prose says **530 %** in the file it guards and
  **534 %** in the four `crates/` sites beside it. **A ±30-point band holds all
  three at once**, so the test is green while the two copies disagree — the
  exact condition `R212` exists to make impossible.

  ⇢ **The prescribed form:** derive the published string **from** the
  authoritative number and assert equality on the formatted result, or assert
  the parsed number **out of the prose** against the recomputation. A band is
  appropriate for a *measurement*; a number two documents both claim to state
  is not a measurement, and giving it a tolerance converts an equality check
  into a plausibility check.

  ★ **Occurrence warrant, stated honestly downward.** n = 1, and the instance
  was found by the same filing that filed the test — a sweep looking for stale
  claims found a weak assertion, which is not independent evidence that the
  shape recurs. **A second instance found by a different filing should mint
  this as an `R212` clause, not at a fresh number.** Full context and the nine
  affected sites: the `Pass 132.0` entry's hard-rule-11 sweep, above.


- **R213 — A MAGNITUDE CLAIM IS A CLAIM ABOUT *ONE* QUANTITY. NAME THE QUANTITY
  IN THE CLAIM ITSELF — IN THE LABEL, NOT IN THE PROSE BESIDE IT — BECAUSE WHEN
  IT IS MISSING THE READER SUPPLIES THE BROADEST ONE AVAILABLE AND **NOTHING
  DISAGREES** (2026-08-22; librarian-minted, two-hundred-and-thirtieth filing;
  `950e3af`/`65e1910`, `PASS 74.6`/`74.6b`; **n=2**, second instance, first
  already on disk as hard rule 10's founding case).**

  **The mechanism, in four sentences.** A ceiling, a throughput, a precision or
  a limit is measured **on something** — a viewport, a clip, a page, a buffer.
  The measurement is correct and the sentence reporting it is true. **What
  travels is the number, and the subject is the half that gets dropped**, because
  a subject is a qualifier and qualifiers are what a summary removes first. The
  reader then supplies the **broadest** subject the context allows — *"the
  system holds to X"* — and **no record anywhere contradicts them**, because
  nothing was ever wrong.

  **★ Why that last clause makes this a rule rather than a caution, and it is
  the load-bearing half.** Every other failure this project has numbered leaves
  a **disagreement** behind: a stale claim contradicts current behaviour
  (hard rule 11), a mis-scored figure contradicts an oracle (`R210`), two copies
  of a contract contradict each other (`R212`), a total contradicts its
  per-item form (hard rule 10). **This one leaves NOTHING to find.** Review
  answers *"is this true?"* — and the answer is **yes**. The defect is only
  visible when an artefact needs **both** quantities at once, and there is no
  reason for such an artefact to exist. Both known instances were found that
  way, by accident, at a cost.

  **The two instances.**

  1. **2026-08-07 — `mask.fill_path`.** Filed as **`5.24 s`** in one RAG file
     and **`8.3 µs`** in another. The quantities: **5.24 s over 24 128 clips =
     217 µs each** and **8.3 µs page-sized**. Both measured correctly. Read as
     one figure for *"the cost of `fill_path`"* — **a 26× contradiction carried
     openly for two filings, the two figures 217 lines apart in the same
     `index.md`.** By the time it was corrected the wrong number had been a
     work-order ranking key for six hours and had **dispatched a fork on a false
     premise**. The correction required no new measurement, only division.
     (Hard rule 10's founding case; full derivation in
     `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_record_can_carry_its_own_refutation_because_review_checks_claims_against_the_world.md`.)
  2. **2026-08-22 — *"deep zoom holds to a trillion percent"*** (`PASS 74.1`/
     `74.2`, `bd9844d`/`71f7055`, 226th filing). **True, and it is about the
     RETURNED VIEWPORT**: a requested 800 × 600 pixmap comes back 800 × 600 out
     to `1 × 10¹² %`. **Three `f32` limits sit under the page-space CONTENT** —
     a path coordinate near `x = 540` has a spacing of `6.1 × 10⁻⁵ pt` =
     **21.5 µm**; a `cm` carrying a page coordinate drifts by
     ≈ `page_x × scale / 16 700 000` px; and the content's device position is
     therefore **quantised in ~500 px steps at `scale = 8.1 × 10⁶`**. Carried
     across **four documents and three Pass entries** for a day. Surfaced only
     when a 50 nm artefact needed the viewport *and* the geometry at once — and
     **confirmed by accident**, when two successive `--region` nudges produced
     **byte-identical framing** because the `f64` viewport moved and the `f32`
     content could not.

  **★ Why these are one mechanism and not two coincidences.** Hard rule 10's
  remedy — *file a total beside its per-item form* — **catches instance 1 and
  cannot catch instance 2**, because a viewport size and a coordinate precision
  are not two forms of one number; they are two numbers about two things. What
  the instances share is only this: **the SUBJECT of a bound went unstated and
  the reader supplied it.** `R213` is the general form; hard rule 10 (a) is the
  special case where the two subjects happen to be convertible.

  **What the rule obliges, in three lines.**
  (a) **Put the subject in the LABEL**, not only in the prose beside it — hard
  rule 10 (b) restated for bounds, and for the same reason: *the label is what
  gets quoted*. `"Numerical reach"` is a heading this project actually shipped
  over a correct paragraph; `"Numerical reach of the returned VIEWPORT"` is the
  whole fix.
  (b) **When you file a ceiling, ask what the NEIGHBOURING quantity's ceiling
  is** — and if you have not measured it, **say that you have not.** *"The
  viewport holds to `1 × 10¹² %`; the page-space geometry ceiling is
  unmeasured"* would have cost one clause and saved a day.
  (c) **A claim inherits no qualifier when it propagates.** The original
  statements of this claim were all correct (`ROADMAP.md:950`, `:1094`,
  `SESSION_LOG.md` — every one says *"holds its **viewport**"*). **It was the
  derived, forward-looking documents that dropped the subject.** So the sweep
  target is not the entry that made the claim; it is everything that repeated
  it.

  **★ Enforcement — there is none, and that is deliberate.** No gate can know
  what a sentence is about. This is the same posture hard rule 10 takes in
  `.claude/agents/pdfce-librarian.md` (*"no checker exists and none is coming —
  this is deliberate, so do not propose one"*), and the same posture `R210` was
  minted with. **`R211` and `R212` are the gateable species and this is not
  one** — do not read the absence of a gate as a weaker rule; read it as a rule
  about the record rather than about the tree.

  **★ Scope, so it is not over-read.** This binds on **bounds and magnitudes**:
  ceilings, floors, throughputs, precisions, capacities, limits. It does **not**
  bind on ordinary measurements that carry their unit and denominator — those
  are hard rule 10's. It does **not** bind on a figure whose instrument is
  under-reporting — that is `R210`'s. **`R213` fires when every number is right
  and every sentence is true**, which is exactly why the other two do not reach
  it.

  Cross-references: hard rule 10 (a)/(b) in `.claude/agents/pdfce-librarian.md`
  (the special case and the label convention this generalises), `R210` (the
  sibling on instruments rather than claims), `R211` (the precision contract
  `PASS 74.7` will have to honour), decision **081** (the single `f64` entry
  point for region geometry — the fix that made the viewport half correct and
  left the content half untouched), `PASS 74.7` under *Backlog* (the content
  half). New RAG file:
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_ceiling_is_a_claim_about_one_quantity.md`. PDF-domain half,
  for any renderer rather than for pdfce:
  `C:/personal_rag/pdf/lesson_20260822_f32_limits_under_pdf_content_rendering.md`.

  **Ceiling moves `R212` → `R213`; next free `R214`.** *(Superseded 2026-08-22

- **R214 — A DOC COMMENT THAT POINTS AT ITS REFERENT BY *POSITION* — *"of
  those"*, *"the above"*, *"this slice"*, *"the next slice"*, *"the former"* —
  IS A DANGLING POINTER. IT BREAKS WHEN SOMETHING **ELSE** MOVES, IT CONTAINS NO
  STALE TOKEN, AND BECAUSE IT NAMES NOTHING IT GIVES **NO WAY TO TELL A *BROKEN*
  REFERENCE FROM A *WRONG* ONE**. NAME THE REFERENT; AND WHEN REPAIRING ONE,
  REPAIR AT THE **REFERENT**, NEVER AT THE NEIGHBOUR (2026-08-22;
  librarian-minted, two-hundred-and-thirty-first filing; `eca07ee`,
  `PASS 74.8`; **n=1 for the doubly-wrong form, n=4 in one commit for the
  mechanism**).**

  **The mechanism, in four sentences.** A doc comment that says *"Of those, N
  were …"* resolves its subject from **whatever is declared before it**, and a
  doc comment that says *"in this slice"* resolves it from **when it was
  written**. Neither subject is written down. **Something else moving — a new
  field declared in between, a slice shipping — invalidates the sentence without
  editing a single character of it**, so there is no stale word, no stale number
  and no stale identifier for a grep or a gate to find. And the second-order
  failure is the expensive one: **when the reference is discovered to be broken,
  the obvious repair is to re-point it at the current neighbour** — which is a
  claim about behaviour made without checking behaviour.

  **The worked instance, and both halves cost a code read to establish.**
  `pdfce-render`'s `Diagnostics::transparency_groups_special` opened
  **"Of those"**.

  - **It was BROKEN**: `soft_masks_on_group_result` had since been declared
    between it and its intended antecedent, so *"those"* pointed at the wrong
    field. (Reported by the 230th filing, found by **reading the struct in
    declaration order** — hard rule 11's discipline, not a search.)
  - **It was ALSO WRONG**: the increment site is
    `is_transparency_group && (knockout || isolated)` — **no flattening
    condition at all** — so the counter was **never** a subset of the flattened
    count it was originally written against.
  - **The first repair restored the "obvious" antecedent and had to be corrected
    by reading the increment site.** Had it stood, a *wrong* reference would have
    become a *plausible* one, and the next reader would have had less reason to
    check it than the one before.

  ⇒ **Repairing the reference without checking the referent silently converts a
  WRONG reference into a BROKEN-THEN-PLAUSIBLY-REPAIRED one.** The defect
  survives and its evidence is destroyed.

  **What the rule obliges, in three lines.**
  (a) **Name the referent.** *"Of the `transparency_groups_composited` count"*,
  not *"Of those"*. One identifier, and the sentence becomes greppable, movable
  and checkable.
  (b) **Never resolve a reference against NOW.** *"in this slice"*, *"the next
  slice"*, *"once X lands"* are pointers at a moving target; write the Pass ID
  and the condition, or write nothing. A document outlives the *now* it was
  written in — this is the prose form of `R193`/`Pass 74.0` (*a limit justified
  by "beyond any plausible use" is a prediction, not a fact*).
  (c) **When you repair a positional reference, go to the REFERENT — the
  increment site, the producing branch, the code — not to the neighbour.** The
  repair is a **new claim** and earns hard rule 10's corollary (*a correction is
  a claim; name its world-source*) and hard rule 11's corollary (*check a draft
  claim of your own against live source*). **With a positional reference you
  cannot even tell which kind of correction you are making**, so this check is
  not diligence — it is the only thing separating a repair from a fresh defect.

  **★★★★ CLAUSE (d), ADDED 2026-08-23 (236th filing, `39b449f`) — A STRUCTURAL
  REPAIR EMITS A NEW CLAIM OF A DIFFERENT KIND: A *SCOPE STATEMENT*, WHICH IS A
  UNIVERSAL QUANTIFIER OVER THE DELIMITED CONTENTS. VERIFY IT AGAINST THEM.**

  *(The head of this rule said "in three lines" and listed (a)–(c). It now lists
  four. The original phrasing is left above, per the append-only convention, as
  the record of what the rule was when it was minted.)*

  **Trigger.** You applied clause (a)'s remedy structurally — promoted a
  positional boundary to a **section heading**, split a section, or otherwise
  replaced a pointer with a delimiter. **Before shipping it, read the scope
  sentence you just wrote against every passage inside the thing it delimits.**

  **The mechanism, and it is the whole clause.** Promoting a boundary to a
  heading removes **positional drift** — the delimiter and the content are the
  same object and cannot get out of step — and that is real, and it is what
  clause (a) buys. **It buys nothing against OVER-SCOPING.** The heading fixes
  **where the claim's edge is**; the sentence beneath it still asserts **what is
  inside**; and *those two are independent*. ⇒ **a heading-bound claim is still a
  claim about a SET, and it can be wrong about its own contents.**

  **Worked instance — the remedy manufactured the defect TWICE in one commit,
  which is why this is a clause of `R214` and not a separate rule.** `641deb9`
  split `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md` §9 (history) from §10 (current), per
  clause (a). Each new section opened with a scope sentence. **Both were false:**

  | section | the scope sentence it emitted | falsified by |
  |---|---|---|
  | **§9** | *"Everything in this section describes pdfce BEFORE `Pass 74.7`"* | its own table's **`after` and `correct`** columns — post-fix measurements. **Repaired by `39b449f`** |
  | **§10** | *"Everything in this section describes pdfce as it stands"* | a **before**-figure (*"76 px out horizontally and 288 px vertically"*), a preserved prior wording (*"said … until 2026-08-23"*), the `93 s` **rejected**-attempt provenance, and a paragraph whose subject is a roadmap table's history. **Repaired by `a68498b`** |
  | **★ `NEXT_SESSION.md`** *(added 2026-08-23, 237th filing)* | *"Everything below this line is unchanged from the previous handoff"* | **two hunks below that line in the very commit that wrote it** — §6 gained items 16–17 and §7's four figures were rewritten (`21 → 26`, `214 → 219`). ★★ **Written by the filing that minted this clause**, in this role's own tree, and found only by a sweep aimed at somebody else's document. ⇒ the clause binds on `docs/` exactly as it binds on `tools/` |

  ⇒ **`n=2`, both produced by the same remedy, in the same commit, in adjacent
  sections.** The engineer's dispatch recommended a **decline at `n=1`** on the
  ground that the general form (*"fixing the form of a claim does not check its
  content"*) is close to platitude. **That ground is accepted and the general
  form is NOT what is filed** — what is filed is the narrow, checkable version:
  *when you convert prose into structure, re-read the structure's own boundary
  statements as claims, because they are new assertions nobody has checked.*

  **Why a clause of `R214` rather than `R216`.** The defect is a **rider on this
  rule's own prescribed remedy**. Filing the warning under a separate number
  detaches it from the remedy that causes it, so the next reader applies clause
  (a) and repeats the defect — which is exactly what happened. Clause (c) already
  establishes that **a repair is a new claim**; what it did not say is *what kind*
  of claim a **structural** repair makes, and its remedy vocabulary (*name the
  referent*) gives no instruction for a **quantifier**. Clause (d) supplies the
  missing half.

  **Decidability — this clause meets the enforcement-layer test below, on the
  stronger side of it.** *"Is this scope sentence true of this section's
  contents?"* is answerable **from one span of one file with no knowledge of
  pdfce's behaviour**: you need only see an `after` column, or the words *"before
  the fix"*, or a quoted prior wording. That is **more** decidable than clause
  (c)'s *"is this reference right?"*, which requires reading the increment site.
  **It is not, however, greppable** — the scope sentence contains no stale token —
  so it belongs in the reading, alongside hard rule 11, and **no gate is proposed
  for it.**

  **★ Scope, so it is not over-read.** This binds on **a scope statement written
  to delimit a section's contents** — the artefact a structural split produces.
  **Ordinary section headings assert nothing about their contents and are
  untouched**, and neither is a heading whose section carries no such sentence.

  **★★ ENFORCEMENT LAYER — the split is decidable on one half and undecidable on
  the other, and the decidable half is where the gate goes.** *"Is this reference
  RIGHT?"* requires reading the increment site — that is knowledge of current
  behaviour, and `R210`'s minting test refuses it. *"Is this reference NAMED?"*
  is **a grep over a closed vocabulary** in doc comments — *of those*, *the
  above*, *the below*, *the former*, *the latter*, *this slice*, *the next
  slice*, *as above*, *see below*, *the previous field*, *the field above* —
  answerable from **one span of one file with no knowledge of pdfce's
  behaviour**. That is `R212`'s enforcement-layer clause applied verbatim: *a
  finding whose general form is undecidable can still have a decidable instance,
  and the instance is where the gate goes.*

  **★ The gate is RECOMMENDED, NOT BUILT, and the sequencing is part of the
  rule.** `tools/` is outside the librarian's remit, and **the baseline is

  make it a permanent warning, which is
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`, this project's
  own finding. A rule that prescribes a gate owes the order in which it becomes
  real.

  **★ Scope, so it is not over-read.** This binds on **references inside prose
  that a reader must resolve** — doc comments, module headers, `--help` text,
  RAG entries, roadmap prose. It does **not** bind on ordinary duplicated prose
  (hard rule 11), on two written copies of one contract (`R212`), or on a
  magnitude with an unstated subject (`R213`). **The distinction from `R213` is
  the one a future session will try to collapse, so it is stated here:** both are

  in the label*, which says nothing about repair; `R214` binds **references** and
  **governs the fix**, which is where its instance did its damage. `R213`
  prevents; `R214` prevents **and** repairs. Recorded as neighbours, deliberately

  **★ Why this was minted rather than folded into `R212`, since that was the
  dispatch's own question.** `R212` requires **two written copies of one

- **R215 — AN ACCEPTANCE ORACLE WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX, FROM THE BROKEN
  SYSTEM'S OWN OUTPUT, ATTRIBUTES THE WHOLE OBSERVABLE TO THE DEFECT IT IS
  HUNTING. WHERE A SECOND, *CORRECT* MECHANISM MOVES THE SAME NUMBER, THE
  ORACLE DEMANDS THE WRONG ANSWER AND WOULD HAVE FAILED THE CORRECT FIX. STATE
  THE EXPECTED VALUE **AND THE MECHANISM THAT PRODUCES IT**, PER ROW; WHERE TWO
  MECHANISMS MOVE ONE NUMBER, DECOMPOSE THEM OR SAY YOU CANNOT** (2026-08-23;
  librarian-minted, two-hundred-and-thirty-second filing; `1d6db9e`,
  `PASS 74.7`; **n=1, and the instance is this role's OWN filed artefact**).**

  **The mechanism, in four sentences.** A defect is characterised by measuring
  the broken system across a parameter — here, forms rendered against rising
  zoom: **`11 → 7 → 3 → 1`**. The healthy end of that curve is then written into
  an acceptance table as the requirement for **every** row: *"required after the
  fix: `11 of 11`"*. **That step is an attribution, not an observation** — it
  says *all* of the decline is the defect. **If any second mechanism also moves
  the number, and that mechanism is CORRECT, the oracle now demands a bug.**

  **The worked instance, and it is this file's own text.** The 230th filing
  opened `Pass 74.7` in *Backlog* with a table headed ***"★★ ACCEPTANCE BASELINE
  — ALREADY MEASURED, WHICH IS RARE ENOUGH TO NAME"***, prose reading *"this Pass
  has a pass/fail oracle **before a line is written**"*, and this column,
  preserved verbatim because deleting a rule's evidence while minting the rule
  is the destruction `R214` clause (c) warns about:

  | `scale` | forms rendered today | required after `74.7` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `2 × 10⁶` | **11 of 11** | 11 of 11 |
  | `5 × 10⁶` | **11 of 11** | 11 of 11 |
  | `1.25 × 10⁷` | **7 of 11** | **11 of 11** |
  | `2.5 × 10⁷` | **3 of 11** | **11 of 11** |
  | `5 × 10⁷` | **1 of 11** (the box alone) | **11 of 11** |

  **The correct post-fix answer is `2` from `1.25 × 10⁷` up** — the box plus the
  one molecule actually in frame. **Two mechanisms were reducing that count:**

  - the **precision** defect, losing forms to a translation quantised in `f32`
    — the thing being hunted; and
  - **`Pass 74.4`'s `/BBox` viewport cull**, losing forms because they genuinely
    left the viewport as the zoom rose — **exact, correct, ISO 32000-1 §8.10.1,
    and shipped by this same project five commits earlier.**

  **A fix that satisfied the filed oracle would have been a BUG** — it would
  have meant nine forms outside the viewport were being painted.

  **★★ WHAT MADE IT AUTHORITATIVE IS THE PART TO CARRY FORWARD.** The table was
  introduced as **unusually rigorous** — *measured in advance*, *rare enough to
  name*. **That praise is what made it hard to question.** Every number in it was
  a correct observation; **the CLAIM was in the column heading**, which is hard
  rule 10 (b) again (*the label is what gets quoted*) at a different target. An
  oracle presented as measured invites matching rather than reasoning, and the
  next reader has **less** reason to check it, not more.

  **What the rule obliges, in three lines.**
  (a) **Every row of an acceptance table states its expected value AND the
  mechanism that produces it.** *"`2 of 11` — the box plus the one form in
  frame; the other nine are outside the viewport and §8.10.1 culls them"*, not
  *"`11 of 11`"*. **A row that cannot say *why* its number is a transcription of
  an observation, not a prediction.**
  (b) **Before writing a "required after" column, enumerate every mechanism that
  moves the measured quantity** — especially the project's **own recent, correct
  ones**. The dangerous second mechanism is not an unknown; here it was five
  commits old and had its own Shipped entry.
  (c) **Where the mechanisms cannot be decomposed, say so and give the oracle a
  weaker form** — a direction, a bound, a "must be ≥ today's" — rather than a
  precise number derived by extrapolation. **A weak oracle that is right beats a
  precise one that is wrong**, because only the second can fail a correct fix.

  **★ Scope, so it is not over-read.** This binds on **acceptance criteria,
  pass/fail oracles and "required after" columns** — the target a test is written
  against, which is written **before** the test and often **by a different
  person**. It does **not** bind on tests themselves; that whole family already
  has its rules and they cover different failures:
  **`R87`** asks *was the instrument pointed at the thing?*, **`R162`** asks
  *could my assertion ever have come out false?*, **`R164`** asks *does this
  verdict depend on its neighbours?*. **All three interrogate the TEST. `R215`
  interrogates the TARGET** — and a test can be perfectly aimed, non-vacuous and
  independent while measuring against a number that is simply wrong.

  **★ Why no gate, stated so the absence is a ruling rather than an omission.**
  *"Does this acceptance row attribute its number to exactly one mechanism when
  several could produce it?"* requires knowing **which mechanisms exist and what
  each does** — knowledge of current behaviour, which is `R210`'s minting test
  answered in the negative, the same answer decision 082's cull-placement
  candidate got. **The decidable sub-question is weaker but real and is
  RECOMMENDED, not built:** *does every row of a "required after" column carry a
  clause explaining its number?* — a property of one table in one file. Measure
  the baseline before wiring anything
  (`D:/dev/rag/rust/ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`).

  **Occurrence warrant, stated rather than inflated: n=1.** The mint does not
  rest on the count. It rests on (i) **the demonstrated failure mode** — the
  oracle would have rejected the correct fix, which is the strongest kind of
  evidence an oracle can produce about itself; (ii) **novelty** — nothing in
  `R87`/`R162`/`R164` or `R210`–`R214` reaches the target as distinct from the
  test; and (iii) **provenance** — the founding defect is **this role's own
  filed artefact**, which is the warrant hardest to dismiss as defensive.
  **Recorded honestly: no harm resulted**, because the engineer measured the
  delivered behaviour and reasoned about what `2` meant rather than matching the
  table. **That is care, not machinery.** The rule exists because the next
  session may match the table.

  **★ The mint DECLINED alongside it, recorded here because the pair is the
  ruling.** The dispatch proposed *"a regression test is not a regression test
  until you have watched it fail"*, on four instances (each caught by a
  deliberate sabotage run, all four tabulated in the Shipped entry). **Declined
  on coverage, not on count**: `R87`, `R162` and `R164` already carry all four
  instances **as conditions**, and
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/prove_test_suite_non_vacuous_by_deliberately_breaking_the_thing_it_tests.md`
  (2026-08-12) states the prescription verbatim. **The decisive ground is
  shape**: every rule in this section names a **condition**; *"watch it fail"*
  names an **action**, and an action with no condition attached reads as
  *sabotage everything* — work rather than care, the ground three mints were
  declined on this week — and **would weaken the three rules that do name the
  conditions**, because a reader holding a blanket rule stops asking which one
  applies. The genuinely new content in that batch is an **arithmetic fact**
  (*two EQUAL large `f32` values cancel perfectly, so a round-numbers fixture
  makes a float-precision test vacuous; the defect needs operands large and
  merely NEARLY equal*) and it is filed as a fact, in
  `D:/dev/rag/rust/a_float_precision_test_with_round_number_operands_cannot_fail_because_equal_values_cancel_exactly.md`,
  rather than buried inside a methodology prescription.

  Cross-references: `R87`, `R162`, `R164` (the test-side family this is
  deliberately **not** part of), `R210` (the minting test, answered in the

  **★★★ AMENDED 2026-08-23 (two-hundred-and-thirty-fourth filing, `4af0c08`) —

  **(d) WHEN A FILED NUMBER IS FOUND WRONG, PUBLISH THE *CORRECTION*, NOT THE
  CORRECTED VALUE — AND KEEP THE WRONG VALUE VISIBLE.** Write *"this said **X**;
  **X** is impossible because **Y**; it is **Z**"*. A bare `Z` is **re-derived
  back to `X`** by the next person reasoning from the same faulty intuition —
  **including yourself an hour later** — because the intuition that produced `X`
  still sounds correct and nothing beside `Z` disputes it.

  **The mechanism this clause was added for, in four sentences, and it is a
  DIFFERENT one from (a)–(c).** (a)–(c) govern how an expected value is
  **derived**, and their failure is a **false alarm on a correct fix**. This
  governs where a number **lands afterwards**: identified as wrong in an
  **expectation**, recorded correctly in the documents that file the fix, and
  then — **hours later, in a third document** — restated as a measured
  **result**. ***An expectation invites checking; a result does not.*** The
  genre change removes the only mechanism that would have caught it, and **it
  happens naturally rather than carelessly**: writing up a fix, you reach for
  the criterion you were working against and report it as met.

  `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md` §9 as prose reading *"The table above is
  superseded: 11 of 11 forms survive at every scale tested"*** — an outcome, in
  the one tree the mint's sweep did not cover — **and the table's own header,
  *"forms rendered of 11"*, made `11` the target at every row**, which is hard
  rule 10 (b) at the same target again. Repaired by `4af0c08`, which obeys
  clause (d) in its own text: it quotes the sentence it replaces, dates it, and
  says why `11` was never achievable.

  **★ Why the clause is a FORM and not a diligence request.** The two neighbours
  that come closest both bind a correction's **sourcing** and neither binds its
  **shape**: hard rule 10's corollary (*a correction is a claim; name its
  world-source*) and `R214` clause (c) (*repair at the referent, not at the

  **★ Scope, so it is not over-read, and the cost of amending rather than

  **The candidate, in one line:** ⇢ ***AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WRITTEN AGAINST A

  **Both instances, cited. Same filing, same day, independently written months

  | # | criterion as filed | why it is now unsatisfiable | where |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `Pass 97.1k` — *"`cmyk_bridged_pixels` reaches **0**"* | it would demand that an `ICCBased`-RGB image **stop bridging**, and there is **no ink in it to keep**. `PCS3_172` bridges after `Pass 130.1` and that is **correct** | `ROADMAP.md`, `Pass 97.1k` entry, quoted in place per clause (d) |

  **The shared cause, which is the content of the candidate.** Both criteria
  were written **against a counter** — a number pdfce emits — instead of
  **against the clause** the counter reports on. A counter's scope is chosen for
  what it is useful to **census**; a criterion's scope is fixed by what the
  **standard** requires. **The two are not the same set, and nothing forces them
  to converge.** When the classification is later understood, the counter is
  correct and the criterion is impossible — **and meeting the criterion would be
  the regression.**

  `overprint_images_unsupported` **unchanged** on the patches whose image sources
  are process spaces"* — the clause first, the counter named as the instrument.
  Compare the shape it replaces: *"the counter reaches 0"*, which asserts a
  property of the **instrument** and says nothing about the **picture**.

  to state **the mechanism that produces its number**. This candidate says
  **where the wrong number comes from in the first place** — the author reached
  for a quantity the system already prints, because a printed quantity feels
  measured. It is the **provenance** clause `R215` does not have. Folding it in
